header: Assembly — step 5, slice 1: RH meets the zero sum. The explicit formula's zero side is `Σ_{|γ|<T} m(ρ)·x^ρ/ρ`. This module defines that sum (`zeroPartialSum`), states the hEF leaf (`StmtExplicitFormula` — the truncated explicit formula with explicit remainder, the one genuinely open piece), and proves what RH does to the zero side, kernel-checked:

decls.name: re_eq_half_of_RH
decls.why: Under RH every nontrivial zero sits on the critical line. The strip membership rules out the trivial zeros and `s = 1`, so Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` applies directly.

decls.name: half_le_norm_of_RH
decls.why: Under RH, `|ρ| ≥ 1/2`.

decls.name: norm_cpow_of_RH
decls.why: The RH collapse: `‖x^ρ‖ = √x` for `x > 0`.

decls.name: norm_term_le_of_RH
decls.why: Each zero term is at most `2√x` in norm, from `|ρ| ≥ 1/2`.

decls.name: zeroPartialSum
decls.why: The order-weighted partial zero sum below height `T`: `Σ_{|γ|<T} m(ρ)·x^ρ/ρ`.

decls.name: StmtExplicitFormula
decls.why: The hEF leaf — the truncated explicit formula with explicit remainder. The one genuinely open analytic input of stage 3 (entry 119): every proof assistant lacks it; IEANTN targets it. Stated over Mathlib's Chebyshev `ψ` and the order-weighted partial sum.

decls.name: StmtExplicitFormulaPoly
decls.why: The `T ≤ x²`-regime form — the shape the contour proof delivers (`Glue.explicit_formula_poly`) and all the assembly consumes (`T = 2^(K+1) ≤ 2x ≤ x²`). Approved leaf-shape change (entry 271).

decls.name: norm_zeroPartialSum_le
decls.why: The zero side controlled by the count, under RH: `‖zeroPartialSum x 2^(K+1)‖ ≤ 2√x·(2|N(2^(K+1))| + W)`, through IEANTN's sorry-free `weighted_cumulative_count_le`. With ZeroSum's `N_abs_le` this is `√x`·(T·log T)-arithmetic under hNT.
decls.proves: ‖zeroPartialSum x ((2 : ℝ) ^ (K + 1))‖ ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt x * (2 * |riemannZeta.N ((2 : ℝ) ^ (K + 1))| + weightedZeroHeightBucket)

decls.name: inv_le_dyadic_sum
decls.why: Scalar dyadic domination: for `1 ≤ γ < 2^(K+1)`, `γ⁻¹ ≤ Σ_{j≤K} (2^j)⁻¹·[γ < 2^(j+1)]` — the largest surviving indicator sits at the shell containing `γ`, and its weight already dominates.
decls.proves: ∀ γ : ℝ, 1 ≤ γ → γ < 2 ^ (K + 1) → γ⁻¹ ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (K + 1), ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)⁻¹ * (if γ < 2 ^ (j + 1) then 1 else 0)

decls.name: norm_term_le_dyadic
decls.why: Each zero term is dominated by the dyadic indicator weights: `‖x^ρ/ρ‖ ≤ 2√x·Σ_{j≤K} (2^j)⁻¹·[|γ| < 2^(j+1)]` for `|γ| < 2^(K+1)`.
decls.proves: ‖(x : ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ) / (ρ : ℂ)‖ ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt x * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (K + 1), ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)⁻¹ * (if |(ρ : ℂ).im| < 2 ^ (j + 1) then 1 else 0)

decls.name: norm_zeroPartialSum_le_sharp
decls.why: The sharp zero-side bound, dyadic form. Under RH, the zero side is controlled level by level: each level's weighted count enters through IEANTN's sorry-free `weighted_cumulative_count_le`, reached by the scalar domination — no shell partition anywhere.
decls.proves: ‖zeroPartialSum x ((2 : ℝ) ^ (K + 1))‖ ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt x * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (K + 1), ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)⁻¹ * (2 * |riemannZeta.N ((2 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1))| + weightedZeroHeightBucket)

decls.name: norm_zeroPartialSum_le_logsq
decls.why: The zero side at `√x·(log T)²`, under RH + hNT — the sharp form. Combining the dyadic bound with ZeroSum's counting arithmetic: with `T = 2^(K+1)`, the zero side is at most `2√x·(2·[(log 2/2π)(K+1)(K+2) + 3(K+1)/π + 2(RvM(T) + 7/8)] + 2W)`.
decls.proves: ‖zeroPartialSum x ((2 : ℝ) ^ (K + 1))‖ ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt x * (2 * (Real.log 2 / (2 * Real.pi) * (K + 1) * (K + 2) + 3 * (K + 1) / Real.pi + 2 * (riemannZeta.RvM b₁ b₂ b₃ ((2 : ℝ) ^ (K + 1)) + 7 / 8)) + 2 * weightedZeroHeightBucket)

decls.name: rem_arith
decls.why: Scalar arithmetic of the remainder: `x ≤ T`, `0 ≤ G ≤ 3L`, `1 ≤ L` give `c₁·x·G²/T + c₂·L ≤ (9c₁+c₂)·L²`.
decls.proves: c₁ * xx * G ^ 2 / TT + c₂ * L ≤ (9 * c₁ + c₂) * L ^ 2

decls.name: zeroinner_arith
decls.why: Scalar arithmetic of the zero side's inner factor: the dyadic level bounds and the RvM bound turn the `(K, RvM)` expression into `2·(7+4b₁+4b₂+2b₃)·L² + 2W`.
needs: hR : R ≤ (2 * b₁ + 2 * b₂ + b₃) * L ^ 2

decls.name: assembly_arith
decls.why: Scalar arithmetic of the final absorption into `C·S·L²`.

decls.name: psiWeak_of_RH_EF_NT
decls.why: THE ASSEMBLY — the decomposition closed. Under hRH (Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`), hEF (`StmtExplicitFormula c₁ c₂ x₁` — the truncated explicit formula, the open leaf), and hNT (`Riemann_vonMangoldt_bound b₁ b₂ b₃` — Rosser Th. 19, the other open leaf), the ψ-side weak bound holds with computed constant: `StmtPsiWeak (9c₁ + c₂ + 28 + 16b₁ + 16b₂ + 8b₃ + 4W) 2 (max x₁ 16)`. The dyadic level is chosen from `x` itself (`K = Nat.log 2 ⌊x⌋`, so `x < 2^(K+1) ≤ 2x`). PsiToPi's `schoenfeldWeak_of_psiWeak` carries the conclusion to `π − Li`, Statement's `weakWindow_of_global` to the window, O68's arit…
decls.proves: StmtPsiWeak (9 * c₁ + c₂ + 28 + 16 * b₁ + 16 * b₂ + 8 * b₃ + 4 * W) 2 (max x₁ 16)

header: AssemblyFloor — block E1 of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. `Assembly.psiWeak_of_RH_EF_NT` with nothing rounded at the end. Inside that proof the contour constants `c₁`, `c₂` multiply `log²x` with no `√x`, and the zero side is a polynomial in `log T`; its closing lemmas round every term up to one multiple of `√x·log²x`, valid from `x ≥ 16` (units 0405, 0406). Here the floor `x₀` is a parameter, the height is the power of two just below `x²` (`StmtExplicitFormulaPoly` allows `T ≤ x²`), and each term keep…

decls.name: floorConst
decls.why: The constant of the assembly at floor `x₀`.
needs: c₁ c₂ b₁ b₂ b₃ W x₀ : ℝ

decls.name: floorConst_nonneg
decls.why: If `c₁`, `c₂`, `b₁`, `b₂`, `b₃`, `W` are nonnegative and `16 ≤ x₀`, then the assembly's constant `floorConst c₁ c₂ b₁ b₂ b₃ W x₀` is nonnegative.
decls.proves: 0 ≤ floorConst c₁ c₂ b₁ b₂ b₃ W x₀

decls.name: rem_floor
decls.why: The remainder with `T` near `x²`: `c₁·x·G²/T ≤ 18·c₁·L²/x`.
decls.proves: c₁ * xx * G ^ 2 / TT ≤ 18 * c₁ * L ^ 2 / xx

decls.name: zeroinner_floor
decls.why: The zero side's inner factor, each term at its own power of `L`.

decls.name: floor_arith
decls.why: The closing arithmetic with every term at its own shape.
needs: hA : A ≤ 18 * c₁ * L ^ 2 / xx + c₂ * L + S * (4 * L ^ 2 + P * L + Q)
decls.proves: A ≤ (4 + P / L₀ + Q / L₀ ^ 2 + 18 * c₁ / (x₀ * S₀) + c₂ / (S₀ * L₀)) * S * L ^ 2

decls.name: psiWeak_floor
decls.why: The assembly at floor `x₀`. Under RH, the truncated explicit formula and the zero-count band, `|ψ x − x| ≤ floorConst … x₀ · √x · log²x` for `x ≥ x₀`. The height is the power of two in `(x²/2, x²]`.
decls.proves: StmtPsiWeak (floorConst c₁ c₂ b₁ b₂ b₃ W x₀) 2 x₀

decls.name: schoenfeldWeak_floor_of_RH
decls.why: From RH to the `π` side, floor a parameter. The three proved inputs composed: `Glue.stmtEF_poly`, `ArgCount.rvM_crude`, and `schoenfeldWeak_of_psiWeak`.
decls.proves: ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 ≤ c₁ ∧ 0 ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ x₀ : ℝ, 16 ≤ x₀ → StmtSchoenfeldWeak (3 * floorConst c₁ c₂ 112 0 698 weightedZeroHeightBucket x₀ + 13) 1 (max (x₀ ^ 2) 9) (fun x => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ)) Li

header: AttainedPi — block C7 of `lean_stage3/design/carlson.md`. 2026-11-23. The one-ladder converse for the count of primes when the largest real part of the zeros of ζ is attained. Let `ρ₀` have the largest real part `Θ` among the zeros. If the count of primes at the doublings `2^r` stays within `C·r²·√2^r` of `Li`, then the Riemann hypothesis holds. There may be infinitely many zeros off the line.

decls.name: norm_ipart_le_of_le
decls.why: The integral in one zero's part, against a larger exponent. For a real part `b > 0`, any `c` with `b ≤ c ≤ 1`, and `x ≥ 4`, the integral is at most `(3√x + 4x^c/(c·log²x))/|ρ|`.
decls.proves: ‖ipart ρ x‖ ≤ ‖ρ‖⁻¹ * (3 * Real.sqrt x + 4 * x ^ c / (c * Real.log x ^ 2))

decls.name: one_le_log
decls.why: `log x ≥ 1` for `x ≥ 4`.

decls.name: norm_log_ipart_le
decls.why: `log x` times the integral in one zero's part. For a real part `b` in `(0, 1]` and `x ≥ 4`, with `c = max b (1/2)`, it is at most `(3√x·log x + 8x^c/log x)/|ρ|`.
decls.proves: Real.log x * ‖ipart ρ x‖ ≤ ‖ρ‖⁻¹ * (3 * (Real.sqrt x * Real.log x) + 8 * (x ^ max ρ.re (1 / 2) / Real.log x))

decls.name: norm_log_piMode_le
decls.why: `log x` times one zero's part of the count. For a real part `b` in `(0, 1]` and `x ≥ 4`, with `c = max b (1/2)`, it is at most `(x^b + 3√x·log x + 8x^c/log x)/|ρ|`.
decls.proves: Real.log x * ‖piMode ρ x‖ ≤ ‖ρ‖⁻¹ * (x ^ ρ.re + 3 * (Real.sqrt x * Real.log x) + 8 * (x ^ max ρ.re (1 / 2) / Real.log x))

decls.name: norm_log_piMode_low
decls.why: A zero at or left of `θ₁`. For a real part `b` in `(0, θ₁]` with `θ₁ ≥ 1/2` and `x ≥ 4`, `log x` times the zero's part is at most `(9x^θ₁ + 3√x·log x)/|ρ|`.
decls.proves: Real.log x * ‖piMode ρ x‖ ≤ ‖ρ‖⁻¹ * (9 * x ^ θ₁ + 3 * (Real.sqrt x * Real.log x))

decls.name: norm_log_piMode_band
decls.why: A zero in the band below the top line. For a real part `b` in `(1/2, Θ]`, `x ≥ 4` and `log x ≥ 8`, `log x` times the zero's part is at most `(2x^Θ + 3√x·log x)/|ρ|`.
decls.proves: Real.log x * ‖piMode ρ x‖ ≤ ‖ρ‖⁻¹ * (2 * x ^ Θ + 3 * (Real.sqrt x * Real.log x))

decls.name: topRow
decls.why: The zeros below height `2^r` with real part `Θ`.

decls.name: slack
decls.why: The part of the row's bound that is small against `(2^Θ)^r` for fixed parameters.
needs: Θ θ₁ C M ε : ℝ

decls.name: slack_isLittleO
decls.why: The slack is small against the top line. If `θ₁ < Θ` and `Θ > 1/2`, the slack is `o((2^Θ)^r)`.
decls.proves: (fun r : ℕ => slack Θ θ₁ C M ε r) =o[atTop] fun r : ℕ => ((2:ℝ) ^ Θ) ^ r

decls.name: fin_bound
decls.why: The zeros of the top line below one row. Let every zero have real part at most `Θ > 1/2`, let `M` bound the weights on the line, and `ε` the weights of every finite set in the band `(θ₁, Θ)`, with `θ₁ ≥ 1/2`. If `r ≥ 12` and the count of primes at `2^r` is within `C·r²·√2^r` of `Li`, the sum of `m(ρ)/ρ·(2^ρ)^r` over the zeros of the line below `2^r` is at most `slack + 2ε·(2^Θ)^r`.
needs: hM : ∀ v : Finset NontrivialZeros, (∀ ρ ∈ v, Θ ≤ (ρ : ℂ).re) → ∑ ρ ∈ v, ZeroSummable.w ρ ≤ M
hband : ∀ F : Finset NontrivialZeros, (∀ ρ ∈ F, θ₁ < (ρ : ℂ).re ∧ (ρ : ℂ).re < Θ) → ∑ ρ ∈ F, ordR ρ * ‖(ρ : ℂ)‖⁻¹ ≤ ε
hrow : |(Nat.primeCounting ⌊(2:ℝ) ^ r⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li ((2:ℝ) ^ r)| ≤ C * (r : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ r
decls.proves: ‖∑ ρ ∈ topRow Θ r, LadderMean.coef ρ * ((2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ r‖ ≤ slack Θ θ₁ C M ε r + 2 * ε * ((2:ℝ) ^ Θ) ^ r

decls.name: band_small
decls.why: The band below the top line carries little weight. For `Θ > 1/2` and `ε > 0` there is `η ∈ (0, (Θ − 1/2)/2]` such that every finite set of zeros with real parts in `(Θ − η, Θ)` has `Σ m(ρ)/|ρ| ≤ ε`.
decls.proves: ∃ η : ℝ, 0 < η ∧ η ≤ (Θ - 1 / 2) / 2 ∧ ∀ F : Finset NontrivialZeros, (∀ ρ ∈ F, Θ - η < (ρ : ℂ).re ∧ (ρ : ℂ).re < Θ) → ∑ ρ ∈ F, ordR ρ * ‖(ρ : ℂ)‖⁻¹ ≤ ε

decls.name: fin_eventually
decls.why: The top line below the rows is eventually small. Let `Θ ∈ (1/2, 1]` bound the real parts of all zeros, and let the count of primes at the doublings stay within `C·r²·√2^r` of `Li`. Then for every `ε > 0`, from some row on, the sum of `m(ρ)/ρ·(2^ρ)^r` over the zeros of the line `Re = Θ` below `2^r` is at most `ε·(2^Θ)^r`.
needs: hrows : ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in atTop, |(Nat.primeCounting ⌊(2:ℝ) ^ r⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li ((2:ℝ) ^ r)| ≤ C * (r : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ r
decls.proves: ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in atTop, ‖∑ ρ ∈ topRow Θ r, LadderMean.coef ρ * ((2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ r‖ ≤ ε * ((2:ℝ) ^ Θ) ^ r

decls.name: lineSet
decls.why: The zeros on the line `Re = Θ`.

decls.name: mem_lineSet
decls.why: A zero is on the line exactly when its real part is `Θ`.

decls.name: term
decls.why: One zero's term at row `r`, measured against `(2^Θ)^r`.

decls.name: tailTerm
decls.why: One zero's term on the line, kept only above height `2^r`.

decls.name: norm_term
decls.why: A zero on the line has a term of size `m(ρ)/|ρ|` at every row.

decls.name: norm_tailTerm_le
decls.why: The part above height `2^r` of a zero's term is at most its weight on the line.
decls.proves: ‖tailTerm Θ r ρ‖ ≤ (lineSet Θ).indicator (fun ρ => ‖LadderMean.coef ρ‖) ρ

decls.name: summable_line
decls.why: For `Θ > 1/2` the weights on the line, as a function on all zeros, are summable.

decls.name: tsum_split
decls.why: The line's sum splits at height `2^r`. For `Θ > 1/2`, the sum over the line of the terms at row `r` is the sum over the zeros of the line below `2^r`, over `(2^Θ)^r`, plus the sum of the parts above `2^r`.
decls.proves: ∑' ρ : lineSet Θ, term Θ r ρ = (∑ ρ ∈ topRow Θ r, LadderMean.coef ρ * ((2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ r) / ((((2:ℝ) ^ Θ : ℝ)) : ℂ) ^ r + ∑' ρ, tailTerm Θ r ρ

decls.name: tendsto_tail
decls.why: The parts above height `2^r` fade. For `Θ > 1/2`, the sum over the line of the terms of the zeros above `2^r` tends to zero as the rows go on.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun r : ℕ => ∑' ρ, tailTerm Θ r ρ) atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: attained_off_line_pi
decls.why: The largest real part attained, and the count of primes of square-root size at the doublings: then the Riemann hypothesis holds. Let `ρ₀` have the largest real part among the zeros of ζ. If the count of primes at `2^r` stays within `C·r²·√2^r` of `Li` from some row on, the Riemann hypothesis holds.
needs: hrows : ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in Filter.atTop, |(Nat.primeCounting ⌊(2:ℝ) ^ r⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li ((2:ℝ) ^ r)| ≤ C * (r : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ r

header: BandJoin — block J5 of `lean_stage3/design/closedloop.md`. 2026-11-23. The band of the deep zero and the strip of the zeros, under one map.

decls.name: bandR
decls.why: The band's map at base `2`: a share, or a real part, `x` goes to `2^(−x)`.

decls.name: bandR_zero
decls.why: Share `0`, the deep zero, is on the outer circle.

decls.name: bandR_one

header: CellBdiff — block T1b of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. Joint T1 on the table tree's own operator. `CellZeros.stencil` is a second writing of `d` backward differences. The table tree's writing is `Chain.bdiff` iterated `d` times, the operator `Chain.A4` and `Superposition` are stated on. Here the two are shown equal on any row, and the cell theorem is restated with `bdiff^[d]`, `Sym`, `mode` and `modeSum`, all four from the table tree.

decls.name: bdZ
decls.why: One backward difference on a row indexed by the integers.

decls.name: iter_bdZ_eq_fwdDiff
decls.why: `n` backward differences of a row are `(−1)^n` times its `n`-th forward difference at step `−1`.
decls.proves: (bdZ^[n]) a r = (-1 : ℂ) ^ n * (fwdDiff (-1 : ℤ))^[n] a r

decls.name: iter_bdZ_eq_stencil
decls.why: `n` backward differences are the stencil.
decls.proves: (bdZ^[n]) a r = CellZeros.stencil n a r

decls.name: bdiff_iter_eq_bdZ
decls.why: The table tree's operator on a function of `ℂ` agrees with the row's on the integers.
needs: hag : ∀ n : ℤ, g (n : ℂ) = a n

decls.name: stencil_eq_bdiff_iter
decls.why: The stencil is the table tree's operator, iterated.
needs: hag : ∀ n : ℤ, g (n : ℂ) = a n
decls.proves: CellZeros.stencil d a r = (Chain.bdiff^[d]) g (r : ℂ)

decls.why: The row of the log-weighted prime count along the doublings, on `ℂ`.

decls.name: psiRow_int
decls.why: On an integer the row is the log-weighted prime count at that doubling.

decls.name: cell_eq_modeSum_bdiff
decls.why: The cell on the table tree's operators. `d` backward differences of the row, with `Chain.bdiff`, are the main mode minus the reweighted sum of the zeros' modes, within the stated error.

header: CellFixedRow — block F3 of `lean_stage3/design/leftedge.md`. 2026-11-23. The cell at a fixed row with the height of the zero sum taken to infinity. `LeftSmooth.explicit_formula_all` holds at every height `T ≥ 2`, with no cap `T ≤ x²`. Through the stencil, the cell at row `r`, depth `d`, and its zero sum to any height differ by the stencil of that bound. As `T → ∞` at the fixed row the first term of the bound tends to zero, and what stays is free of the height.

decls.name: cell_eq_zero_sum_all
decls.why: The cell as a sum over the zeros, at every height. For `16 ≤ 2^(r−d)` and any `T ≥ 2`, the cell at row `r`, depth `d`, minus its main term, plus the sum over the zeros below `T`, has norm at most the stencil of the explicit formula's error at every height, read on the `d + 1` rows the stencil touches.

decls.name: cell_zero_sum_finset_all
decls.why: The same, over the finite set of zeros below the height.
decls.proves: ‖CellZeros.stencil d (fun n : ℤ => (Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ) ^ n) : ℂ)) r - (2:ℂ) ^ r * (1 - (2:ℂ)⁻¹) ^ d + ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, term d r ρ‖ ≤ ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), (d.choose j : ℝ) * (Glue.c1n * (2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ)) * Real.log ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ)) * T) ^ 2 / T + Glue.c3n * Real.log ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ))) + LeftSmooth.Bleft * ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ))) ^ (-(1:ℝ) / 4))

decls.name: Bleft_nonneg
decls.why: The left-edge constant is nonnegative: it bounds a norm at `x = 16`, `T = 2`.

decls.name: tendsto_log_sq_div
decls.why: For a fixed constant `c > 0`, `log²(c·T)/T` times `a` tends to zero as `T → ∞`.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun T : ℝ => a * c * Real.log (c * T) ^ 2 / T) atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: cell_fixed_row
decls.why: The cell at a fixed row, the height to infinity. For `d + 4 ≤ r` and every `ε > 0`, for all large heights `T` the cell at row `r`, depth `d`, minus its main term, plus its sum over the zeros below `T`, has norm at most `2^d·(c3n·log 2·r + Bleft) + ε`. The bound left is free of the height.
decls.proves: ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in Filter.atTop, ‖CellZeros.stencil d (fun n : ℤ => (Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ) ^ n) : ℂ)) (r : ℤ) - (2:ℂ) ^ (r : ℤ) * (1 - (2:ℂ)⁻¹) ^ d + ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, term d (r : ℤ) ρ‖ ≤ 2 ^ d * (Glue.c3n * Real.log 2 * r + LeftSmooth.Bleft) + ε

decls.name: resid
decls.why: The residual of the count on the rung `a·2^m`.

decls.name: cellResid
decls.why: The residual of the cell `(r, d)` on the ladder started at `a`.

decls.name: cellSize
decls.why: Square-root size at the cell `(r, d)`.

decls.name: CellsSqrt
decls.why: Every cell of every dyadic ladder has its residual at square-root size.

decls.name: stencilR_abs_le
decls.why: A cell is no larger than its window allows. If the values the stencil reads shrink by a factor `t` per step down the window, the cell is at most the top bound times `(1 + t)^n`.
needs: h : ∀ k ∈ range (n + 1), |g (r - k)| ≤ B * t ^ k
decls.proves: |stencilR n g r| ≤ B * (1 + t) ^ n

decls.name: stencilR_one
decls.why: The stencil of order one is one backward difference.
decls.proves: stencilR 1 g r = g r - g (r - 1)

decls.name: weak_nonneg
decls.why: The square-root bound on the count may be taken with a constant that is not negative and a starting point of at least two.

decls.proves: StmtSchoenfeldWeak (max C 0) 1 (max x₀ 2) (fun x => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ)) Stage3.Li

decls.name: resid_le
decls.why: One rung. Under the square-root bound on the count, the residual on the rung `a·2^m` is at most a constant times `(m + 1)·2^(m/2)`.

decls.name: cells_of_RH
decls.why: Forward, from the Riemann hypothesis. Under it every cell of every dyadic ladder has its residual at square-root size.

decls.name: step_le
decls.why: A depth-0 cell is the difference of two neighbouring rungs, so `CellsSqrt` bounds that difference.

decls.why: The square root of two is at least four thirds; the telescoping sum closes on this.

decls.name: ladder_le
decls.why: The depth-0 cells, summed up one ladder.

decls.name: base_bound

decls.name: schoenfeldWeak_of_cells

decls.why: The Riemann hypothesis is the cells at square-root size, over every dyadic ladder.

decls.why: The integer cell, cast, is the stencil of the count one order up.

header: CellRows — block T3a of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. The height of the zero sum taken to infinity along the rows. At row `r` the height is the doubling of the cell's lowest row, `2^(r−d)`. The cell is then its main term minus the sum over the zeros below that height, within a constant times `r²`. Against square-root size that error tends to zero: the tail of the zero sum is inside the error.

decls.name: cell_eq_zero_sum_rows
decls.why: The cell at the row's own height.

decls.name: cell_tail_tendsto
decls.why: The tail of the zero sum is inside the error. With the height `2^(r−d)` at row `r`, the distance between the cell and its zero sum, over `√2^r`, tends to zero.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun r : ℕ => ‖CellZeros.stencil d (fun n : ℤ => (Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ) ^ n) : ℂ)) (r : ℤ) - (2:ℂ) ^ (r : ℤ) * (1 - (2:ℂ)⁻¹) ^ d + ∑ ρ ∈ ZF ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - d)), term d (r : ℤ) ρ‖ / Real.sqrt 2 ^ r) atTop (𝓝 0)

header: CellZeros — block T1 of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. The cell as a sum over the zeros. For the row `ψ(2^n)` of the log-weighted prime count along the doublings, the `d`-fold backward difference at `r` is the main term `2^r·(1 − 1/2)^d` minus a sum over the zeros of ζ below a height, each zero a mode `(2^ρ)^r` multiplied by the symbol `(1 − 2^(−ρ))` once per depth, within a stated error. No RH.

decls.name: stencil
decls.why: The `d`-fold backward difference of a row, read at `r`.

decls.name: stencil_add
decls.why: The stencil of a sum of two rows is the sum of their stencils.
decls.proves: stencil d (fun n => a n + b n) r = stencil d a r + stencil d b r

decls.name: stencil_sub
decls.why: The stencil of a difference of two rows is the difference of their stencils.
decls.proves: stencil d (fun n => a n - b n) r = stencil d a r - stencil d b r

decls.name: stencil_const_mul
decls.why: The stencil of a row multiplied by a constant `c` is `c` times the stencil of the row.
decls.proves: stencil d (fun n => c * a n) r = c * stencil d a r

decls.name: stencil_sum
decls.why: The stencil of a finite sum of rows is the sum of the stencils of the rows.
decls.proves: stencil d (fun n => ∑ i ∈ s, f i n) r = ∑ i ∈ s, stencil d (f i) r

decls.name: stencil_mode
decls.why: On a mode the stencil is the symbol to the `d`.
decls.proves: stencil d (fun n : ℤ => w ^ n) r = w ^ r * (1 - w⁻¹) ^ d

decls.proves: ‖stencil d a r‖ ≤ ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), (d.choose j : ℝ) * B j

decls.name: two_cpow_ne_zero

decls.name: stencil_zeroPartialSum
decls.why: The stencil passes through the sum over the zeros.

decls.why: The cell as a sum over the zeros.

header: ClosedLoopJoin — block J1 of `lean_stage3/design/closedloop.md`: the join between `lean_primebeat` and Stage 3. 2026-11-23.

decls.name: epsilon
decls.why: The displacement from one half. Restated from the closed loop, Part VII.

decls.name: restoringForce
decls.why: The closed loop's restoring force. Restated from Part VII.

decls.name: primeWeight
decls.why: The scaling weight of a prime. Restated from Part VIII.

decls.name: isHermitianHandshake
decls.why: The Hermitian handshake. Restated from Part VIII.

decls.name: force_eq
decls.why: The closed loop's force is five times the distance from one half.

decls.name: force_join
decls.why: The two forces are one. For a base above one, the mirror imbalance of a mode of the table is the closed loop's restoring force at the mode's real part, times a constant that depends on the base alone.
decls.proves: StencilWeil.restoringForce b ρ = 2 * Real.log b / 5 * restoringForce ρ.re

decls.name: force_eq_zero_iff
decls.why: The closed loop's force is zero exactly at one half.

decls.name: primeWeight_eq_inv_side
decls.why: A prime's weight at the real part of a point is the reciprocal of the size of the prime's mode there.
decls.proves: primeWeight p ρ.re = (‖((p : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ ρ‖)⁻¹

decls.name: handshake_iff_sides
decls.why: The handshake is the two sides agreeing. The Hermitian handshake at the real part of a point holds exactly when, at every prime above three, the mode and its mirror have the same size.
decls.proves: isHermitianHandshake ρ.re ↔ ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p > 3 → ‖((p : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ ρ‖ = ‖((p : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (1 - ρ)‖

decls.name: handshake_iff_half
decls.why: The handshake holds exactly at one half.

decls.name: structural_contradiction
decls.why: The structural contradiction, the closed loop's main theorem (Part XI): away from one half the restoring force is nonzero and the handshake fails.

decls.name: off_line_zero
decls.why: The structural contradiction at a zero of zeta. If a nontrivial zero is off the line, then the closed loop's force there is nonzero, the handshake fails, the mirror imbalance of its mode is nonzero at every base above one, and one of the mode's two sides is longer than the square root of the base.
decls.proves: restoringForce (ρ : ℂ).re ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ isHermitianHandshake (ρ : ℂ).re ∧ ∀ b : ℝ, 1 < b → StencilWeil.restoringForce b (ρ : ℂ) ≠ 0 ∧ Real.sqrt b < max ‖(b : ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)‖ ‖(b : ℂ) ^ (1 - (ρ : ℂ))‖

decls.name: rh_iff_re_half
decls.why: The Riemann hypothesis is every nontrivial zero having real part one half.

decls.name: rh_iff_force_zero
decls.why: The Riemann hypothesis is the force at rest. RH holds exactly when the closed loop's restoring force is zero at every nontrivial zero of zeta.

decls.name: rh_iff_handshake
decls.why: The Riemann hypothesis is the handshake. RH holds exactly when the Hermitian handshake holds at every nontrivial zero of zeta.

header: CompositeSplit — block R10 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`. 2026-11-23. The composite table has no signs. The sieve's sum counts a composite once for every set of small primes dividing it and corrects with the Pascal signs. Each composite has exactly one least prime. Counted under its least prime, every composite is counted once, and every part is a positive count. The part of a prime `p` is the same table at the scale `N/p`: the numbers up to `N/p` that no prime below `p` divides.

decls.name: rough
decls.why: The numbers from `1` to `N/p` that no prime below `p` divides: the table at the scale `N/p`, sieved by the primes below `p`.

decls.name: least_prime_fiber
decls.why: The numbers from `2` to `N` whose least prime is `p` are `p` times the numbers up to `N/p` that no prime below `p` divides.
decls.proves: (Icc 2 N).filter (fun n => n.minFac = p) = ((Icc 1 (N / p)).filter (fun m => ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → q < p → ¬ q ∣ m)).image (fun m => p * m)

decls.name: card_least_prime
decls.why: The part of a prime. The count of the numbers from `2` to `N` with least prime `p` is the table's count at the scale `N/p`.
decls.proves: ((Icc 2 N).filter (fun n => n.minFac = p)).card = rough N p

decls.name: minFac_mem_smallPrimes
decls.why: A composite up to `N` has its least prime among the primes up to `√N`.

decls.name: composites_by_least_prime
decls.why: Every composite once, under its least prime. No signs.
decls.proves: ((Icc 2 N).filter (fun n => ¬ n.Prime)).card = ∑ p ∈ smallPrimes N, ((Icc 2 N).filter (fun n => ¬ n.Prime ∧ n.minFac = p)).card

decls.name: composite_part
decls.why: A prime's part of the composites, with the prime itself put back, is the table's count at the scale `N/p`.
decls.proves: ((Icc 2 N).filter (fun n => ¬ n.Prime ∧ n.minFac = p)).card + 1 = rough N p

decls.name: composites_no_signs
decls.why: The composite table, no signs. The composites up to `N`, with one for each prime up to `√N`, are the sum over those primes of the table's count at the scale `N/p`. Every term is a count.
decls.proves: ((Icc 2 N).filter (fun n => ¬ n.Prime)).card + (smallPrimes N).card = ∑ p ∈ smallPrimes N, rough N p

header: Compression — block R11 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`. 2026-11-23. The primes as the compression of the composites. The combinations of the primes up to `√N` never repeat and do not fill the numbers up to `N`. What they leave is exactly the new primes, each with its multiples, and no number is counted twice: a number up to `N` has at most one prime factor above `√N`.

decls.name: smooth
decls.why: The numbers from `1` to `N` that are combinations of the primes up to `√N`: every prime dividing them is at most `√N`.

decls.name: newPrimes
decls.why: The new primes: those above `√N`, up to `N`.

decls.name: unique_new_prime
decls.why: No number is claimed twice. A number up to `N` has at most one prime factor above `√N`.

decls.name: nonSmooth_eq_biUnion
decls.why: The numbers that are not combinations of the primes so far are the multiples of the new primes.
decls.proves: (Icc 1 N).filter (fun n => ¬ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ n → p ≤ Nat.sqrt N) = (newPrimes N).biUnion (fun p => (Icc 1 N).filter (fun n => p ∣ n))

decls.name: compression
decls.why: The compression. The numbers up to `N` are the combinations of the primes up to `√N`, and for each new prime its multiples up to `N`, with nothing counted twice.
decls.proves: N = smooth N + ∑ p ∈ newPrimes N, N / p

header: # The contour shift — slices 2, 3, 4 (hEF's build order, entry 257) Written as the slice map for the contour shift, with named `sorry`s so the obligations were real Lean statements before proof. S2 and S4 are proved here; S3 is proved downstream (`EdgeBound`, `Glue`) and its placeholder is gone. Sorry-free since 2026-09-01.

decls.name: zeroGap
decls.why: The ordinate gap the pigeonhole delivers: crude-explicit, `1/(180·log T + 1060)`.

decls.name: zeroGap_pos
decls.why: For `T ≥ 2`, the ordinate gap `zeroGap T` is positive.

decls.name: zeroGap_le
decls.why: For `T ≥ 2`, the ordinate gap `zeroGap T` is at most `9/10`.

decls.name: zeta_analyticAt
decls.why: `ζ` is analytic away from the pole.

decls.name: one_le_zeta_order
decls.why: At a zero away from the pole, the order is at least one.

decls.name: partner_zero
decls.why: The reflection partner: every ordinate of a nontrivial zero carries a zero with `re ∈ [1/2, 1)` at the same ordinate.
decls.proves: ∃ ρ' : ℂ, riemannZeta ρ' = 0 ∧ ρ'.im = ρ.im ∧ 1/2 ≤ ρ'.re ∧ ρ'.re < 1

decls.name: mem_zetaWindow
decls.why: Membership in a `zetaWindow` from coordinate bounds.

decls.name: goodT_exists
decls.why: Slice 2 — good heights exist.
decls.proves: ∃ T' ∈ Set.Icc T (T+1), ∀ ρ : ℂ, riemannZeta ρ = 0 → 0 < ρ.re → zeroGap T ≤ |ρ.im - T'|

decls.name: borderIntegrable_sum_poles
decls.why: A finite sum of simple-pole principal parts is border-integrable when every pole is interior.
needs: pIn : ∀ p ∈ P, Rectangle z w ∈ nhds p
decls.proves: RectangleBorderIntegrable (fun s ↦ ∑ p ∈ P, A p / (s - p)) z w

decls.name: rectangleIntegral_sum_poles
decls.why: The rectangle integral of a finite sum of simple-pole principal parts, all poles interior, is the sum of the residues.
needs: pIn : ∀ p ∈ P, Rectangle z w ∈ nhds p
decls.proves: RectangleIntegral' (fun s ↦ ∑ p ∈ P, A p / (s - p)) z w = ∑ p ∈ P, A p

decls.name: residue_rectangle_multi
decls.why: The multi-pole residue theorem on a rectangle. If `f` agrees off the pole set with `g + Σ_p A p/(s − p)` for `g` holomorphic on the whole rectangle and every pole interior, then the rectangle integral of `f` collects every residue.
needs: pIn : ∀ p ∈ P, Rectangle z w ∈ nhds p
principal : Set.EqOn (f - fun s ↦ ∑ p ∈ P, A p / (s - p)) g (Rectangle z w \ (P : Set ℂ))
decls.proves: RectangleIntegral' f z w = ∑ p ∈ P, A p

decls.name: residue_rectangle_of_local
decls.why: The residue theorem from local data. `f` holomorphic on the rectangle off a finite interior pole set, and at each pole `p` equal to `(analytic at p) + A p/(s − p)` on a punctured neighborhood: the rectangle integral collects every residue. The global extension is glued from the local analytic parts.
needs: pIn : ∀ p ∈ P, Rectangle z w ∈ nhds p
fHolo : HolomorphicOn f (Rectangle z w \ (P : Set ℂ))
hloc : ∀ p ∈ P, ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ h p ∧ ∀ᶠ s in nhdsWithin p {p}ᶜ, f s = h s + A p / (s - p)
decls.proves: RectangleIntegral' f z w = ∑ p ∈ P, A p

decls.name: analyticAt_dslope
decls.why: `dslope` of an analytic function is analytic at the point.

decls.name: div_sub_eq_dslope
decls.why: Off the point, `f s/(s−p)` splits as `f p/(s−p) + dslope f p s`.
decls.proves: f s / (s - p) = f p / (s - p) + dslope f p s

decls.name: zeta_local_data
decls.why: The local pole data of `G = (−ζ′/ζ)·x^s/s` at a factorization point. Where `ζ` factors as `(s−p)^n·g` with `g` analytic and nonvanishing at `p ≠ 0`, `G` splits as `analytic + (−n·x^p/p)/(s−p)` on a punctured neighborhood: the pole is simple with residue `−n·x^p/p`. Covers every nontrivial zero (`n = order ≥ 1`) and the pole of `ζ` at `1` (`n = −1`, residue `+x`) in one statement.
needs: hfac : ∀ᶠ s in nhdsWithin p {p}ᶜ, riemannZeta s = (s - p) ^ n * g s
decls.proves: ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ h p ∧ ∀ᶠ s in nhdsWithin p {p}ᶜ, - deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ s / s = h s + (-(n:ℂ) * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ p / p) / (s - p)

decls.name: zeta_order_ne_top
decls.why: The order of `ζ` at any point off the pole is finite (identity theorem on `ℂ∖{1}`, as in `one_le_zeta_order`).

decls.name: zeta_local_data_zero
decls.why: Local pole data of `G` at a nontrivial zero: residue `−(order)·x^ρ/ρ`.
decls.proves: ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ h ρ ∧ ∀ᶠ s in nhdsWithin ρ {ρ}ᶜ, - deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ s / s = h s + (-(analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta ρ : ℂ) * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ ρ / ρ) / (s - ρ)

decls.name: zeta_local_data_one
decls.why: Local pole data of `G` at `1`: residue `+x`. The factorization `ζ = (s−1)^{−1}·g` is built from the completed zeta function.
decls.proves: ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ h 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ s in nhdsWithin 1 {1}ᶜ, - deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ s / s = h s + ((x:ℝ):ℂ) / (s - 1)

decls.name: zeta_local_data_origin
decls.why: Local pole data of `G` at `0`: residue `−ζ′(0)/ζ(0)`.
decls.proves: ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ h 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ s in nhdsWithin 0 {0}ᶜ, - deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ s / s = h s + (- deriv riemannZeta 0 / riemannZeta 0) / (s - 0)

decls.name: zeta_ne_zero_of_re_mem
decls.why: No zeros on the strip `re ∈ [−1, 0]`: the functional equation carries nonvanishing over from `re ∈ [1, 2]`. The cosine factor can only vanish at `s = 1`, where `ζ` has its pole instead.

decls.name: sq_mul_zeta_analyticAt_one
decls.why: `(s−1)²·ζ` is analytic at `1`, from the unconditional completed-zeta formula (junk values at `s = 1` agree on both sides).

decls.name: zeta_meromorphicOn
decls.why: `ζ` is meromorphic on any set.

decls.name: zeta_zeros_rectangle_finite
decls.why: The zeros of `ζ` in a closed rectangle form a finite set.
decls.proves: {ρ : ℂ | riemannZeta ρ = 0 ∧ ρ ∈ Rectangle z w}.Finite

decls.name: order_bridge
decls.why: The ledger's `riemannZeta.order` agrees with `analyticOrderNatAt` away from the pole (mirrors PNT+ KadiriZeroCounting's own bridge).
decls.proves: ((riemannZeta.order ρ : ℤ) : ℂ) = ((analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta ρ : ℕ) : ℂ)

decls.name: zeroPartialSum_eq_sum
decls.why: `zeroPartialSum` as a concrete finite sum, over any `Finset` enumerating exactly the nontrivial zeros below the height.
needs: hiff : ∀ ρ : ℂ, ρ ∈ ZF ↔ (ρ ∈ Kadiri.NontrivialZeros ∧ |ρ.im| < T')
decls.proves: Stage3.zeroPartialSum x T' = ∑ p ∈ ZF, ((analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta p : ℂ) * ((x : ℂ) ^ p / p))

decls.name: analyticAt_conj_conj
decls.why: Analyticity transports through conjugation: `conj ∘ g ∘ conj` is analytic at `conj p`.
decls.proves: AnalyticAt ℂ (fun w ↦ (starRingEnd ℂ) (g ((starRingEnd ℂ) w))) ((starRingEnd ℂ) p)

decls.name: zeta_order_conj
decls.why: The order of `ζ` at the conjugate of a point equals the order at the point (`ζ(conj s) = conj ζ(s)`).
decls.proves: analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta ((starRingEnd ℂ) ρ) = analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta ρ

decls.name: zeta_order_reflect
decls.why: The reflection-order lemma: the order of `ζ` at `1 − conj ρ` equals the order at `ρ`, on the open strip — the functional equation's factor is analytic and nonvanishing there.
decls.proves: analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) ρ) = analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta ρ

decls.name: residue_identity
decls.why: Slice 4 — the residue identity on the good rectangle. The zeros enter here: pulling the line integral to `σ = −1` collects the pole at `1` (residue `x`), the pole at `0` (residue `−ζ′/ζ(0)`), and every nontrivial zero below height `T'` (residue `−m_ρ·x^ρ/ρ`).
needs: hgood : ∀ ρ : ℂ, riemannZeta ρ = 0 → 0 < ρ.re → zeroGap T ≤ |ρ.im - T'|
decls.proves: RectangleIntegral' (fun s : ℂ ↦ (- deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s) * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ s / s) (((-1/4 : ℝ):ℂ) - Complex.I * T') (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * T') = (x : ℂ) - deriv riemannZeta 0 / riemannZeta 0 - Stage3.zeroPartialSum x T'

header: CountEuler — block N3-E of `lean_stage3/design/countmodes.md`, from its section "After the independent check". 2026-11-23.

decls.name: binom_shift
decls.why: The binomial identity of the transform. For any `ζ`, `c` and `m`, `Σ_{j≤m} C(m,j)·(−c)^(m−j)·ζ^(j+1) = ζ·(ζ − c)^m`.
decls.proves: ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), (m.choose j : ℂ) * (-c) ^ (m - j) * ζ ^ (j + 1) = ζ * (ζ - c) ^ m

decls.name: zeta
decls.why: The point of the segment of a mode at depth `s`: `ζ_s = e^w·e^(−s)`.

decls.name: coefE
decls.why: The coefficient of the Euler transform: `C(m,j)·(−c)^(m−j)`.

decls.name: seg
decls.why: The transformed integrand: `ζ_s·(ζ_s − c)^m/(w − s)`.

decls.name: F
decls.why: The transformed segment integral: `∫₀^∞ ζ_s·(ζ_s − c)^m/(w − s) ds`.

decls.name: zeta_pow
decls.why: The power of the point of the segment is the integrand of `J`: `ζ_s^k/(w − s) = e^(k(w−s))/(w − s)`.
decls.proves: zeta w s ^ k / (w - s) = Complex.exp ((k:ℂ) * (w - s)) / (w - s)

decls.name: J_eq_zeta
decls.why: `J k w` written with the point of the segment.
decls.proves: CountModes.J k w = ∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), zeta w s ^ k / (w - s)

decls.name: integrable_zeta_pow
decls.why: For `1 ≤ k` and `Im w ≠ 0`, `ζ_s^k/(w − s)` is integrable on `s > 0`.
decls.proves: IntegrableOn (fun s : ℝ => zeta w s ^ k / (w - s)) (Set.Ioi 0)

decls.name: seg_sum
decls.why: The transformed integrand is the transform of the powers.
decls.proves: seg w c m s = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), coefE c m j * (zeta w s ^ (j + 1) / (w - s))

decls.name: transform_eq
decls.why: The transform of the segment integrals. For `Im w ≠ 0`, `Σ_{j≤m} C(m,j)·(−c)^(m−j)·J_{j+1}(w) = ∫₀^∞ ζ_s·(ζ_s − c)^m/(w − s) ds`.
decls.proves: ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), coefE c m j * CountModes.J (j + 1) w = F w c m

decls.name: transform_le
decls.why: The size of the transform. If `‖a_k‖ ≤ A·k²·X^k` for every `k ≥ 1`, with `A, X ≥ 0`, then `‖Σ_{j≤m} C(m,j)·(−c)^(m−j)·a_{j+1}‖ ≤ A·(m+1)²·X·(X + ‖c‖)^m`.
needs: ha : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖a k‖ ≤ A * (k:ℝ) ^ 2 * X ^ k
decls.proves: ‖∑ j ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), coefE c m j * a (j + 1)‖ ≤ A * ((m:ℝ) + 1) ^ 2 * X * (X + ‖c‖) ^ m

decls.name: seg_in_ball
decls.why: The segment stays in the ball. If `‖c‖ ≤ r` and `‖z − c‖ ≤ r`, then `‖z·t − c‖ ≤ r` for `0 ≤ t ≤ 1`: `z·t − c = t·(z − c) + (1 − t)·(−c)`.

decls.name: others_le
decls.why: One other mode. For `Im w ≠ 0`, `‖c‖ ≤ r` and `‖e^w − c‖ ≤ r`, the transformed segment integral is at most `‖e^w‖·r^m/|Im w|`.
decls.proves: ‖F w c m‖ ≤ ‖Complex.exp w‖ * r ^ m / |w.im|

decls.name: lor
decls.why: The Cauchy weight of `w`: `((s − Re w)² + (Im w)²)⁻¹ = 1/|w − s|²`.

decls.name: lor_nonneg
decls.why: The Cauchy weight is nonnegative.

decls.name: lor_eq
decls.why: The Cauchy weight is `π/|Im w|` times the Cauchy density at `Re w` of scale `|Im w|`.
decls.proves: lor w s = Real.pi / |w.im| * ProbabilityTheory.cauchyPDFReal w.re ‖w.im‖₊ s

decls.name: integrable_lor
decls.why: For `Im w ≠ 0` the Cauchy weight is integrable on the line.

decls.name: integral_lor
decls.why: For `Im w ≠ 0` the Cauchy weight integrates to `π/|Im w|` over the line.

decls.name: setIntegral_lor_le
decls.why: For `Im w ≠ 0` the Cauchy weight integrates to at most `π/|Im w|` over `s > 0`.
decls.proves: ∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), lor w s ≤ Real.pi / |w.im|

decls.name: norm_sub_sq
decls.why: `‖(w − s)²‖ = (s − Re w)² + (Im w)²`.

decls.name: gf
decls.why: The real profile of the class: `g(s) = p·e^(−s) + κ`.

decls.name: gf_nonneg
decls.why: The profile is nonnegative for `p, κ ≥ 0`.

decls.name: gf_le
decls.why: For `s ≥ 0` the profile is at most `p + κ`.
decls.proves: gf p κ s ≤ p + κ

decls.name: gf_lt
decls.why: For `s > 0` and `p > 0` the profile is below `p + κ`.
decls.proves: gf p κ s < p + κ

decls.name: gf_zero
decls.why: At `s = 0` the profile is `p + κ`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_gf
decls.why: The derivative of the profile: `−p·e^(−s)`.

decls.name: Pc
decls.why: The class integrand: `p·e^(−s)·g(s)^m/(w − s)`.

decls.name: Qc
decls.why: The correction integrand: `g(s)^n/(w − s)²`.

decls.name: Gc
decls.why: The antiderivative: `−g(s)^n/(n·(w − s))`.

decls.name: integrable_Pc
decls.why: For `Im w ≠ 0`, `p, κ ≥ 0` the class integrand is integrable on `s > 0`.

decls.name: norm_Qc_le
decls.why: For `s ≥ 0` the correction integrand is at most `(p + κ)^n` times the Cauchy weight.
decls.proves: ‖Qc w p κ n s‖ ≤ (p + κ) ^ n * lor w s

decls.name: integrable_Qc
decls.why: For `Im w ≠ 0`, `p, κ ≥ 0` the correction integrand is integrable on `s > 0`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_Gc
decls.why: The derivative of the antiderivative: `G' = P − Q/(m + 1)`.
decls.proves: HasDerivAt (Gc w p κ (m + 1)) (Pc w p κ m s - Qc w p κ (m + 1) s / ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ)) s

decls.name: tendsto_Gc
decls.why: The antiderivative tends to zero at infinity.

decls.name: class_main
decls.why: The class integral, exactly. For `Im w ≠ 0`, `p, κ ≥ 0`, `R = p + κ`: `∫₀^∞ p·e^(−s)·g(s)^m/(w − s) ds = R^(m+1)/((m+1)·w) + (∫₀^∞ g(s)^(m+1)/(w − s)² ds)/(m+1)`. The antiderivative is `−g^(m+1)/((m+1)(w − s))`.
decls.proves: ∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), Pc w p κ m s = (((p + κ) ^ (m + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) / (((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ) * w) + (∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), Qc w p κ (m + 1) s) / ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ)

decls.name: seg_class
decls.why: On the class, `ζ_s·(ζ_s − c)^m/(w − s) = u^(m+1)·p·e^(−s)·g(s)^m/(w − s)`, for `e^w = p·u` and `c = −κ·u`.
decls.proves: seg w (-(κ:ℂ) * u) m s = u ^ (m + 1) * Pc w p κ m s

decls.name: F_class
decls.why: On the class, the transformed segment integral is `u^(m+1)·∫₀^∞ P`.
decls.proves: F w (-(κ:ℂ) * u) m = u ^ (m + 1) * ∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), Pc w p κ m s

decls.name: Nn
decls.why: The normaliser: `N_m = u^(m+1)·R^(m+1)/(m+1)`.

decls.name: Qn
decls.why: The normalised correction integrand: `(g(s)/(p + κ))^n/(w − s)²`.

decls.name: norm_Qn_le
decls.why: For `s ≥ 0`, `p > 0`, `κ ≥ 0`, the normalised correction integrand is at most the Cauchy weight.
decls.proves: ‖Qn w p κ n s‖ ≤ lor w s

decls.name: continuous_Qn
decls.why: For `Im w ≠ 0` the normalised correction integrand is continuous.

decls.name: class_ratio
decls.why: The class over the normaliser. For `Im w ≠ 0`, `p > 0`, `κ ≥ 0`, `‖u‖ = 1` and `e^w = p·u`: `F w (−κu) m / N_m = 1/w + ∫₀^∞ (g/R)^(m+1)/(w − s)² ds`, `R = p + κ`.
decls.proves: F w (-(κ:ℂ) * u) m / Nn u (p + κ) m = 1 / w + ∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), Qn w p κ (m + 1) s

decls.name: class_lim
decls.why: The class correction fades. For `Im w ≠ 0`, `p > 0`, `κ ≥ 0`: `∫₀^∞ (g/R)^(m+1)/(w − s)² ds → 0`, by dominated convergence under the Cauchy weight; `g(s) < R` for `s > 0`.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => ∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), Qn w p κ (m + 1) s) atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: norm_Qn_int_le
decls.why: For `Im w ≠ 0`, `p > 0`, `κ ≥ 0`, the class correction is at most `π/|Im w|`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), Qn w p κ n s‖ ≤ Real.pi / |w.im|

decls.name: class_tendsto
decls.why: The class tends to its weight. Under the hypotheses of `class_ratio`, `F w (−κu) m / N_m → 1/w`.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => F w (-(κ:ℂ) * u) m / Nn u (p + κ) m) atTop (𝓝 (1 / w))

decls.name: class_bound
decls.why: The class stays bounded. Under the hypotheses of `class_ratio`, `‖F w (−κu) m / N_m‖ ≤ (1 + π)/|Im w|`.
decls.proves: ‖F w (-(κ:ℂ) * u) m / Nn u (p + κ) m‖ ≤ (1 + Real.pi) / |w.im|

decls.name: others_ratio_le
decls.why: One other mode over the normaliser. For `Im w ≠ 0`, `‖c‖ ≤ r`, `‖e^w − c‖ ≤ r`, `0 < r`, `0 < R` and `‖u‖ = 1`: `‖F w c m / N_m‖ ≤ ‖e^w‖/(r·|Im w|)·((m+1)·(r/R)^(m+1))`.
decls.proves: ‖F w c m / Nn u R m‖ ≤ ‖Complex.exp w‖ / (r * |w.im|) * (((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * (r / R) ^ (m + 1))

decls.name: ordC
decls.why: The order of a zero, as a complex number.

decls.name: wz
decls.why: The exponent of a zero's mode: `w = ρ·log 2`.

decls.name: aSum
decls.why: The segment sum of block N2: `a_k = Σ'_{β≥σ} m(ρ)·J_k(ρ·log 2)`.

decls.name: norm_ordC_mul
decls.why: The order of a zero, as a factor, multiplies the size by the order.

decls.name: re_ord_div_w_pos
decls.why: The weight of a zero's class has positive real part: `Re(m(ρ)/(ρ·log 2)) > 0`.

decls.name: summable_ord_im
decls.why: For `σ > 1/2` the weights `m(ρ)/|Im w_ρ|` of the zeros right of `σ` are summable: `1/|γ| ≤ cim/|ρ|` (`CountReduction.inv_abs_im_le`) and `ZeroSummable.summable_order_div`.
decls.proves: Summable fun ρ : {ρ : NontrivialZeros // σ ≤ (ρ:ℂ).re} => FiniteOffLinePi.ordR ρ.1 / |(wz ρ.1).im|

decls.name: tsum_transform
decls.why: The transform as a sum over the zeros. For `σ > 1/2`: `Σ_{j≤m} C(m,j)·(−c)^(m−j)·a_{j+1} = Σ'_{β≥σ} m(ρ)·F(w_ρ, c, m)`. The finite sum over `j` passes through the sum over the zeros, each `j` summable by `summable_J`.
decls.proves: ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), coefE c m j * aSum σ (j + 1) = ∑' ρ : {ρ : NontrivialZeros // σ ≤ (ρ:ℂ).re}, ordC ρ.1 * F (wz ρ.1) c m

decls.name: term_class
decls.why: A zero of the class. If `e^(w_ρ) = p·u`, `p > 0`, `‖u‖ = 1`, `c = −κu`, `R = p + κ`, then `m(ρ)·F/N_m → m(ρ)/w_ρ`, and every term is at most `K₃·m(ρ)/|Im w_ρ|` for `K₃ ≥ 1 + π`.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => ordC ρ * (F (wz ρ) c m / Nn u R m)) atTop (𝓝 (ordC ρ * (1 / wz ρ))) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, ‖ordC ρ * (F (wz ρ) c m / Nn u R m)‖ ≤ K₃ * (FiniteOffLinePi.ordR ρ / |(wz ρ).im|)

decls.name: term_other
decls.why: A zero off the class. If `‖c‖ ≤ r`, `‖e^(w_ρ) − c‖ ≤ r`, `0 < r < R`, `‖u‖ = 1` and `(m+1)·(r/R)^(m+1) ≤ K` for every `m`, then `m(ρ)·F/N_m → 0`, and every term is at most `K₃·m(ρ)/|Im w_ρ|` for `K₃ ≥ 2K/r`.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => ordC ρ * (F (wz ρ) c m / Nn u R m)) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, ‖ordC ρ * (F (wz ρ) c m / Nn u R m)‖ ≤ K₃ * (FiniteOffLinePi.ordR ρ / |(wz ρ).im|)

decls.name: core
decls.why: The core of block N3-E. Let `σ > 1/2`, `σ ≤ E`, and let the segment sums satisfy `‖a_k‖ ≤ A·k²·2^(kE)` for `k ≥ 2`. Let `ρ₁` have `β₁ > E`, `z₁ = 2^ρ₁`, `u = z₁/|z₁|`, `κ ≥ 0`, and let every other mode of a zero right of `σ` lie within `r₀ < |z₁| + κ` of `−κu`. Then contradiction.

decls.name: euler_exposed_false
decls.why: No mode outside a disc holding the others (block N3-E). Let the count of primes at the doublings stay within `C·k²·√2^k` of `Li`, let `1/2 < σ < Θ ≤ 1`, and let every zero have real part at most `Θ`. Then there is `E` with `σ ≤ E < Θ` such that no zero `ρ₁` with real part above `E` has its mode `z₁ = 2^ρ₁` strictly outside a disc, centred at `−κ·z₁/|z₁|` (`κ ≥ 0`) on the ray opposite to it, of radius `r₀ < |z₁| + κ`, which holds every other mode of the zeros right of `σ`.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → |(Nat.primeCounting ⌊(2:ℝ)^k⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li ((2:ℝ)^k)| ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k
decls.proves: ∃ E : ℝ, σ ≤ E ∧ E < Θ ∧ ∀ (ρ₁ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros), E < (ρ₁:ℂ).re → ∀ κ r₀ : ℝ, 0 ≤ κ → r₀ < ‖(2:ℂ)^(ρ₁:ℂ)‖ + κ → (∀ ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros, σ ≤ (ρ:ℂ).re → (2:ℂ)^(ρ:ℂ) ≠ (2:ℂ)^(ρ₁:ℂ) → ‖(2:ℂ)^(ρ:ℂ) + (κ:ℂ) * ((2:ℂ)^(ρ₁:ℂ) / ‖(2:ℂ)^(ρ₁:ℂ)‖)‖ ≤ r₀) → False

header: CountModes — block N1 of `lean_stage3/design/countmodes.md`, as corrected in its section "After the independent check". 2026-11-23.

decls.name: norm_tail_le
decls.why: On the real interval `(0, 1)` the Euler–Maclaurin tail of `ζ` at `N = 1` is at most `1/(2b)` in size.

decls.name: riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_Ioo
decls.why: `ζ` has no zero on the real interval `(0, 1)`. By the Euler–Maclaurin form at `N = 1`, `ζ(b) = 1/2 − 1/(1 − b) + b·I` with `|b·I| ≤ 1/2`, while `|1/2 − 1/(1 − b)| > 1/2`.

decls.name: im_ne_zero
decls.why: No nontrivial zero of ζ is real. A zero with imaginary part `0` would be a zero of `ζ` on the real interval `(0, 1)`.

decls.name: J
decls.why: The segment integral of one zero on the count's ladder: `J_k(w) = ∫₀^∞ e^(k(w−s))/(w − s) ds`.

decls.name: sub_ofReal_ne_zero
decls.why: For `Im w ≠ 0`, the point `w − s` is never zero for real `s`.

decls.name: continuous_integrand
decls.why: For `Im w ≠ 0`, the integrand of `J k w` is continuous in `s`.
decls.proves: Continuous (fun s : ℝ => Complex.exp ((k:ℂ) * (w - s)) / (w - s))

decls.name: norm_integrand_le
decls.why: The size of the integrand of `J k w`: at most `e^(k·Re w)/|Im w|·e^(−ks)`.
decls.proves: ‖Complex.exp ((k:ℂ) * (w - s)) / (w - s)‖ ≤ Real.exp (k * w.re) / |w.im| * Real.exp (-k * s)

decls.name: integral_exp_neg_mul
decls.why: The real exponential `e^(−ks)` integrates to `1/k` over `s > 0`.
decls.proves: ∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), Real.exp (-k * s) = 1 / k

decls.name: integrable_J
decls.why: For `1 ≤ k` and `Im w ≠ 0` the integrand of `J k w` is integrable on `s > 0`.
decls.proves: IntegrableOn (fun s : ℝ => Complex.exp ((k:ℂ) * (w - s)) / (w - s)) (Set.Ioi 0)

decls.name: norm_J_le
decls.why: The size of the segment integral. For `1 ≤ k` and `Im w ≠ 0`, `‖J k w‖ ≤ e^(k·Re w)/(k·|Im w|)`.

decls.name: integrand_sub
decls.why: For `s` real and `Im w ≠ 0`, the difference of the integrands of `J k w` and `J 1 w` at `s` is `∫₁ᵏ e^((w−s)v) dv`.
decls.proves: Complex.exp ((k:ℂ) * (w - s)) / (w - s) - Complex.exp (((1:ℕ):ℂ) * (w - s)) / (w - s) = ∫ v in (1:ℝ)..(k:ℝ), Complex.exp ((w - s) * v)

decls.name: integral_inner
decls.why: For `v > 0`, `∫₀^∞ e^((w−s)v) ds = e^(vw)/v`.
decls.proves: ∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), Complex.exp ((w - s) * v) = Complex.exp ((v:ℂ) * w) / (v:ℂ)

decls.name: integrable_prod
decls.why: For `1 ≤ k`, the function `(s, v) ↦ e^((w−s)v)` is integrable on `(0, ∞) × (1, k]`.
decls.proves: Integrable (Function.uncurry fun (s v : ℝ) => Complex.exp ((w - s) * v)) ((volume.restrict (Set.Ioi (0:ℝ))).prod (volume.restrict (Set.Ioc (1:ℝ) k)))

decls.name: J_sub
decls.why: The difference of two segment integrals. For `1 ≤ k` and `Im w ≠ 0`, `J k w − J 1 w = ∫₁ᵏ e^(vw)/v dv`. By Fubini: the difference of the integrands is `∫₁ᵏ e^((w−s)v) dv`, and `∫₀^∞ e^((w−s)v) ds = e^(vw)/v`.
decls.proves: J k w - J 1 w = ∫ v in (1:ℝ)..(k:ℝ), Complex.exp ((v:ℂ) * w) / (v:ℂ)

decls.name: cpow_two_rpow
decls.why: The complex power `ρ` of the real `2^v` is `e^(v·ρ·log 2)`.
decls.proves: (((2:ℝ) ^ v : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ ρ = Complex.exp ((v:ℂ) * (ρ * (Real.log 2 : ℂ)))

decls.name: term1_eq
decls.why: The first term of `piMode ρ (2^v)` is `e^(vw)/(vw)`, with `w = ρ·log 2`.
decls.proves: (((2:ℝ) ^ v : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ ρ / ρ / (Real.log ((2:ℝ) ^ v) : ℂ) = Complex.exp ((v:ℂ) * (ρ * (Real.log 2 : ℂ))) / ((v:ℂ) * (ρ * (Real.log 2 : ℂ)))

decls.name: continuousOn_integrand
decls.why: The integrand of `piMode` is continuous on `t > 1`.
decls.proves: ContinuousOn (fun t : ℝ => (t : ℂ) ^ ρ / ρ * PiZeros.wt t) (Set.Ioi 1)

decls.name: hasDerivAt_ipart
decls.why: The derivative of the integral part of `piMode ρ` at `y > 1` is the integrand.
decls.proves: HasDerivAt (fun u => ∫ t in (2:ℝ)..u, (t : ℂ) ^ ρ / ρ * PiZeros.wt t) ((y : ℂ) ^ ρ / ρ * PiZeros.wt y) y

decls.name: hasDerivAt_term1
decls.why: The derivative of `e^(uw)/(uw)` at `u ≠ 0`, for `w ≠ 0`.
decls.proves: HasDerivAt (fun u : ℝ => Complex.exp ((u:ℂ) * w) / ((u:ℂ) * w)) ((Complex.exp ((v:ℂ) * w) * w * ((v:ℂ) * w) - Complex.exp ((v:ℂ) * w) * w) / ((v:ℂ) * w) ^ 2) v

decls.name: hasDerivAt_piMode_two_rpow
decls.why: The derivative of one zero's part along the doublings. For `v > 0` and `ρ ≠ 0`, `v ↦ piMode ρ (2^v)` has derivative `e^(vw)/v`, `w = ρ·log 2`.
decls.proves: HasDerivAt (fun u : ℝ => PiZeros.piMode ρ ((2:ℝ) ^ u)) (Complex.exp ((v:ℂ) * (ρ * (Real.log 2 : ℂ))) / (v:ℂ)) v

decls.name: piMode_doubling_sub_of
decls.why: One zero's part of the count between two doublings. For `ρ ≠ 0` and `1 ≤ k`, `piMode ρ (2^k) − piMode ρ 2 = ∫₁ᵏ e^(vw)/v dv`, `w = ρ·log 2`.
decls.proves: PiZeros.piMode ρ ((2:ℝ) ^ k) - PiZeros.piMode ρ 2 = ∫ v in (1:ℝ)..(k:ℝ), Complex.exp ((v:ℂ) * (ρ * Real.log 2)) / (v:ℂ)

decls.name: piMode_doubling_sub
decls.why: One zero's part of the count between two doublings, for a nontrivial zero: `piMode ρ (2^k) − piMode ρ 2 = ∫₁ᵏ e^(vw)/v dv`, `w = ρ·log 2`.
decls.proves: PiZeros.piMode (ρ:ℂ) ((2:ℝ) ^ k) - PiZeros.piMode (ρ:ℂ) 2 = ∫ v in (1:ℝ)..(k:ℝ), Complex.exp ((v:ℂ) * ((ρ:ℂ) * Real.log 2)) / (v:ℂ)

decls.name: im_w
decls.why: The imaginary part of `w = ρ·log 2` is `γ·log 2`.

decls.name: re_w
decls.why: The real part of `w = ρ·log 2` is `β·log 2`.

decls.name: w_im_ne_zero
decls.why: For a nontrivial zero, `w = ρ·log 2` is not real.

decls.name: cst
decls.why: The constant of one zero's part on the count's ladder: `piMode ρ 2 − J_1(w)`.

decls.name: piMode_doubling
decls.why: One zero's part on the count's ladder is a segment plus a constant. For a nontrivial zero and `1 ≤ k`, `piMode ρ (2^k) = J_k(ρ·log 2) + cst ρ`.
decls.proves: PiZeros.piMode (ρ:ℂ) ((2:ℝ)^k) = J k ((ρ:ℂ) * Real.log 2) + cst ρ

decls.name: norm_J_doubling_le
decls.why: The size of a zero's segment on the count's ladder. For `1 ≤ k`, `‖J_k(ρ·log 2)‖ ≤ 2^(kβ)/(k·|γ|·log 2)`.

decls.name: norm_piMode_two_le
decls.why: The value of one zero's part at `2`: `‖piMode ρ 2‖ ≤ 2/(|γ|·log 2)`.

decls.name: norm_cst_le
decls.why: The size of the constant. `‖cst ρ‖ ≤ 4/(|γ|·log 2)`: each of `piMode ρ 2` and `J_1(ρ·log 2)` is at most `2^β/(|γ|·log 2) ≤ 2/(|γ|·log 2)`.

decls.name: J_eq_segment
decls.why: The segment form. `J_k(w) = ∫₀^∞ (e^w·e^(−s))^k/(w − s) ds`: the integrand is the pure mode `z·e^(−s)`, `z = e^w`, raised to the `k`-th power, with density `1/(w − s)`. It holds for every `k` and `w`.
decls.proves: J k w = ∫ s in Set.Ioi (0:ℝ), (Complex.exp w * Real.exp (-s)) ^ k / (w - s)

header: CountReduction — block N2 of `lean_stage3/design/countmodes.md`, as corrected in its section "After the independent check". 2026-11-23.

decls.name: cim
decls.why: A constant bounding `|ρ|/|γ|` over every nontrivial zero: `2` plus the sum of `|ρ|/|γ|` over the finitely many zeros of height below one.

decls.name: two_le_cim
decls.why: The constant `cim` is at least `2`.

decls.name: inv_abs_im_le
decls.why: The height of a zero against its size. For every nontrivial zero, `1/|γ| ≤ cim/|ρ|`. Above height one `|ρ| ≤ 1 + |γ| ≤ 2|γ|`; below it there are finitely many zeros.

decls.name: ratio_pow
decls.why: The shell ratio as a power: `(2^θ'/2)^k = 2^(−k(1−θ'))`.

decls.name: sum_tail_le
decls.why: For `0 ≤ r < 1`, a finite sum of `(j + 1)·r^j` over indices `j ≥ k` is at most `(k + 1)·r^k·S`, with `S = Σ' (i + 1)·r^i`: shift every index down by `k`.

decls.name: tail_rate
decls.why: The rate of the tail. For `1/2 < σ ≤ 1` there are `0 ≤ θ' < 1` and `Ct ≥ 0` such that, for every `k ≥ 1`, the weights `m(ρ)/|ρ|` over any finite set of zeros with `Re ρ ≥ σ` and `|Im ρ| ≥ 2^k` sum to at most `Ct·k·2^(−k(1−θ'))`. decls.name: summable_J
decls.why: The segment terms right of a line are absolutely summable. For `σ > 1/2` and `k ≥ 1`, `‖m(ρ)·J_k(ρ·log 2)‖ ≤ cim·2^k/(k·log 2)·m(ρ)/|ρ|`, and these weights are summable (`ZeroSummable.summable_order_div`).

Let the count of primes at the doublings stay within `C·k²·√2^k` of `Li`, let `1/2 < σ < Θ ≤ 1`, and let every zero have real part at most `Θ`. decls.proves: ∃ E A : ℝ, σ ≤ E ∧ E < Θ ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ‖∑' ρ : {ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros // σ ≤ (ρ:ℂ).re}, ((riemannZeta.order ((ρ:Kadiri.NontrivialZeros):ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * CountModes.J k (((ρ:Kadiri.NontrivialZeros):ℂ) * Real.log 2)‖ ≤ A * (k:ℝ)^2 * (2:ℝ)^((k:ℝ) * E)

decls.why: For `n ≥ 1`, the power `n^{-it}` is the exponential `exp(i·(−log n)·t)`.

decls.proves: ((∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖∑ n ∈ Icc 1 N, a n * (n : ℂ) ^ (-(Complex.I * (t : ℂ)))‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) = ∑ m ∈ Icc 1 N, ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 N, a m * (starRingEnd ℂ) (a n) * ∫ t in T₁..T₂, Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((Real.log n - Real.log m : ℝ) : ℂ) * t)

decls.name: norm_integral_exp_le
decls.why: For a nonzero real frequency `θ`, the integral of `e^{iθt}` over any window has norm at most `2/|θ|`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in T₁..T₂, Complex.exp (Complex.I * (θ : ℂ) * t)‖ ≤ 2 / |θ|

decls.name: log_gap
decls.why: For `1 ≤ n < m ≤ N`, the gap between the logarithms is at least `(m − n)/N`.
decls.proves: ((m : ℝ) - n) / N ≤ Real.log m - Real.log n

decls.name: inv_log_gap
decls.why: For distinct `m, n` in `[1, N]`, `2/|log n − log m|` is at most `2N/|m − n|`.
decls.proves: 2 / |Real.log n - Real.log m| ≤ 2 * N * |(m : ℝ) - n|⁻¹

decls.name: sum_inv_le_harmonic
decls.why: A sum of `1/g(n)` over a set on which `g` is injective with values in `[1, N]` is at most the harmonic sum up to `N`.
needs: hmap : ∀ n ∈ s, g n ∈ Icc 1 N
decls.proves: ∑ n ∈ s, ((g n : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 N, (k : ℝ)⁻¹

decls.name: sum_inv_Icc_le
decls.why: The harmonic sum `Σ_{k=1}^{N} 1/k` is at most `1 + log N`.
decls.proves: ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 N, (k : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ 1 + Real.log N

decls.name: sum_inv_dist_le
decls.why: For `m` in `[1, N]`, the sum of `1/|m − n|` over the other `n` in `[1, N]` is at most `2(1 + log N)`.
decls.proves: ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 N, (if m = n then 0 else |(m : ℝ) - n|⁻¹) ≤ 2 * (1 + Real.log N)

decls.name: sum_mul_mul_le
decls.why: For a symmetric nonnegative kernel `K` whose rows sum to at most `R`, the quadratic form `Σ_m Σ_n A_m A_n K_{mn}` is at most `R · Σ A_m²`.
needs: hK0 : ∀ m ∈ s, ∀ n ∈ s, 0 ≤ K m n
hsym : ∀ m n, K m n = K n m
hrow : ∀ m ∈ s, ∑ n ∈ s, K m n ≤ R
decls.proves: ∑ m ∈ s, ∑ n ∈ s, A m * A n * K m n ≤ R * ∑ m ∈ s, A m ^ 2

decls.name: dirichlet_mean_value_window
decls.why: On a window `[T₁, T₂]`, the mean square of a finite Dirichlet sum `Σ_{n ≤ N} a_n n^{-it}` is at most `(T₂ − T₁ + 8N(1 + log N))·Σ |a_n|²`.
decls.proves: ∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, a n * (n : ℂ) ^ (-(Complex.I * (t : ℂ)))‖ ^ 2 ≤ (T₂ - T₁ + 8 * N * (1 + Real.log N)) * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ‖a n‖ ^ 2

decls.name: dirichlet_mean_value
decls.why: On `[0, T]`, the mean square of a finite Dirichlet sum `Σ_{n ≤ N} a_n n^{-it}` is at most `(T + 8N(1 + log N))·Σ |a_n|²`.
decls.proves: ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..T, ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, a n * (n : ℂ) ^ (-(Complex.I * (t : ℂ)))‖ ^ 2 ≤ (T + 8 * N * (1 + Real.log N)) * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ‖a n‖ ^ 2

decls.name: dirichlet_mean_value_sigma
decls.why: With a real part `σ`, the mean square on `[0, T]` of `Σ_{n ≤ N} a_n n^{-(σ+it)}` is at most `(T + 8N(1 + log N))·Σ |a_n|²·n^{-2σ}`.
decls.proves: ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..T, ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, a n * (n : ℂ) ^ (-((σ : ℂ) + Complex.I * (t : ℂ)))‖ ^ 2 ≤ (T + 8 * N * (1 + Real.log N)) * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ‖a n‖ ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) ^ (-2 * σ)

header: DirichletMeanW — block C1b of `lean_stage3/design/carlson.md`. 2026-11-23. A weighted mean value theorem for a finite Dirichlet sum. It replaces the uniform length `N` of block C1 by each term's own index: for `S(t) = Σ_{n ≤ N} a_n n^{-it}` the integral of `|S|²` over a window of length `L` is at most `Σ |a_n|²·(L + 6n(1 + log N))`. The square expands into a double sum as in `DirichletMean`. Off the diagonal the kernel is at most `2/|log m − log n|`. A weighted Schur test with weights `1/n` charges row `m` the cost…

decls.name: log_gap_larger
decls.why: For `1 ≤ p < q`, the gap between the logarithms is at least `(q − p)/q`, with the larger index in the denominator.
decls.proves: ((q : ℝ) - p) / q ≤ Real.log q - Real.log p

decls.name: weighted_gap
decls.why: For distinct `m, n ≥ 1`, the off-diagonal kernel bound `2/|log n − log m|` times the weight ratio `m/n` is at most `2m(1/|m − n| + 1/n)`.
decls.proves: 2 / |Real.log n - Real.log m| * ((m : ℝ) / n) ≤ 2 * m * (|(m : ℝ) - n|⁻¹ + (n : ℝ)⁻¹)

decls.name: sum_mul_mul_le_weighted
decls.why: Weighted Schur test: for a symmetric nonnegative kernel `K` and positive weights `w`, the quadratic form `Σ_m Σ_n A_m A_n K_{mn}` is at most `Σ_m A_m²·R_m` whenever each weighted row `Σ_n K_{mn}·(w_m/w_n)` is at most `R_m`.
needs: hK0 : ∀ m ∈ s, ∀ n ∈ s, 0 ≤ K m n
hsym : ∀ m n, K m n = K n m
hrow : ∀ m ∈ s, ∑ n ∈ s, K m n * (w m / w n) ≤ R m
decls.proves: ∑ m ∈ s, ∑ n ∈ s, A m * A n * K m n ≤ ∑ m ∈ s, A m ^ 2 * R m

decls.name: dirichlet_mean_value_weighted
decls.why: On a window `[T₁, T₂]`, the mean square of a finite Dirichlet sum `Σ_{n ≤ N} a_n n^{-it}` is at most `Σ |a_n|²·(T₂ − T₁ + 6n(1 + log N))`, each term charged its own index `n`.
decls.proves: ∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, a n * (n : ℂ) ^ (-(Complex.I * (t : ℂ)))‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ‖a n‖ ^ 2 * ((T₂ - T₁) + 6 * n * (1 + Real.log N))

decls.name: dirichlet_mean_value_weighted_sigma
decls.why: With a real part `σ`, the mean square on `[T₁, T₂]` of `Σ_{n ≤ N} a_n n^{-(σ+it)}` is at most `Σ |a_n|²·n^{-2σ}·(T₂ − T₁ + 6n(1 + log N))`, each term charged its own index `n`.
decls.proves: ∫ t in T₁..T₂, ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, a n * (n : ℂ) ^ (-((σ : ℂ) + Complex.I * (t : ℂ)))‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ‖a n‖ ^ 2 * (n : ℝ) ^ (-2 * σ) * ((T₂ - T₁) + 6 * n * (1 + Real.log N))

header: Doubling — block R15 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`. 2026-11-24. The self-bound at `N` less twice the self-bound at `⌊N/2⌋`. The even scales `N/(2j)` are the scales of `⌊N/2⌋`, so the difference keeps the odd scales and subtracts the even ones: an alternating sum of the staircase, equal to `log N! − 2·log ⌊N/2⌋!`. By Stirling that is `N log 2` up to `O(log N)`, and the alternating sum of `N/k` is `N log 2` up to `N` times the tail of the alternating harmonic series, at most `1`. The alternating residuals add up to…

decls.name: neg_one_pow_succ_eq
decls.why: The sign `(−1)^(k+1)` read off the parity of `k`.

decls.name: alt_scales
decls.why: The doubling. The self-bound at `N` less twice the self-bound at `⌊N/2⌋` is the alternating sum of the staircase over the scales `N/k`.
decls.proves: ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 N, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * Chebyshev.psi ((N : ℝ) / (k : ℝ)) = ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 N, Real.log n - 2 * ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 (N / 2), Real.log n

decls.name: log_step
decls.why: One step of the logarithm against `1/x`.
decls.proves: 1 / (x + 1) ≤ Real.log (x + 1) - Real.log x ∧ Real.log (x + 1) - Real.log x ≤ 1 / x

decls.name: harmonic_block
decls.why: The harmonic sum from `n+1` to `n+k` against `log((n+k)/n)`.
decls.proves: Real.log ((n + k : ℕ) : ℝ) - Real.log (n : ℝ) - (1 / (n : ℝ) - 1 / ((n + k : ℕ) : ℝ)) ≤ ∑ i ∈ Icc 1 (n + k), 1 / (i : ℝ) - ∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 / (i : ℝ) ∧ ∑ i ∈ Icc 1 (n + k), 1 / (i : ℝ) - ∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 / (i : ℝ) ≤ Real.log ((n + k : ℕ) : ℝ) - Real.log (n : ℝ)

decls.name: alt_even
decls.why: The alternating sum up to `2m` is the harmonic sum from `m+1` to `2m`.

decls.name: alt_even_bound
decls.why: The alternating sum up to `2m` lies within `1/(2m)` below `log 2`.

decls.name: alt_harmonic
decls.why: The alternating harmonic sum. Within `1/N` of `log 2`.

decls.name: doubling_smooth
decls.why: The smooth parts of the two log-sums against `N log 2`.
decls.proves: |(N : ℝ) * Real.log N - N - 2 * ((M : ℝ) * Real.log M - M) - N * Real.log 2| ≤ Real.log N + 1

decls.name: alt_resid_small
decls.why: The alternating residuals are small. Over the scales `N/k` with the signs `(−1)^(k+1)`, the residuals of the staircase add up to at most `4 log N + 5`.
decls.proves: |∑ k ∈ Icc 1 N, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * (Chebyshev.psi ((N : ℝ) / (k : ℝ)) - (N : ℝ) / (k : ℝ))| ≤ 4 * Real.log N + 5

header: # S3 — the edge bound (FinalBound rescale + gap-eating) The Landau partial fraction transported from PNT+'s normalized `FinalBound` (unit ball) to the ball at `3/2 + iT′`, for `g = (s−1)²·ζ` (entire; the pole cleared, one extra order-1 zero at `1`). Inputs: `ZetaGrowth.sq_zeta_band_bound` (the B), PNT+'s `ZetaFixedLowerBound` (the f(0)), `ContourShift`'s good heights, fences, and reflection-order (the eating).

decls.name: c0
decls.why: The ball center at height `T′`.

decls.name: gz
decls.why: `g = (s−1)²·ζ` — entire, zeros = ζ-zeros plus an order-1 zero at 1.

decls.name: gz_analytic
decls.why: The function `gz = (s−1)²·ζ` is analytic at every complex point `s`.

decls.name: c0_im
decls.why: The imaginary part of the ball center `c0 T'` is `T'`.

decls.name: c0_re
decls.why: The real part of the ball center `c0 T'` is `3/2`.

decls.name: gz_lower
decls.why: The explicit lower bound at the center.

decls.name: zeta_ratio_pos
decls.why: The lower-bound constant is positive.

decls.name: gz_c0_ne
decls.why: The center's value is nonzero.

decls.name: gz_zero_cases
decls.why: A `gz`-zero is `1` or a `ζ`-zero.

decls.name: gz_zeros_ball_finite
decls.why: The `gz`-zeros in any ball around the center are finite.
decls.proves: {w : ℂ | gz w = 0 ∧ ‖w - c0 T'‖ ≤ ρ}.Finite

decls.name: gz_partial_fraction
decls.why: The rescaled Landau partial fraction. At any height `T′ ≥ 2` and any `u` on the segment `re ∈ [−1/4, 2]` at that height that is not a `gz`-zero, the log-derivative of `gz` minus the simple-pole sum over `gz`-zeros within `46/25` of the center is `≤ C·log T′`. Transported from PNT+'s normalized `FinalBound` with radii `22/25 < 23/25 < 19/20 < 49/50`.
decls.proves: ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ T' : ℝ, 2 ≤ T' → ∀ u : ℂ, u.im = T' → -1/4 ≤ u.re → u.re ≤ 2 → gz u ≠ 0 → ‖deriv gz u / gz u - ∑ w ∈ (gz_zeros_ball_finite T' (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 46/25)).toFinset, (analyticOrderNatAt gz w : ℂ) / (u - w)‖ ≤ C * Real.log T'

decls.name: gz_order_eq
decls.why: Away from `1`, the order of `gz` is the order of `ζ` — the factor `(s−1)²` carries order zero there.
decls.proves: analyticOrderNatAt gz w = analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta w

decls.name: ball_zero_shape
decls.why: Every ball zero at heights `≥ 2` is a `ζ`-zero on the open strip, with ordinate within `46/25` of `T′`.

decls.name: ball_order_sum_le
decls.why: The ball order-count: the total multiplicity of `gz`-zeros in the `46/25`-ball at height `T′` is `≤ C·log T′` — four Jensen windows for `T′ ≥ 4` with the reflection charging left-zeros to partners, and a fixed-rectangle constant for `T′ < 4`.
decls.proves: ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ T' : ℝ, 2 ≤ T' → (∑ w ∈ (gz_zeros_ball_finite T' (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 46/25)).toFinset, (analyticOrderNatAt gz w : ℝ)) ≤ C * Real.log T'

decls.name: gz_logderiv
decls.why: The log-derivative identity: `gz′/gz = 2/(s−1) + ζ′/ζ` away from the pole and the zeros.
decls.proves: deriv gz u / gz u = 2/(u - 1) + deriv riemannZeta u / riemannZeta u

decls.name: deriv_zeta_conj
decls.why: Conjugation transfers the derivative of `ζ`.
decls.proves: deriv riemannZeta ((starRingEnd ℂ) s) = (starRingEnd ℂ) (deriv riemannZeta s)

decls.name: edge_bound_core
decls.why: The pointwise edge bound, unified. For `u` on the band `re ∈ [−1/4, 2]` at height `t ≥ 2`, with a lower bound `δ ≤ 1` on the distance from `u` to every ball zero: `‖ζ′/ζ(u)‖ ≤ C·(log t)/δ + C·log t`. Both edges specialize this: the left edge with `δ = 1/4`, the good horizontals with `δ = zeroGap T`.
decls.proves: ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, 2 ≤ t → ∀ u : ℂ, u.im = t → -1/4 ≤ u.re → u.re ≤ 2 → riemannZeta u ≠ 0 → ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → δ ≤ 1 → (∀ w ∈ (gz_zeros_ball_finite t (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 46/25)).toFinset, δ ≤ ‖u - w‖) → ‖deriv riemannZeta u / riemannZeta u‖ ≤ C * Real.log t / δ

header: EdgeNum — block E8a of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. `EdgeBound`'s three edge theorems with their constants as definitions. Each proof is the original with its existence step replaced: the band bound is `BoxBounds.sq_zeta_band_explicit` in place of `sq_zeta_band_bound`, and each `refine ⟨<expression>, _, ?_⟩` is the definition unfolding to that expression (`LOOP.md` § 3). `EdgeBound.lean` is untouched.

decls.why: The partial fraction's constant.

decls.name: C1n_pos
decls.why: The partial fraction's constant `C1n` is positive.

decls.name: gz_partial_fraction_num

At any height `T′ ≥ 2` and any `u` on the segment `re ∈ [−1/4, 2]` at that height that is not a `gz`-zero, the log-derivative of `gz` minus the simple-pole sum over `gz`-zeros within `46/25` of the center is `≤ C·log T′`. Transported from PNT+'s normalized `FinalBound` with radii `22/25 < 23/25 < 19/20 < 49/50`.
decls.proves: ∀ T' : ℝ, 2 ≤ T' → ∀ u : ℂ, u.im = T' → -1/4 ≤ u.re → u.re ≤ 2 → gz u ≠ 0 → ‖deriv gz u / gz u - ∑ w ∈ (gz_zeros_ball_finite T' (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 46/25)).toFinset, (analyticOrderNatAt gz w : ℂ) / (u - w)‖ ≤ C1n * Real.log T'

decls.name: C2n
decls.why: The ball count's constant.

decls.name: C2n_pos
decls.why: The ball count's constant `C2n` is positive.

decls.name: ball_order_sum_le_num
decls.why: The ball order-count: the total multiplicity of `gz`-zeros in the `46/25`-ball at height `T′` is `≤ C·log T′` — four Jensen windows for `T′ ≥ 4` with the reflection charging left-zeros to partners, and a fixed-rectangle constant for `T′ < 4`.
decls.proves: ∀ T' : ℝ, 2 ≤ T' → (∑ w ∈ (gz_zeros_ball_finite T' (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 46/25)).toFinset, (analyticOrderNatAt gz w : ℝ)) ≤ C2n * Real.log T'

decls.name: Cen
decls.why: The edge constant.

decls.name: Cen_pos
decls.why: The edge constant `Cen` is positive.

decls.name: edge_bound_core_num
decls.why: The pointwise edge bound, unified. For `u` on the band `re ∈ [−1/4, 2]` at height `t ≥ 2`, with a lower bound `δ ≤ 1` on the distance from `u` to every ball zero: `‖ζ′/ζ(u)‖ ≤ C·(log t)/δ + C·log t`. Both edges specialize this: the left edge with `δ = 1/4`, the good horizontals with `δ = zeroGap T`.
decls.proves: ∀ t : ℝ, 2 ≤ t → ∀ u : ℂ, u.im = t → -1/4 ≤ u.re → u.re ≤ 2 → riemannZeta u ≠ 0 → ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → δ ≤ 1 → (∀ w ∈ (gz_zeros_ball_finite t (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 46/25)).toFinset, δ ≤ ‖u - w‖) → ‖deriv riemannZeta u / riemannZeta u‖ ≤ Cen * Real.log t / δ

header: ExplicitBump — a concrete `ν`, so `mellin_bump_bounded`'s `B` is a numeral. WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `RHPull.psi_weak_of_RH` (`Stage3/LineBound.lean:2357`) assembles its constant from four distinct existentials:

decls.name: sqPos_eq
decls.why: `(max 0 u)²` written without the max, for differentiation.
decls.proves: (max 0 u) ^ 2 = if u ≤ 0 then 0 else u ^ 2

decls.name: hasDerivAt_sqPos
decls.why: The derivative of `(max 0 ·)²` is `2·max 0 ·`, everywhere — including at the join, where both one-sided derivatives vanish.
decls.proves: HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => (max 0 t) ^ 2) (2 * max 0 u) u

decls.name: contDiff_sqPos
decls.why: The squared positive part `t ↦ (max 0 t)²` is continuously differentiable.

decls.name: bumpP
decls.why: The interval polynomial: `p x = (x − 1/2)(2 − x)`, positive exactly on `Ioo (1/2) 2`.

decls.name: bumpC
decls.why: The normalising constant `c = 1 / ∫_{1/2}^{2} p²/x`, in closed form. `∫ p²/x = 33/16 − (3/2)·log 2`.

decls.name: bump
decls.why: The explicit bump. `C¹`, supported exactly on `Icc (1/2) 2`, non-negative, and normalised so `∫ ν(x)/x dx = 1`.

decls.name: bumpP_nonpos_of_le
decls.why: Helper: for `x ≤ 1/2`, the interval polynomial satisfies `bumpP x ≤ 0`.

decls.name: bumpP_nonpos_of_ge
decls.why: Helper: for `x ≥ 2`, the interval polynomial satisfies `bumpP x ≤ 0`.

decls.name: bumpC_pos
decls.why: `∫ p²/x` is positive, so `bumpC` is well defined and positive.

decls.name: bump_nonneg
decls.why: The explicit bump is non-negative at every real `x`.

decls.name: bump_support
decls.why: Support. Off `Icc (1/2) 2` the polynomial is non-positive, so the positive part is zero.

decls.name: bump_contDiff
decls.why: `C¹`. The polynomial is smooth and the positive-part square is `C¹`, so the composite is.

decls.name: bumpP_le
decls.why: `p` peaks at `x = 5/4` with value `9/16`.

decls.name: bump_le
decls.why: The sup of the bump, at the peak: `sup ν = c·(9/16)²`.

decls.name: bump_le_numeral
decls.why: The numeral. `sup ν ≤ 1.4757`, hence `mellin_bump_bounded`'s `B = 3·sup‖ν‖ + 1 ≤ 5.4271`. Both bounds are decimal, so a consumer can carry them arithmetically.

header: ExplicitLeft — block F1 of `lean_stage3/design/leftedge.md`. 2026-11-23. The truncated explicit formula at every height `T ≥ 2`, with no cap `T ≤ x²`. `Glue.explicit_formula_split_num` used the cap once, to bound the left edge `VIntegral (Gf x) (-1/4) (-T') T'` by `log²x`. Here the left edge is kept as a term, and bounded separately by `log²T'`. The bound grows with the height: an absolute value on the line `Re s = −1/4` loses `log²T'` (the lost factor of the design note). Block F2 removes it.

decls.name: Aleft
decls.why: The left-edge constant at every height: eight times `Glue.Dln`.

decls.name: Aleft_pos
decls.why: The left-edge constant `Aleft` is positive.

decls.name: explicit_formula_left
decls.why: The explicit formula with the left edge kept. For `16 ≤ x` and `2 ≤ T` there is a height `T′` in `[T, T+1]` with `‖ψ(x) − x + Σ_{|γ|<T} m·x^ρ/ρ‖ ≤ c1n·x·log²(xT)/T + c3n·log x + ‖left edge at T′‖`. `Glue.explicit_formula_split_num`'s proof with the left edge left unbounded; no cap on `T`.
