decls.name: edge_left_any
decls.why: The left edge at any height. For `16 ≤ x` and `2 ≤ T′`, the integral of `−ζ′/ζ(s)·x^s/s` up `Re s = −1/4` from `−T′` to `T′` has norm at most `Aleft·log²T′·x^(−1/4)`. `Glue.edge_left_sharp_num`'s proof with `log T′` kept.

decls.name: explicit_formula_any
decls.why: The truncated explicit formula at every height. For `16 ≤ x` and `2 ≤ T`, `‖ψ(x) − x + Σ_{|γ|<T} m·x^ρ/ρ‖ ≤ c1n·x·log²(xT)/T + c3n·log x + Aleft·log²(T+1)·x^(−1/4)`. No cap on `T`; the last term grows with `T`.
decls.proves: ‖(Chebyshev.psi x : ℂ) - (x:ℂ) + Stage3.zeroPartialSum x T‖ ≤ Glue.c1n * x * Real.log (x*T)^2 / T + Glue.c3n * Real.log x + Aleft * (Real.log (T+1))^2 * x ^ (-(1:ℝ)/4)

header: ExplicitTwo — block G2 of `lean_stage3/design/floor.md`. 2026-11-23. `LeftSmooth.explicit_formula_all` with the floor lowered from `16 ≤ x` to `2 ≤ x`, as a parallel chain. Perron's formula comes from block G1 (`PerronTwo.explicit_formula_perron_two`). Every `x`-free lemma is reused unchanged; the lemmas below are copies of the originals with the lines that used the floor rewritten. No proved file is edited.

decls.name: residue_identity_two
decls.why: The residue identity from `x > 1`. `ContourShift.residue_identity` with the hypothesis `16 ≤ x` lowered to `1 < x`: on the good rectangle from `−1/4 − iT′` to `1 + 1/log x + iT′`, the normalized contour integral of `−ζ′/ζ(s)·x^s/s` is `x − ζ′/ζ(0) − Σ_{|γ|<T′} m·x^ρ/ρ`. The proof is the original's; only the derivations of `0 < x` and `0 < log x` change.
needs: hgood : ∀ ρ : ℂ, riemannZeta ρ = 0 → 0 < ρ.re → zeroGap T ≤ |ρ.im - T'|
decls.proves: RectangleIntegral' (fun s : ℂ ↦ (- deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s) * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ s / s) (((-1/4 : ℝ):ℂ) - Complex.I * T') (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * T') = (x : ℂ) - deriv riemannZeta 0 / riemannZeta 0 - Stage3.zeroPartialSum x T'

decls.name: zeroPartialSum_swap_two
decls.why: The swap from `x ≥ 1`. `Glue.zeroPartialSum_swap_num` with `16 ≤ x` lowered to `1 ≤ x`: moving the zero sum from a height `T′ ∈ [T, T+1]` back to `T` costs at most `Csn·x·log T/T`.
decls.proves: ∀ x T T' : ℝ, 1 ≤ x → 2 ≤ T → T ≤ T' → T' ≤ T + 1 → ‖Stage3.zeroPartialSum x T' - Stage3.zeroPartialSum x T‖ ≤ Glue.Csn * x * Real.log T / T

decls.name: logDeriv_re_ge_two
decls.why: The absolute bound right of `Re = 2`. For `2 ≤ Re u`, `‖ζ′/ζ(u)‖ ≤ 6`, from `Slice5.norm_logDerivZeta_of_one_lt_re` (`≤ 2/(σ−1) + 4/(σ−1)²`, RH-free).

decls.name: Cpn_ge
decls.why: The good-height constant is at least `360`: `Cpn = Cen·2·(180 + 1060/log 2)` with `Cen = C1n + C2n + 1/log 2 ≥ 1`.

decls.name: logDeriv_good_ext
decls.why: The good-height bound on the wider band. `Glue.zeta_logderiv_good_bound_num` extended from `−1/4 ≤ Re u ≤ 2` to `−1/4 ≤ Re u ≤ 5/2`, same constant `Cpn`: below `Re u = 2` it is the original; above, `‖ζ′/ζ(u)‖ ≤ 6 ≤ 360·log²2 ≤ Cpn·log²T`.
decls.proves: ∀ T T' : ℝ, 2 ≤ T → T' ∈ Set.Icc T (T+1) → (∀ ρ : ℂ, riemannZeta ρ = 0 → 0 < ρ.re → ContourShift.zeroGap T ≤ |ρ.im - T'|) → ∀ u : ℂ, |u.im| = T' → -1/4 ≤ u.re → u.re ≤ 5/2 → ‖deriv riemannZeta u / riemannZeta u‖ ≤ Glue.Cpn * Real.log T ^ 2

decls.name: Cht
decls.why: The horizontal-edge constant from `x = 2`: `Cpn·3·(11/4)`. The edge runs from `−1/4` to `c ≤ 5/2`, length at most `11/4`.

decls.name: Cht_pos
decls.why: The horizontal-edge constant `Cht` is positive.

decls.name: edge_horizontal_bound_two
decls.why: The horizontal-edge integral bound from `x = 2`. `Glue.edge_horizontal_bound_num` for `2 ≤ x`: at a good height, both signs, the integral of `−ζ′/ζ(s)·x^s/s` along `Im s = y`, `|y| = T′`, from `−1/4` to `1 + 1/log x`, has norm at most `Cht·x·log²T/T`. The abscissa is now `≤ 5/2`, the good bound is `logDeriv_good_ext`, and the edge length is `≤ 11/4`.
decls.proves: ∀ x T T' : ℝ, 2 ≤ x → 2 ≤ T → T' ∈ Set.Icc T (T+1) → (∀ ρ : ℂ, riemannZeta ρ = 0 → 0 < ρ.re → ContourShift.zeroGap T ≤ |ρ.im - T'|) → ∀ y : ℝ, |y| = T' → ‖HIntegral (Glue.Gf x) (-1/4) (1 + 1/Real.log x) y‖ ≤ Cht * x * Real.log T ^ 2 / T

decls.name: c1t
decls.why: The explicit formula's first constant from `x = 2`: `2800 + 2·Cht + Csn`.

decls.name: c3t
decls.why: The explicit formula's log-constant from `x = 2`: `18 + ‖ζ′(0)/ζ(0)‖/log 2`.

decls.name: explicit_formula_left_two
decls.why: The explicit formula with the left edge kept, from `x = 2`. For `2 ≤ x` and `2 ≤ T` there is a height `T′` in `[T, T+1]` with `‖ψ(x) − x + Σ_{|γ|<T} m·x^ρ/ρ‖ ≤ c1t·x·log²(xT)/T + c3t·log x + ‖left edge at T′‖`. `ExplicitLeft.explicit_formula_left`'s proof on the chain from `x = 2`: Perron from `PerronTwo`, the residue identity, the horizontal edges and the swap from this file.
decls.proves: ∃ T' : ℝ, T ≤ T' ∧ T' ≤ T + 1 ∧ ‖(Chebyshev.psi x : ℂ) - (x:ℂ) + Stage3.zeroPartialSum x T‖ ≤ c1t * x * Real.log (x*T)^2 / T + c3t * Real.log x + ‖VIntegral (Glue.Gf x) (-1/4) (-T') T'‖

decls.name: series_side_two
decls.why: The series side from `x = 2`. `LeftKernel.series_side` for `2 ≤ x`: the Dirichlet-series half of the left edge, `∫_{−T}^{T} ζ'/ζ(5/4 − it)·x^(−1/4+it)/(−1/4+it) dt`, has norm at most `4·Bser·x^(−1/4)`. The kernel's `1/log(x·n)` is now bounded by `1/log 2 = 4/log 16`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in (-T)..T, (deriv riemannZeta ((5/4:ℂ) - (t:ℂ) * Complex.I) / riemannZeta ((5/4:ℂ) - (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) * ((x:ℂ) ^ (((-1/4 : ℝ):ℂ) + (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) / (((-1/4 : ℝ):ℂ) + (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ 4 * Bser * x ^ (-(1:ℝ)/4)

decls.name: smooth_side_two
decls.why: The smooth side from `x = 2`. `LeftSmooth.smooth_side` for `2 ≤ x`: with `s = −1/4 + it` and `w = 5/4 − it`, the integral of `(ζ′/ζ(s) + ζ′/ζ(w))·x^s/s` over `[−T, T]` has norm at most `4·Bsm·x^(−1/4)`. The three pieces are bounded by `Nsm/log x` as before; the last step uses `log 2 ≤ log x`, and `Nsm/log 2 = 4·Bsm`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in (-T)..T, (deriv riemannZeta (((-1/4 : ℝ):ℂ) + (t:ℂ) * Complex.I) / riemannZeta (((-1/4 : ℝ):ℂ) + (t:ℂ) * Complex.I) + deriv riemannZeta ((5/4:ℂ) - (t:ℂ) * Complex.I) / riemannZeta ((5/4:ℂ) - (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) * ((x:ℂ) ^ (((-1/4 : ℝ):ℂ) + (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) / (((-1/4 : ℝ):ℂ) + (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ 4 * Bsm * x ^ (-(1:ℝ)/4)

decls.name: Bleft2
decls.why: The left-edge constant from `x = 2`: four times `LeftSmooth.Bleft`.

decls.name: left_edge_bound_two
decls.why: The left edge from `x = 2`. For `2 ≤ x` and `2 ≤ T`, the integral of `−ζ′/ζ(s)·x^s/s` up `Re s = −1/4` from `−T` to `T` has norm at most `Bleft2·x^(−1/4)`, with `Bleft2` free of `x` and `T`: the smooth side plus the series side.

decls.name: explicit_formula_all_two
decls.why: The explicit formula at every height, from `x = 2`. For `2 ≤ x` and `2 ≤ T`: `‖ψ(x) − x + Σ_{|γ|<T} m·x^ρ/ρ‖ ≤ c1t·x·log²(xT)/T + c3t·log x + Bleft2·x^(−1/4)`, with no cap on `T` and the left edge bounded free of the height.
decls.proves: ‖(Chebyshev.psi x : ℂ) - (x:ℂ) + Stage3.zeroPartialSum x T‖ ≤ c1t * x * Real.log (x*T)^2 / T + c3t * Real.log x + Bleft2 * x ^ (-(1:ℝ)/4)

header: FilterAccum — block S3 of `lean_stage3/design/stencil.md`, in its corrected form (the section "After the independent check"). 2026-11-23.

decls.name: qP
decls.why: The filter that vanishes at the inverses of the points of `P`: `q(u) = Π_{p ∈ P} (u − 1/p)`.

decls.name: eval_qP
decls.why: The filter's value at `w` is the product of `w − 1/p` over the points of `P`.

decls.name: L
decls.why: The bound `Π_{p ∈ P} (1 + |1/p|)` on the product of the factors of the filter.

decls.name: L_pos
decls.why: The bound `L` is positive.

decls.name: xiz
decls.why: The rate with `a = 1`, as a function of the mode `z`: `z^b·q(1/z)`.

decls.name: xi_eq_xiz
decls.why: With `a = 1` the rate of a zero depends on the zero only through its mode.
decls.proves: FilterAttained.xi q 1 b ρ = xiz q b ((2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ))

decls.name: one_le_norm_mode
decls.why: The mode of a zero has size at least one.

decls.name: norm_mode_le_two
decls.why: The mode of a zero has size at most two.

decls.name: norm_xiz_near_le
decls.why: A mode near a point of `P` has a small rate. For a mode `z` with `1 ≤ |z| ≤ 2` and a point `p₀` of `P` with `|z − p₀| ≤ ε`, the rate under the filter of `P` is at most `2^b·(ε·L)`.
decls.proves: ‖xiz (qP P) b z‖ ≤ 2 ^ b * (ε * L P)

decls.name: eval_qP_ne_zero
decls.why: A mode outside `P` is not a zero of the filter. For `z` outside `P`, `q(1/z) ≠ 0`.

decls.name: exists_b
decls.why: A large enough `b`. For `c > 0` and `r > 1` there is `b` above the degree of `q` with `W < c·r^b`.
decls.proves: ∃ b : ℕ, q.natDegree < b ∧ W < c * r ^ b

decls.name: finite_accumulation_false
decls.why: Finitely many accumulation points, and a zero right of `σ` off them: the ladder bound fails. Let `|ψ(2^k) − 2^k| ≤ C·k²·√2^k` for `k ≥ 1` and `σ > 1/2`. Let `P` be a finite set of nonzero points such that, for every `ε > 0`, the mode values `2^ρ` of the zeros with real part at least `σ` that lie at distance at least `ε` from every point of `P` form a finite set. Then no zero with real part above `σ` has its mode outside `P`.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖(Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ)^k) : ℂ) - (((2:ℝ)^k : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k
hacc : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → {z : ℂ | ∃ ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros, σ ≤ (ρ : ℂ).re ∧ (2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ) = z ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, ε ≤ ‖z - p‖}.Finite

decls.name: rh_of_finite_accumulation
decls.why: Finitely many accumulation points on every line right of `1/2`, and the ladder of `ψ` of square-root size: then the Riemann hypothesis holds. Let `|ψ(2^k) − 2^k| ≤ C·k²·√2^k` for every `k ≥ 1`. Suppose that for every `σ > 1/2` the modes `2^ρ` of the zeros with real part at least `σ` accumulate only at the points of a finite set `P` of nonzero points (for every `ε > 0` the mode values at distance at least `ε` from all of `P` are finitely many), none of which is the mode of a zero with real part above `σ`. Then the Riemann hypothesis holds.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖(Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ)^k) : ℂ) - (((2:ℝ)^k : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k

hfin : ∀ σ : ℝ, 1/2 < σ → ∃ P : Finset ℂ, (∀ p ∈ P, p ≠ 0) ∧ (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → {z : ℂ | ∃ ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros, σ ≤ (ρ : ℂ).re ∧ (2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ) = z ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, ε ≤ ‖z - p‖}.Finite) ∧ (∀ ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros, σ < (ρ : ℂ).re → (2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ) ∉ P)

header: FilterAttained — block S2 of `lean_stage3/design/stencil.md`, in its corrected form (the section "After the independent check"). 2026-11-23.

decls.name: xi
decls.why: the rate of a zero under the filter

decls.name: S
decls.why: The zeros with real part at least `σ`.

decls.name: ratio
decls.why: The rate of a zero divided by a fixed size `M`.

decls.name: xi_pow
decls.why: The `k`-th power of the rate is the filter `q^(ak)` read on the mode `(2^ρ)^(bk)`.

decls.name: summable_S
decls.why: For `σ > 1/2` the weights `|m(ρ)/ρ|` of the zeros right of `σ`, as a function on all zeros, are summable.

decls.name: finite_part_le
decls.why: The zeros below height `2^(bk)`. Under the hypothesis on the ladder, for `k ≥ 2` and `M > 0`, the sum over the zeros below `2^(bk)` with real part at least `σ ≥ 1/2` of `m(ρ)/ρ·(ξ(ρ)/M)^k` is at most `Afl C·b²·k²·(2^(σb)·‖q‖_W^a/M)^k`.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖(Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ)^k) : ℂ) - (((2:ℝ)^k : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k
decls.proves: ‖∑ ρ ∈ (ZF ((2:ℝ) ^ (b * k))).filter (fun ρ : NontrivialZeros => σ ≤ (ρ : ℂ).re), LadderMean.coef ρ * ratio q a b M ρ ^ k‖ ≤ FilterLadder.Afl C * (b:ℝ) ^ 2 * (k:ℝ) ^ 2 * ((2:ℝ) ^ (σ * b) * FilterLadder.Wn q ^ a / M) ^ k

decls.name: tailT
decls.why: One zero's term at row `k`, kept only when it is right of `σ` and above height `2^(bk)`.

decls.name: norm_tailT_le
decls.why: If the rate over `M` has size at most one right of `σ`, the part of a term above height `2^(bk)` is at most the weight `|m(ρ)/ρ|` of the zero, kept right of `σ`.
needs: hle : ∀ ρ ∈ S σ, ‖ratio q a b M ρ‖ ≤ 1
decls.proves: ‖tailT q a b σ M k ρ‖ ≤ (S σ).indicator (fun ρ => ‖LadderMean.coef ρ‖) ρ

decls.name: tendsto_tailT
decls.why: The parts above height `2^(bk)` fade. For `b ≥ 1`, `σ > 1/2` and the rate over `M` of size at most one right of `σ`, the sum of the parts above `2^(bk)` tends to zero.
needs: hle : ∀ ρ ∈ S σ, ‖ratio q a b M ρ‖ ≤ 1
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => ∑' ρ, tailT q a b σ M k ρ) atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: tsum_split
decls.why: The sum right of `σ` splits at height `2^(bk)`: it is the finite sum over the zeros below `2^(bk)` plus the sum of the parts above.
needs: hle : ∀ ρ ∈ S σ, ‖ratio q a b M ρ‖ ≤ 1
decls.proves: ∑' ρ, (S σ).indicator (fun ρ => LadderMean.coef ρ * ratio q a b M ρ ^ k) ρ = ∑ ρ ∈ (ZF ((2:ℝ) ^ (b * k))).filter (fun ρ : NontrivialZeros => σ ≤ (ρ : ℂ).re), LadderMean.coef ρ * ratio q a b M ρ ^ k + ∑' ρ, tailT q a b σ M k ρ

decls.name: tendsto_full
decls.why: The normalized sum right of `σ` tends to zero. Under the hypothesis on the ladder, with `b ≥ 1`, `a·deg q < b`, `σ > 1/2`, the rate over `M` of size at most one right of `σ`, and `M` above the threshold `2^(σb)·‖q‖_W^a`, the sum over the zeros right of `σ` of `m(ρ)/ρ·(ξ(ρ)/M)^k` tends to zero.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖(Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ)^k) : ℂ) - (((2:ℝ)^k : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k
hle : ∀ ρ ∈ S σ, ‖ratio q a b M ρ‖ ≤ 1
hthr : (2:ℝ) ^ (σ * b) * FilterLadder.Wn q ^ a < M
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => ∑' ρ, (S σ).indicator (fun ρ => LadderMean.coef ρ * ratio q a b M ρ ^ k) ρ) atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: filter_attained_false
decls.why: An attained rate above the threshold under some filter is impossible. Let the ladder of `ψ` be of square-root size, `|ψ(2^k) − 2^k| ≤ C·k²·√2^k` for `k ≥ 1`. Fix a polynomial `q`, naturals `a`, `b` with `b ≥ 1` and `a·deg q < b`, and `σ > 1/2`. No zero `ρ₀` with real part at least `σ` can have the largest rate `|ξ|` among the zeros with real part at least `σ` while that rate exceeds `2^(σb)·‖q‖_W^a`.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖(Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ)^k) : ℂ) - (((2:ℝ)^k : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k
hmax : ∀ ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros, σ ≤ (ρ : ℂ).re → ‖xi q a b ρ‖ ≤ ‖xi q a b ρ₀‖
hthr : (2:ℝ) ^ (σ * b) * FilterLadder.Wn q ^ a < ‖xi q a b ρ₀‖

decls.name: attained_psi
decls.why: The largest real part attained, and the ladder of `ψ` of square-root size: then the Riemann hypothesis holds. Let `ρ₀` have the largest real part among the zeros of ζ. If `|ψ(2^k) − 2^k| ≤ C·k²·√2^k` for every `k ≥ 1`, the Riemann hypothesis holds. It is `filter_attained_false` with no filter: `q = 1`, `a = 0`, `b = 1`.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖(Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ)^k) : ℂ) - (((2:ℝ)^k : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k

header: FilterLadder — block S1 of `lean_stage3/design/stencil.md`. 2026-11-23. The filtered ladder. Put `a_k = ψ(2^k) − 2^k`. A polynomial `q` acts on the ladder by `Σ_j q_j·a_{n−j}`, and on a mode `z^n` as multiplication by `q(1/z)`. With the weighted norm `‖q‖_W = Σ_j |q_j|·2^(−j/2)`, which is submultiplicative, the filter `q^m` with `m·deg q < n` reads only rows `≥ 1`. If the ladder is of square-root size, `|a_k| ≤ C·k²·√2^k`, then the explicit formula at `x = 2^k` and the one height `2^n` for every `k ≤ n` writes the …

decls.name: Wb
decls.why: The weighted size of a polynomial at weight `t`: the sum of the sizes of its coefficients, the `j`-th times `t^j`.

decls.name: Wn
decls.why: The weighted norm of the design: the `j`-th coefficient's size times `2^(−j/2)`.

decls.name: rpow_half_eq
decls.why: The weight `2^(−j/2)` is the `j`-th power of `1/√2`.

decls.name: Wn_eq_Wb
decls.why: The weighted norm of the design is the weighted size at weight `1/√2`.

decls.name: Wb_eq_range
decls.why: The weighted size is the same sum over any range longer than the degree.
decls.proves: Wb t q = ∑ j ∈ range N, ‖q.coeff j‖ * t ^ j

decls.name: Wb_nonneg
decls.why: The weighted size is nonnegative at a nonnegative weight.

decls.name: Wn_nonneg
decls.why: The weighted norm of the design is nonnegative.

decls.name: posPoly
decls.why: The real polynomial whose coefficients are the sizes of the coefficients of `q`.

decls.name: coeff_posPoly
decls.why: Each coefficient of `posPoly q` is the size of the same coefficient of `q`.

decls.name: Wb_eq_eval
decls.why: The weighted size is the value of `posPoly q` at the weight.

decls.name: natDegree_posPoly_le
decls.why: The degree of `posPoly q` is at most that of `q`.

decls.name: Wb_mul_le
decls.why: The weighted size is submultiplicative. At a nonnegative weight, `Wb t (p·q) ≤ Wb t p · Wb t q`: each coefficient of the product is at most the same coefficient of `posPoly p · posPoly q`, whose value at `t` is the product.
decls.proves: Wb t (p * q) ≤ Wb t p * Wb t q

decls.name: Wb_one
decls.why: The weighted size of the constant `1` is `1`.

decls.name: Wb_pow_le
decls.why: The weighted size of a power is at most the power of the weighted size.
decls.proves: Wb t (q ^ m) ≤ Wb t q ^ m

decls.name: Wn_pow_le
decls.why: Fact (i) of block S1. The weighted norm of a power is at most the power of the weighted norm: `‖q^m‖_W ≤ ‖q‖_W^m`.

decls.name: norm_eval_le_Wb
decls.why: The value of a polynomial at `u` has size at most its weighted size at `|u|`.

decls.name: Wb_mono
decls.why: The weighted size grows with the weight.
decls.proves: Wb t q ≤ Wb t' q

decls.name: norm_eval_le_Wn
decls.why: Fact (ii) of block S1. For `|u| ≤ 2^(−1/2)` the value `q(u)` has size at most `‖q‖_W`. For `|u| ≤ 2^(−β)` in general, `norm_eval_le_Wb` and `Wb_mono` give `|q(u)| ≤ Wb (2^(−β)) q = Σ_j |q_j|·2^(−jβ)`.

decls.name: filter_mode
decls.why: Fact (iii) of block S1: the filter on a mode. If `(q^m)` has degree at most `N ≤ n` and `z ≠ 0`, then `Σ_{j≤N} (q^m)_j·z^(n−j) = z^n·q(1/z)^m`.
decls.proves: ∑ j ∈ range (N + 1), (q ^ m).coeff j * z ^ (n - j) = z ^ n * (q.eval z⁻¹) ^ m

decls.name: ladder
decls.why: The ladder: `a_k = ψ(2^k) − 2^k`, as a complex number.

decls.name: Kf
decls.why: The constant of the explicit formula on the rows `k ≤ n` at height `2^n`: `4·c1t + c3t + Bleft2`.

decls.name: Kf_nonneg
decls.why: The constant `Kf` is nonnegative.

decls.name: wz
decls.why: The weight of a zero in the explicit formula: its order over the zero.

decls.name: formula_row
decls.why: The explicit formula on one row, at the one height `2^n`. For `1 ≤ k ≤ n`, the ladder at row `k` plus the sum over the zeros below `2^n` of `m(ρ)/ρ·(2^ρ)^k` has size at most `Kf·n²`. The set of zeros is the same for every `k`.
decls.proves: ‖ladder k + ∑ ρ ∈ ZF ((2:ℝ) ^ n), wz ρ * ((2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ k‖ ≤ Kf * (n:ℝ) ^ 2

decls.name: Afl
decls.why: The constant of the filtered sum: `C + Kf + 39000·Mlow`. It depends on the constant `C` of the hypothesis and on nothing else.

decls.name: filtered_modes_small_sq
decls.why: The filtered modes of the zeros with real part at least `σ`, sharp form. Let the ladder be of square-root size, `|ψ(2^k) − 2^k| ≤ C·k²·√2^k` for `k ≥ 1`, and let `σ ≥ 1/2`. For every polynomial `q` and every `n ≥ 2`, `m` with `m·deg q < n`, the sum over the zeros below `2^n` with real part at least `σ` of `m(ρ)/ρ·q(2^(−ρ))^m·(2^ρ)^n` has size at most `Afl C·n²·2^(σn)·‖q‖_W^m`.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖(Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ)^k) : ℂ) - (((2:ℝ)^k : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k
decls.proves: ‖∑ ρ ∈ (FiniteOffLine.ZF ((2:ℝ)^n)).filter (fun ρ : NontrivialZeros => σ ≤ (ρ : ℂ).re), ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) / (ρ : ℂ) * (q.eval (((2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ))⁻¹)) ^ m * ((2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ n‖ ≤ Afl C * (n:ℝ)^2 * (2:ℝ)^(σ * n) * Wn q ^ m

decls.name: filtered_modes_small
decls.why: Block S1: the filtered modes of the zeros with real part at least `σ`. Let the ladder be of square-root size, `|ψ(2^k) − 2^k| ≤ C·k²·√2^k` for `k ≥ 1`, and let `σ > 1/2`. There is one constant `A` (it is `Afl C`, and depends on `C` alone) such that for every polynomial `q` and every `n ≥ 2`, `m` with `m·deg q < n`, the sum over the zeros below `2^n` with real part at least `σ` of `m(ρ)/ρ·q(2^(−ρ))^m·(2^ρ)^n` has size at most `A·n⁴·2^(σn)·‖q‖_W^m`. The sharp form with `n²` is `filtered_modes_small_sq`.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖(Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ)^k) : ℂ) - (((2:ℝ)^k : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k
decls.proves: ∃ A : ℝ, ∀ (q : Polynomial ℂ) (n m : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → m * q.natDegree < n → ‖∑ ρ ∈ (FiniteOffLine.ZF ((2:ℝ)^n)).filter (fun ρ : NontrivialZeros => σ ≤ (ρ : ℂ).re), ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) / (ρ : ℂ) * (q.eval (((2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ))⁻¹)) ^ m * ((2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ n‖ ≤ A * (n:ℝ)^4 * (2:ℝ)^(σ * n) * Wn q ^ m

header: FiniteOffLine — block J10d of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. The one-ladder converse, in the case of finitely many zeros off the line. Let a finite set hold every zero of ζ off the line. If at one depth the cells of the log-weighted prime count on the table's own ladder stay within `C·r²·√2^r` of their main term, then no zero is off the line.

decls.name: ZF
decls.why: The zeros below a height, as a finite set.

decls.name: mem_ZF
decls.why: A zero is in the finite set exactly when its height is below `T`.

decls.name: tsum_sub_eq_sum
decls.why: A sum over the zeros below a height, read over the finite set.
decls.proves: ∑' σ : {ρ : NontrivialZeros // |(ρ : ℂ).im| < T}, f σ.1 = ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, f ρ

decls.name: order_nonneg
decls.why: The order of a zero is nonnegative.

decls.name: onLineInv
decls.why: The reciprocal size of a zero on the line; zero off the line.

decls.name: onLineInv_nonneg
decls.why: The reciprocal size of a zero on the line, and zero off it, is nonnegative.

decls.name: onLineInv_le_dyadic
decls.why: A zero on the line, below `2^(K+1)`, is dominated by the dyadic weights.
decls.proves: onLineInv ρ ≤ 2 * ∑ j ∈ range (K + 1), ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)⁻¹ * (if |(ρ : ℂ).im| < 2 ^ (j + 1) then 1 else 0)

decls.name: sum_order_onLineInv_le
decls.why: The zeros on the line, weighted by reciprocal size, below a height.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ ZF ((2 : ℝ) ^ (K + 1)), ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) * onLineInv ρ ≤ 2 * ∑ j ∈ range (K + 1), ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)⁻¹ * (2 * |riemannZeta.N ((2 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1))| + weightedZeroHeightBucket)

decls.name: dyadic_count_le
decls.why: The dyadic count, as a square of the number of levels.
decls.proves: ∑ j ∈ range (K + 1), ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)⁻¹ * (2 * |riemannZeta.N ((2 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1))| + weightedZeroHeightBucket) ≤ 3000 * ((K : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2

decls.name: term
decls.why: One zero's term in the cell `(r, d)` of the log-weighted count.

decls.name: norm_two_cpow
decls.why: The size of `2^ρ` is `2` to the real part of `ρ`.

decls.name: norm_term_le
decls.why: The size of one zero's term: its order over its size, times the mode's size.
decls.proves: ‖term d (r : ℤ) ρ‖ ≤ ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) * (2 ^ d * ((2:ℝ) ^ (ρ : ℂ).re) ^ r * ‖(ρ : ℂ)‖⁻¹)

decls.name: cell_zero_sum_finset
decls.why: The cell as a sum over the zeros below a height, read over the finite set.
decls.proves: ‖CellZeros.stencil d (fun n : ℤ => (Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ) ^ n) : ℂ)) r - (2:ℂ) ^ r * (1 - (2:ℂ)⁻¹) ^ d + ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, term d r ρ‖ ≤ ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), (d.choose j : ℝ) * (Glue.c1n * (2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ)) * Real.log ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ)) * T) ^ 2 / T + Glue.c3n * Real.log ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ))) + Glue.c4n * ((Real.log ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ)))) ^ 2 * ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ))) ^ (-(1:ℝ) / 4)))

decls.name: err_le
decls.why: The error of the cell's zero sum at height `2^(K+1)`, `r = d + K + 1`: at most a constant times `r²`.

decls.name: finite_off_line
decls.why: Finitely many zeros off the line, and cells of square-root size on the one ladder: then no zero is off the line. Let a finite set hold every zero of ζ off the line. If at one depth the cells of the log-weighted prime count on the table's own ladder stay within `C·r²·√2^r` of their main term, the Riemann hypothesis holds.
needs: hF : ∀ ρ : NontrivialZeros, (ρ : ℂ).re ≠ 1 / 2 → ρ ∈ F
hcells : ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in atTop, ‖CellZeros.stencil d (fun n : ℤ => (Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ) ^ n) : ℂ)) (r : ℤ) - (2:ℂ) ^ (r : ℤ) * (1 - (2:ℂ)⁻¹) ^ d‖ ≤ C * (r : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ r

header: FiniteOffLinePi — block J10e of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-23. The one-ladder converse for the count of primes, in the case of finitely many zeros off the line. Let a finite set hold every zero of ζ off the line. If the count of primes at the doublings `2^r` stays within `C·r²·√2^r` of `Li`, then no zero is off the line.

decls.name: ipart
decls.why: The integral in one zero's part of the count.

decls.name: piMode_eq
decls.why: One zero's part of the count is `x^ρ/ρ` over `log x`, plus the integral.
decls.proves: piMode ρ x = (x : ℂ) ^ ρ / ρ / (Real.log x : ℂ) + ipart ρ x

decls.name: norm_integrand
decls.why: For `t ≥ 2` the integrand has size `t^b/(|ρ|·t·log²t)`, with `b` the real part.
decls.proves: ‖(t : ℂ) ^ ρ / ρ * wt t‖ = ‖ρ‖⁻¹ * (t ^ ρ.re * (t * Real.log t ^ 2)⁻¹)

decls.name: norm_ipart_le
decls.why: The integral in one zero's part. For a real part `b` in `(0, 1]` and `x ≥ 4`, the integral is at most `(3√x + 4x^b/(b·log²x))/|ρ|`.
decls.proves: ‖ipart ρ x‖ ≤ ‖ρ‖⁻¹ * (3 * Real.sqrt x + 4 * x ^ ρ.re / (ρ.re * Real.log x ^ 2))

decls.name: norm_piMode_le
decls.why: One zero's part of the count. For a real part `b` in `(0, 1]` and `x ≥ 4`, the part is at most `((1 + 4/b)·x^b + 3√x)/|ρ|`.
decls.proves: ‖piMode ρ x‖ ≤ ‖ρ‖⁻¹ * ((1 + 4 / ρ.re) * x ^ ρ.re + 3 * Real.sqrt x)

decls.name: norm_piMode_half
decls.why: One zero on the line. For real part `1/2` and `x ≥ 4`, the zero's part of the count is at most `12√x/|ρ|`.

decls.name: sqrt_doubling
decls.why: The square root of `2^r` is `√2^r`.

decls.name: rpow_doubling
decls.why: The real power `b` of `2^r` is `(2^b)^r`.

decls.name: cpow_doubling
decls.why: The complex power `ρ` of `2^r` is `(2^ρ)^r`.

decls.name: ordR
decls.why: The order of a zero, as a real number.

decls.name: ordR_nonneg
decls.why: The order of a zero is nonnegative.

decls.name: norm_order_mul
decls.why: The order of a zero, as a factor, multiplies the size by the order.
decls.proves: ‖((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * w‖ = ordR ρ * ‖w‖

decls.name: rowBound
decls.why: The bound on the top line's sum at row `r`.

decls.name: rowBound_isLittleO
decls.why: The row's bound is small against the top line. If `β > 1/2` and every zero of `F \ S` has real part below `β`, the bound is `o((2^β)^r)`.
needs: hlt : ∀ ρ ∈ F \ S, (ρ : ℂ).re < β
decls.proves: (fun r : ℕ => rowBound F S β C r) =o[atTop] fun r : ℕ => ((2:ℝ) ^ β) ^ r

decls.name: row_bound
decls.why: The top line's sum at one row. Let `S ⊆ F` have real part `β`, let `F` hold every zero off the line and lie below `2^r`, with `r ≥ 8`. If the count of primes at `2^r` is within `C·r²·√2^r` of `Li`, the sum `Σ_{ρ∈S} m(ρ)·(2^ρ)^r/ρ` is at most `rowBound F S β C r`.
needs: hF : ∀ ρ : NontrivialZeros, (ρ : ℂ).re ≠ 1 / 2 → ρ ∈ F
hrow : |(Nat.primeCounting ⌊(2:ℝ) ^ r⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li ((2:ℝ) ^ r)| ≤ C * (r : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ r
decls.proves: ‖∑ ρ ∈ S, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * (((2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)) ^ r / (ρ : ℂ))‖ ≤ rowBound F S β C r

decls.name: finite_off_line_pi
decls.why: Finitely many zeros off the line, and the count of primes of square-root size at the doublings: then no zero is off the line. Let a finite set hold every zero of ζ off the line. If the count of primes at `2^r` stays within `C·r²·√2^r` of `Li` from some row on, the Riemann hypothesis holds.
needs: hF : ∀ ρ : NontrivialZeros, (ρ : ℂ).re ≠ 1 / 2 → ρ ∈ F
hrows : ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in atTop, |(Nat.primeCounting ⌊(2:ℝ) ^ r⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li ((2:ℝ) ^ r)| ≤ C * (r : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ r

header: FixedRowTwo — block G3 of `lean_stage3/design/floor.md`. 2026-11-23. The fixed-row theorems of `CellFixedRow` and `PiFixedRow` restated on `ExplicitTwo.explicit_formula_all_two`, the explicit formula at every height from `x = 2`. The originals read `LeftSmooth.explicit_formula_all` and carry its floor (`r ≥ d + 4`, `r ≥ d + 6`, `x ≥ 16`). Here every row the cell's identity reads is at least `2`, so the theorems hold at every row where the identity holds. For the count the whole integral `∫₂ˣ` is read from the formu…

decls.name: c1t_nonneg
decls.why: The first constant of the formula from `x = 2` is nonnegative.

decls.name: c3t_nonneg
decls.why: The logarithmic constant of the formula from `x = 2` is nonnegative.

decls.name: Bleft2_nonneg
decls.why: The left-edge constant from `x = 2` is nonnegative: it is four times `Bleft`.

decls.name: cell_eq_zero_sum_two
decls.why: The cell as a sum over the zeros, at every height, from row value `2`. For `2 ≤ 2^(r−d)` and any `T ≥ 2`, the cell at row `r`, depth `d`, minus its main term, plus the sum over the zeros below `T`, has norm at most the stencil of the error of the explicit formula from `x = 2`, read on the `d + 1` rows the stencil touches.
decls.proves: ‖CellZeros.stencil d (fun n : ℤ => (Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ) ^ n) : ℂ)) r - (2:ℂ) ^ r * (1 - (2:ℂ)⁻¹) ^ d + ∑' ρ : {ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros // |(ρ : ℂ).im| < T}, ((riemannZeta.order ((ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros) : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * (((2:ℂ) ^ ((ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros) : ℂ)) ^ r * (1 - ((2:ℂ) ^ ((ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros) : ℂ))⁻¹) ^ d / ((ρ : Kadiri.NontrivialZeros) : ℂ))‖ ≤ ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), (d.choose j : ℝ) * (ExplicitTwo.c1t * (2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ)) * Real.log ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ)) * T) ^ 2 / T + ExplicitTwo.c3t * Real.log ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ))) + ExplicitTwo.Bleft2 * ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ))) ^ (-(1:ℝ) / 4))

decls.name: cell_zero_sum_finset_two
decls.why: The same, over the finite set of zeros below the height.
decls.proves: ‖CellZeros.stencil d (fun n : ℤ => (Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ) ^ n) : ℂ)) r - (2:ℂ) ^ r * (1 - (2:ℂ)⁻¹) ^ d + ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, term d r ρ‖ ≤ ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), (d.choose j : ℝ) * (ExplicitTwo.c1t * (2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ)) * Real.log ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ)) * T) ^ 2 / T + ExplicitTwo.c3t * Real.log ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ))) + ExplicitTwo.Bleft2 * ((2:ℝ) ^ (r - (j : ℤ))) ^ (-(1:ℝ) / 4))

decls.name: cell_fixed_row_two
decls.why: The cell at a fixed row, the height to infinity, from row `d + 1`. For `d + 1 ≤ r` and every `ε > 0`, for all large heights `T` the cell at row `r`, depth `d`, minus its main term, plus its sum over the zeros below `T`, has norm at most `2^d·(c3t·log 2·r + Bleft2) + ε`. The bound left is free of the height.
decls.proves: ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in Filter.atTop, ‖CellZeros.stencil d (fun n : ℤ => (Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ) ^ n) : ℂ)) (r : ℤ) - (2:ℂ) ^ (r : ℤ) * (1 - (2:ℂ)⁻¹) ^ d + ∑ ρ ∈ FiniteOffLine.ZF T, FiniteOffLine.term d (r : ℤ) ρ‖ ≤ 2 ^ d * (ExplicitTwo.c3t * Real.log 2 * r + ExplicitTwo.Bleft2) + ε

decls.name: Api2
decls.why: The constant of the count at a fixed row from `x = 2`: `(3/2)·c3t + (9/4)·Bleft2`. The factors are `1/log t ≤ 3/2` and `1/log²t ≤ 9/4` on `t ≥ 2`.

decls.name: Api2_nonneg
decls.why: The constant `Api2` is nonnegative.

decls.name: norm_integrand_two_le
decls.why: The integrand on `[2, x]`. For `2 ≤ t ≤ x` and `T ≥ 2`, the remainder of the explicit formula times the weight has norm at most `(9/4)·c1t·log²(xT)/T + Api2/t`.
decls.proves: ‖efRem T t * wt t‖ ≤ 9 / 4 * ExplicitTwo.c1t * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T + Api2 * t⁻¹

decls.name: norm_integral_two_le
decls.why: The whole integral from `x = 2`. For `2 ≤ x` and `T ≥ 2`, the integral of the remainder against the weight over `[2, x]` is at most `(x − 2)·(9/4)·c1t·log²(xT)/T + Api2·log(x/2)`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in (2:ℝ)..x, efRem T t * wt t‖ ≤ (x - 2) * (9 / 4 * ExplicitTwo.c1t * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T) + Api2 * Real.log (x / 2)

decls.name: norm_tr_efRem_le_height_two
decls.why: The passage of the remainder at a fixed row and a finite height, from `x = 2`. For `2 ≤ x` and `T ≥ 2`, `‖tr (efRem T) x‖ ≤ Api2·(1 + log x) + 4·c1t·x·log²(xT)/T`.
decls.proves: ‖tr (efRem T) x‖ ≤ Api2 * (1 + Real.log x) + 4 * ExplicitTwo.c1t * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T

decls.name: tr_efRem_fixed_two
decls.why: The passage of the remainder at a fixed row, the height to infinity, from `x = 2`. For `2 ≤ x` and every `ε > 0`, for all large heights `T`, `‖tr (efRem T) x‖ ≤ Api2·(1 + log x) + ε`.
decls.proves: ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in Filter.atTop, ‖PiZeros.tr (PiZeros.efRem T) x‖ ≤ Api2 * (1 + Real.log x) + ε

decls.name: pi_fixed_row_two
decls.why: The count at a fixed row, the height to infinity, from `x = 2`. For `2 ≤ x` and every `ε > 0`, for all large heights `T`, the count minus `Li`, plus each zero's part below `T`, plus the higher prime powers, is at most `Api2·(1 + log x) + ε`.
decls.proves: ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in Filter.atTop, ‖(((Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li x : ℝ) : ℂ) + ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * piMode (ρ : ℂ) x + tr psiTheta x‖ ≤ Api2 * (1 + Real.log x) + ε

decls.name: table_cell_fixed_row_two
decls.why: The integer table's cell at a fixed row, the height to infinity, from row `d + 2`. For `d + 2 ≤ r` and every `ε > 0`, for all large heights `T`, the cell `(r, d)` of the table of the prime count along the doublings, less the smooth cell, plus each zero's part below `T` under the stencil, plus the stencil of the higher prime powers, is at most `2^(d+1)·(Api2·(1 + log 2·r)) + ε`.
decls.proves: ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in Filter.atTop, ‖((((Construction.tableFrom TableRoute.rowN (r : ℤ) d : ℤ) : ℝ) - Nonvanishing.stencilR (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => Stage3.Li ((2 : ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) (r : ℤ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * CellZeros.stencil (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => piMode (ρ : ℂ) ((2:ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) (r : ℤ) + CellZeros.stencil (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => tr psiTheta ((2:ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) (r : ℤ)‖ ≤ 2 ^ (d + 1) * (Api2 * (1 + Real.log 2 * r)) + ε

header: GateEval — block E9 of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. The table gate's own inequality, evaluated on the explicit-formula route at the floor `x₀ = 2^36` and depth six.

decls.name: floor_bound
decls.why: Helper: the arithmetic of `routeConst` at the floor `2^36`. If `c1 ≤ 88216610000`, `c3 ≤ 15`, `c4 ≤ 6468930000` and `24.95 ≤ ℓ`, then the expression with `ℓ` in place of the logarithm of the floor is at most `414`.

decls.name: routeConst_le
decls.why: The route constant at the floor `2^36` is at most `414`.

decls.name: gate_ineq
decls.why: The gate's inequality at depth six: if `80 ≤ r`, then `414·(log 2·r)·2^(-((r - 7)/2)) < (log 2)^6/(2·r·3^7)`.

decls.name: gate_hyp_of_RH
decls.why: The gate's two hypotheses, under RH, at depth six from row 80.
decls.proves: ∃ ρ : ℝ, JointDialGate.StmtRelErrWindow (fun m : ℤ => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊(2 : ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ)⌋₊ : ℝ)) (fun m : ℤ => 2 / Real.log 2 + ∫ t in (1 : ℝ)..(m : ℝ), Real.exp (Real.log 2 * t) / t) r (6 + 1) ρ ∧ ρ < Real.log 2 ^ 6 / (2 * r * 3 ^ (6 + 1))

header: # The glue — assembling StmtExplicitFormula from the four slices Pieces, in build order: - the band count and the `zeroPartialSum` swap (`T′ → T`), - the edge-integral estimates (S3's pointwise bounds integrated), - the rectangle-edge splitting matching S1's line integral, - the final assembly in the `T ≤ x²` regime + the consumer patch.

decls.name: band_order_sum_le
decls.why: The band count: any finite set of strip zeros with `|im|` in `[T, T+1]` has total multiplicity `≤ C·log T` — two windows per sign, reflection for the left half, conjugation for the negative sign.
decls.proves: ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ T : ℝ, 2 ≤ T → ∀ F : Finset ℂ, (∀ ρ ∈ F, riemannZeta ρ = 0 ∧ (0 < ρ.re ∧ ρ.re < 1) ∧ T ≤ |ρ.im| ∧ |ρ.im| ≤ T + 1) → (∑ ρ ∈ F, (analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta ρ : ℝ)) ≤ C * Real.log T

decls.name: zeroPartialSum_swap
decls.why: The swap: moving the zero sum from a height `T′ ∈ [T, T+1]` back to `T` costs `≤ C·x·log T / T`.
decls.proves: ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x T T' : ℝ, 16 ≤ x → 2 ≤ T → T ≤ T' → T' ≤ T + 1 → ‖Stage3.zeroPartialSum x T' - Stage3.zeroPartialSum x T‖ ≤ C * x * Real.log T / T

decls.name: Gf
decls.why: The contour integrand of the explicit formula.

decls.name: zeta_logderiv_good_bound
decls.why: The pointwise good-height bound, both signs of the height.
decls.proves: ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ T T' : ℝ, 2 ≤ T → T' ∈ Set.Icc T (T+1) → (∀ ρ : ℂ, riemannZeta ρ = 0 → 0 < ρ.re → ContourShift.zeroGap T ≤ |ρ.im - T'|) → ∀ u : ℂ, |u.im| = T' → -1/4 ≤ u.re → u.re ≤ 2 → ‖deriv riemannZeta u / riemannZeta u‖ ≤ C * Real.log T ^ 2

decls.name: edge_horizontal_bound
decls.why: The horizontal-edge integral bound at a good height, both signs: `≤ C·x·log²T/T`.
decls.proves: ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x T T' : ℝ, 16 ≤ x → 2 ≤ T → T' ∈ Set.Icc T (T+1) → (∀ ρ : ℂ, riemannZeta ρ = 0 → 0 < ρ.re → ContourShift.zeroGap T ≤ |ρ.im - T'|) → ∀ y : ℝ, |y| = T' → ‖HIntegral (Gf x) (-1/4) (1 + 1/Real.log x) y‖ ≤ C * x * Real.log T ^ 2 / T

decls.name: Gf_norm_conj
decls.why: Conjugation symmetry of the integrand's norm.

header: HalfSieve — block R6 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`. 2026-11-23. The half of the closed loop, carried into the sieve.

decls.name: ignition_is_zeta_zero
decls.why: The half is zeta at zero. The offset of the midpoint of the `n`-th doubling above `2^n − 1` is minus the value of zeta at zero, at every `n`.
decls.proves: ((ClosedLoopChain.Midpoint n : ℚ) : ℂ) - ((2 : ℂ) ^ n - 1) = - riemannZeta 0

decls.name: two_mem_smallPrimes
decls.why: From `N = 4` on the prime `2` is among the sieve's primes.

decls.name: half_cancels
decls.why: The signs of the sieve add to nothing. Over all the sieve's terms the signs `(−1)^|T|` sum to zero: the alternating sum of a Pascal row.

decls.name: netRounding_centered
decls.why: The roundings measured from one half. The half of every rounding cancels identically in the sieve's sum.
decls.proves: netRounding N = ∑ T ∈ (smallPrimes N).powerset, (-1 : ℚ) ^ T.card * (Int.fract ((N : ℚ) / ((∏ p ∈ T, p : ℕ) : ℚ)) - 1 / 2)

decls.name: resid
decls.why: The residual of the count at `N`.

decls.name: resid_step
decls.why: The residual, one square root down.
decls.proves: resid N = resid (Nat.sqrt N) - wobble N

decls.name: resid_of_wobble
decls.why: The wobble carries the residual. If the wobble is at square-root size at every `N ≥ 2`, so is the residual of the count.

decls.name: wobble_of_spiralLink

header: HolyChannel — block J9 of `lean_stage3/design/closedloop.md`. 2026-11-23. Julian's Holy Family is an uneven mirror pair: support `J = 1/3`, condition `M = 2/3`, adding to one, the condition the mirror of the support. Every prime carries that pair as its residual and never resolves it. The zero is the channel the residual passes through: it sits at the pair's midpoint and is never a member. Two facing mirrors cannot tell A from B exactly when they are one mirror; a zero is its own mirror exactly at the midpoint.

decls.name: midpoint_half
decls.why: The midpoint of any Holy Family is one half.

decls.name: holy_pair_shares
decls.why: The pair's shape. A zero whose share is the support has its mirror at the condition.

decls.name: member_is_two
decls.why: A member is two mirrors. A zero at the share of either member of the Holy Family is a different point from its mirror, and at every total above one its mode and its mirror's are different sizes.
decls.proves: mirrorZ ρ ≠ ρ ∧ ‖(T : ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)‖ ≠ ‖(T : ℂ) ^ ((mirrorZ ρ : NontrivialZeros) : ℂ)‖

decls.name: meet_iff_channel
decls.why: The channel. A zero's mode meets its mirror's exactly when the zero's share is the Holy Family's midpoint.
decls.proves: ‖(T : ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)‖ = ‖(T : ℂ) ^ ((mirrorZ ρ : NontrivialZeros) : ℂ)‖ ↔ (ρ : ℂ).re = (hf.J + hf.M) / 2

decls.name: channel_iff_self_mirror
decls.why: One mirror. A zero is at the channel exactly when it is its own mirror.

decls.name: ZeroIsChannel
decls.why: Every zero sits at the midpoint of the Holy Family: the channel.

decls.name: spiralLink_iff_channel
decls.why: The link, as the channel. The spiral link holds exactly when every zero is the channel of the Holy Family.

header: JensenCount — `StmtLocalCount` discharged: the Backlund-style local zero count for `ζ`, with explicit constants.

decls.name: zeta_centre_lower
decls.why: For every real `T`, the norm of `ζ` at the centre `2 + iT` is at least `1/3`.

decls.name: zeta_disk_upper
decls.why: The majorant on the wide disk. `‖ζ w‖ ≤ 28 T` for `T ≥ 2` and `‖w - (2 + iT)‖ ≤ 15/8`; this is the `R = 15/16` radius of the Jensen step pulled back through `s = 2z + (2 + iT)`. On that disk `Re w ≥ 1/8 > 0` and `Im w ≥ T - 15/8 ≥ 1/8`, so the pole at `s = 1` is avoided with room.

decls.name: zeta_centre_ne_zero
decls.why: The centre `2 + iT` has real part `2`, hence `ζ` does not vanish there.

decls.name: pole_away
decls.why: The pole stays outside the mapped ball. For `T ≥ 2` and `‖z‖ ≤ 11/10`, the point `2z + (2 + iT)` is never the pole `s = 1`.

decls.name: pole_away_centre
decls.why: The pole stays outside the window. For `T ≥ 2`, every point within `11/5` of `2 + iT` differs from `1`.

decls.name: zetaWindowTwo_finite
decls.why: `ζ` has finitely many zeros within `2` of the centre.

decls.name: zetaWindow
decls.why: The window. `ζ`'s zeros in the closed disk of radius `7/4` about `2 + iT`. On the critical line this disk covers `|γ - T| ≤ √(13/16)` ≈ `0.901`, an interval of positive length — which is what radius `3/2` fails to do, being tangent to the line and so catching only `γ = T`.

decls.name: zetaWindow_finite
decls.why: For `T ≥ 2`, the window of zeros of `ζ` within `7/4` of `2 + iT` is finite.

decls.name: jensenF
decls.why: The normalised local model. `f z = ζ (2z + 2 + iT) / ζ (2 + iT)`; the closed unit ball maps onto `|s - (2+iT)| ≤ 2`.

decls.name: zeta_comp_analytic
decls.why: For `T ≥ 2` and `‖w‖ ≤ 11/10`, the map `z ↦ ζ (2z + (2 + iT))` is analytic at `w`.
decls.proves: AnalyticAt ℂ (fun z : ℂ => ζ (2 * z + (2 + Complex.I * (T : ℂ)))) w

decls.name: jensenF_analytic
decls.why: For `T ≥ 2`, the normalised local model `jensenF T` is analytic on a neighbourhood of the closed unit ball.

decls.name: jensenF_zero_eq_one
decls.why: The normalised local model takes the value `1` at the origin: `jensenF T 0 = 1`.

decls.name: jensenF_zeros_finite
decls.why: For `T ≥ 2`, the zero set `SetOfZeros 1 (jensenF T)` of the normalised local model at radius `1` is finite.

decls.name: jensenF_bound
decls.why: For `T ≥ 2` and `‖z‖ ≤ 15/16`, the normalised local model satisfies `‖jensenF T z‖ ≤ 84 T`.

decls.name: analyticOrderNatAt_fun_comp_affine
decls.why: The analytic order is unchanged by an invertible affine change of variable.
decls.proves: analyticOrderNatAt (fun w : ℂ => g (a * w + b)) z = analyticOrderNatAt g (a * z + b)

decls.name: jensenF_order
decls.why: For `T ≥ 2` and `‖w‖ ≤ 11/10`, the analytic order of `jensenF T` at `w` equals the analytic order of `ζ` at `2w + (2 + iT)`.
decls.proves: analyticOrderNatAt (jensenF T) w = analyticOrderNatAt ζ (2 * w + (2 + Complex.I * (T : ℂ)))

decls.name: zeta_local_zero_count
decls.why: THE LOCAL ZERO COUNT. For every `T ≥ 2`, the total order of the zeros of `ζ` in the closed disk `|s - (2 + iT)| ≤ 7/4` — a disk which meets the critical line in the segment `|γ - T| ≤ √(13/16)` — is at most `15 log T + 73`.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ (zetaWindow_finite hT).toFinset, (analyticOrderNatAt ζ ρ : ℝ) ≤ 15 * Real.log T + 73

decls.name: zetaLocalCount
decls.why: The count function. Total zero order of `ζ` in `|s - (2+iT)| ≤ 7/4`.

decls.name: zetaLocalCount_eq
decls.why: For `T ≥ 2`, the count function `zetaLocalCount T` equals the sum of the analytic orders of `ζ` over the finite window of zeros within `7/4` of `2 + iT`.
decls.proves: zetaLocalCount T = ∑ ρ ∈ (zetaWindow_finite hT).toFinset, (analyticOrderNatAt ζ ρ : ℝ)

decls.name: localCount_holds
decls.why: THE LEAF, DISCHARGED. `StmtLocalCount` holds for the concrete zeta zero count with the explicit constants `A₁ = 15`, `A₃ = 73`. Entry 130's budget accepts `A₁ ≤ 100`, `A₃ ≤ 1000`, so these clear it with room; the widening from radius `3/2` to `7/4` cost roughly a factor of two in `A₁` and is paid out of that budget.

header: LadderFading — block J10b of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. Joint 10 on the table's own ladder, second piece. `AliasClass` showed that the zeros the ladder folds together contribute one mode with a weight that is not zero. This module shows that finitely many such modes of one size cannot fade: their sum along the rows is not small against that size. The proof is the table's own operation: one difference with the symbol of a mode removes that mode and keeps every other weight nonzero.

decls.why: If `s ≠ 0`, `s ≠ 1` and `ζ s ≠ 0`, then `Phi` is complex differentiable at `s`.

decls.name: Phi_principal_part
decls.why: At a zero `ρ` of `ζ` with `ρ ≠ 0` and `ρ ≠ 1`, of order `m`, there is a function `h` analytic at `ρ` such that `Phi s = h s + m/(ρ(1−ρ))/(s−ρ)` for `s` near `ρ`, `s ≠ ρ`.
decls.proves: ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ h ρ ∧ ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[≠] ρ, LandauMellinG.Phi s = h s + (analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta ρ : ℂ) / (ρ * (1 - ρ)) / (s - ρ)

decls.name: Phi_regular_at_one
decls.why: There is a function `h` analytic at `1` with `Phi s = h s` for `s` near `1`, `s ≠ 1`.
decls.proves: ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ h 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[≠] 1, LandauMellinG.Phi s = h s

header: LandauPoleSub — finitely many simple poles subtracted on an open set, and what that gives for the Taylor coefficients. Nothing here is about `ζ`. Block 3b1 of `lean_stage3/design/landau.md`. 2026-11-22.

decls.name: iteratedDeriv_inv_sub
decls.why: The `k`-th derivative of `s ↦ (s − q)⁻¹` at `c` is `(−1)^k·k!·(c − q)^(−1−k)`.
decls.proves: iteratedDeriv k (fun s : ℂ => (s - q)⁻¹) c = (-1) ^ k * (k.factorial : ℂ) * (c - q) ^ (-1 - (k : ℤ))

decls.name: exists_differentiableOn_sub_poles
decls.why: If `f` is differentiable at every point of `U` off the finite set `P`, and near each `p ∈ P` has the local form `f = h + A p/(s − p)` with `h` analytic at `p`, then there is a `g` differentiable on `U` with `g = f − Σ_{q ∈ P} A q/(s − q)` off `P`.
needs: hf : ∀ s ∈ U, s ∉ P → DifferentiableAt ℂ f s
hloc : ∀ p ∈ P, ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ h p ∧ ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[≠] p, f s = h s + A p / (s - p)
decls.proves: ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ g U ∧ ∀ s, s ∉ P → g s = f s - ∑ q ∈ P, A q / (s - q)

decls.name: taylor_coeff_sub_poles
decls.why: If the closed ball of radius `R > 0` about `c` lies in the open set `U`, `c ∉ P`, and `g` is differentiable on `U` with `g = f − Σ_{q ∈ P} A q/(s − q)` off `P`, then there is a `C` such that for every `k` the `k`-th derivative of `f` at `c` is within `k!·C/R^k` of `Σ_{q ∈ P} A q·(−1)^k·k!·(c − q)^(−1−k)`.
needs: hgf : ∀ s, s ∉ P → g s = f s - ∑ q ∈ P, A q / (s - q)
decls.proves: ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ k : ℕ, ‖iteratedDeriv k f c - ∑ q ∈ P, A q * ((-1) ^ k * (k.factorial : ℂ) * (c - q) ^ (-1 - (k : ℤ)))‖ ≤ k.factorial * C / R ^ k

header: LandauPrimeSide — the primes' reading of the Taylor coefficients of `Phi`, bounded from above by a window bound on `G`. Block 7a of `lean_stage3/design/landau.md`. 2026-11-22.

decls.name: Ik_integrable
decls.why: For real `σ > 1` and every natural `k`, the integrand `G(y)·(log y)^k·y^(−σ−1)` of `Ik` is integrable on `(1, ∞)`.
decls.proves: IntegrableOn (fun y : ℝ => LandauWindow.G y * Real.log y ^ k * y ^ (-σ - 1)) (Ioi 1)

decls.name: iteratedDeriv_Phi_eq_Ik
decls.why: For real `σ > 1`, the `k`-th derivative of `Phi` at `σ` is `(−1)^k · Ik σ k`.
decls.proves: iteratedDeriv k LandauMellinG.Phi (σ : ℂ) = (-1) ^ k * ((Ik σ k : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: Ik_le
decls.why: The upper bound on the primes' integral. For `σ > 1`, `θ < σ`, `C ≥ 0`, `Y ≥ 1`, `δ ≥ 0`, a window bound `G y ≤ C·y^θ` on `[Y, Y^(1+δ)]`, and shifts `b > 0`, `0 < b' < σ − 1`: `Ik σ k ≤ C·k!/(σ−θ)^(k+1) + 8·Y^b·k!/(σ−1+b)^(k+1) + 8·(Y^(1+δ))^(−b')·k!/(σ−1−b')^(k+1)`.
needs: hwin : ∀ y ∈ Icc Y (Y ^ (1 + δ)), LandauWindow.G y ≤ C * y ^ θ
decls.proves: Ik σ k ≤ C * (k.factorial / (σ - θ) ^ (k + 1)) + 8 * (Y ^ b * (k.factorial / (σ - 1 + b) ^ (k + 1))) + 8 * ((Y ^ (1 + δ)) ^ (-b') * (k.factorial / (σ - 1 - b') ^ (k + 1)))

header: LandauRates — the scalar inequalities of the assembly. Block 7c of `lean_stage3/design/landau.md`. 2026-11-22.

decls.name: key_ineq
decls.why: The inequality between the rates of the two tails. If `0 < δ ≤ 1` and `0 ≤ λ ≤ δ²/240`, then `4(λ − log(1−δ/12)) < (1+δ)(log(1+δ/3) − λ)`, and both `log(1+δ/3) − λ` and `λ − log(1−δ/12)` are positive.
decls.proves: 4 * (lam - Real.log (1 - δ / 12)) < (1 + δ) * (Real.log (1 + δ / 3) - lam) ∧ 0 < Real.log (1 + δ / 3) - lam ∧ 0 < lam - Real.log (1 - δ / 12)

decls.name: exists_centre
decls.why: The choice of the real centre. If `0 ≤ θ < Re ρ₀ < 1` and `0 < δ`, there is a real `σ₀ > 1` with `‖σ₀ − ρ₀‖ < σ₀ − θ` and `‖σ₀ − ρ₀‖ ≤ (σ₀ − 1)(1 + δ²/240)`.

decls.name: exists_pow_small
decls.why: If `0 ≤ q < 1` and `0 < ε`, there is a `K` such that `c·q^k < ε` for every `k ≥ K`.
decls.proves: ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ k : ℕ, K ≤ k → c * q ^ k < ε

header: LandauTail — the kernel off the window: the integral of `(log y)^k·y^(−a−1)` over `(1, Y]` and over `(Z, ∞)`, each bounded by a shift of the exponent. Block 4b of `lean_stage3/design/landau.md`. 2026-11-22.

decls.name: kernel_nonneg
decls.why: Helper: the kernel `(log y)^k·y^(−a−1)` is nonnegative almost everywhere on `(1, ∞)`.
decls.proves: 0 ≤ᵐ[volume.restrict (Ioi (1 : ℝ))] fun y : ℝ => Real.log y ^ k * y ^ (-a - 1)

decls.name: lower_tail_le
decls.why: For `a > 0`, `b > 0` and `Y ≥ 1`, the integral of the kernel `(log y)^k·y^(−a−1)` over `(1, Y]` is at most `Y^b · k!/(a+b)^(k+1)`.
decls.proves: ∫ y in Ioc (1 : ℝ) Y, Real.log y ^ k * y ^ (-a - 1) ≤ Y ^ b * (k.factorial / (a + b) ^ (k + 1))

decls.name: upper_tail_le
decls.why: For `0 < b < a` and `Z ≥ 1`, the integral of the kernel `(log y)^k·y^(−a−1)` over `(Z, ∞)` is at most `Z^(−b) · k!/(a−b)^(k+1)`.
decls.proves: ∫ y in Ioi Z, Real.log y ^ k * y ^ (-a - 1) ≤ Z ^ (-b) * (k.factorial / (a - b) ^ (k + 1))

header: LandauTaylor — the derivatives of `Phi` on `Re s > 1`, from the primes: iteratedDeriv k Phi s = ∫₁^∞ G(y)·(−log y)^k·y^(−s−1) dy.

decls.name: integrand_norm_le
decls.why: The domination: for `Re s ≥ 1 + a` the integrand is at most this.
decls.proves: ‖(LandauWindow.G y : ℂ) * (-(Real.log y : ℂ)) ^ k * (y : ℂ) ^ (-s - 1)‖ ≤ 8 * (Real.log y ^ k * y ^ (-a - 1) + Real.log y ^ (k + 1) * y ^ (-a - 1))

decls.name: bound_integrable
decls.why: Helper: for `a > 0`, the dominating function `8·((log y)^k·y^(−a−1) + (log y)^(k+1)·y^(−a−1))` is integrable on `(1, ∞)`.
decls.proves: IntegrableOn (fun y : ℝ => 8 * (Real.log y ^ k * y ^ (-a - 1) + Real.log y ^ (k + 1) * y ^ (-a - 1))) (Ioi 1)

decls.name: mellinLog_integrable
decls.why: For `Re s > 1` and every `k`, the integrand of `mellinLog k s`, `G(y)·(−log y)^k·y^(−s−1)`, is integrable on `(1, ∞)`.
decls.proves: IntegrableOn (fun y : ℝ => (LandauWindow.G y : ℂ) * (-(Real.log y : ℂ)) ^ k * (y : ℂ) ^ (-s - 1)) (Ioi 1)

decls.name: mellinLog_hasDerivAt
decls.why: For `Re s > 1` and every `k`, the function `mellinLog k` has complex derivative `mellinLog (k+1) s` at `s`.

decls.name: iteratedDeriv_Phi
decls.why: For `Re s > 1`, the `k`-th derivative of `Phi` at `s` equals `mellinLog k s`, the integral `∫₁^∞ G(y)·(−log y)^k·y^(−s−1) dy`.
decls.proves: iteratedDeriv k LandauMellinG.Phi s = mellinLog k s

decls.name: mellinLog_real
decls.why: At a real point `σ`, `mellinLog k σ` equals `(−1)^k` times the real integral `∫₁^∞ G(y)·(log y)^k·y^(−σ−1) dy`.
decls.proves: mellinLog k (σ : ℂ) = (-1) ^ k * ((∫ y in Ioi (1 : ℝ), LandauWindow.G y * Real.log y ^ k * y ^ (-σ - 1) : ℝ) : ℂ)

header: LandauTrig — a real exponential sum is large somewhere in every long block. Block 6 of `lean_stage3/design/landau.md`. 2026-11-22.

decls.name: norm_geom_Ico_le
decls.why: If `w` has modulus one and `w ≠ 1`, then the geometric sum of `w^n` over a block of `N` consecutive `n` starting at `a` has norm at most `2/‖w - 1‖`.
decls.proves: ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.Ico a (a + N), w ^ n‖ ≤ 2 / ‖w - 1‖

decls.name: re_mul_geom_ge
decls.why: The real part of `c·Σ w^n` over a block, from below, when `w ≠ 1`.
decls.proves: -(‖c‖ * (2 / ‖w - 1‖)) ≤ (c * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ico a (a + N), w ^ n).re

decls.name: sum_block_ge
decls.why: For `T n = Σ_j c_j·z_j^n` real-valued with every `z_j` of modulus one and the coefficient at `z_j = 1` of nonnegative real part, the sum of `T` over any block of consecutive `n` is at least `-Σ_j ‖c_j‖·(2/‖z_j - 1‖)`.
needs: hconst : ∀ j ∈ s, z j = 1 → 0 ≤ (c j).re
hT : ∀ n, (T n : ℂ) = ∑ j ∈ s, c j * z j ^ n
decls.proves: -(∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ * (2 / ‖z j - 1‖)) ≤ ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ico a (a + N), T n

decls.name: abs_le_sum_norm
decls.why: For `T n = Σ_j c_j·z_j^n` real-valued with every `z_j` of modulus one, `|T n|` is at most `Σ_j ‖c_j‖` for every `n`.
needs: hT : ∀ n, (T n : ℂ) = ∑ j ∈ s, c j * z j ^ n

decls.name: sum_sq_block_ge
decls.why: For `T n = Σ_j c_j·z_j^n` real-valued with the `z_j` of modulus one and distinct, the sum of `T²` over a block of `N` consecutive `n` is at least `N·Σ_j ‖c_j‖²` minus the off-diagonal sum `Σ_{j ≠ l} ‖c_j‖·‖c_l‖·(2/‖z_j·conj z_l - 1‖)`.
needs: hT : ∀ n, (T n : ℂ) = ∑ j ∈ s, c j * z j ^ n
decls.proves: (N : ℝ) * ∑ j ∈ s, ‖c j‖ ^ 2 - ∑ j ∈ s, ∑ l ∈ s, (if j = l then 0 else ‖c j‖ * ‖c l‖ * (2 / ‖z j * conj (z l) - 1‖)) ≤ ∑ n ∈ Finset.Ico a (a + N), T n ^ 2

decls.name: exists_large_in_block
decls.why: For `T n = Σ_j c_j·z_j^n` real-valued with the `z_j` of modulus one and distinct, the coefficient at `z_j = 1` of nonnegative real part and some `c_j ≠ 0`, there are `τ > 0` and `N₀` such that every block of `N ≥ N₀` consecutive `n` holds an `n` with `τ ≤ T n`.
needs: hconst : ∀ j ∈ s, z j = 1 → 0 ≤ (c j).re
hT : ∀ n, (T n : ℂ) = ∑ j ∈ s, c j * z j ^ n
decls.proves: ∃ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ ∧ ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ a N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N → ∃ n ∈ Finset.Ico a (a + N), τ ≤ T n

header: LandauWindow — the Landau window criterion as a statement, and what it gives: a one-sided bound on one function of the primes, on long windows, implies Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`. Block 1 of `lean_stage3/design/landau.md`. 2026-11-22.

decls.name: rampSum
decls.why: `Σ_{n ≤ y} Λ(n)·(y/n − 1)`, the von Mangoldt sum against the ramp.

decls.name: G
decls.why: The ramp sum with its main terms removed.

decls.name: WindowBound
decls.why: The hypothesis: `G(y) ≤ C·y^θ` on a window `[Y, Y^(1+δ)]`, for arbitrarily large `Y`.

decls.name: StmtLandauWindow
decls.why: The Landau window criterion, as a statement.

decls.name: zeta_neg_nat_ne_zero
decls.why: `ζ` does not vanish at a nonpositive integer other than a trivial zero.

decls.name: rh_of_zeroFree_half
decls.why: From a zero-free half-plane to the Riemann hypothesis.
needs: h : ∀ s : ℂ, 1 / 2 < s.re → riemannZeta s ≠ 0

decls.name: zeroFree_half_of_window
decls.why: The criterion and a window bound at every `θ` above `1/2` give a zero-free half-plane.
needs: hW : ∀ θ : ℝ, 1 / 2 < θ → θ < 1 → ∃ δ C : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ WindowBound θ δ C

decls.name: rh_of_window
decls.why: The window bound gives the Riemann hypothesis, given the criterion.
needs: hW : ∀ θ : ℝ, 1 / 2 < θ → θ < 1 → ∃ δ C : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ WindowBound θ δ C

header: LandauZeroSide — the zeros' reading of the Taylor coefficients of `Phi`, from below. Block 7b of `lean_stage3/design/landau.md`. 2026-11-22.

decls.name: exists_gap
decls.why: Past the nearest points of a finite set there is a gap.
decls.proves: ∃ R₂ : ℝ, r < R₂ ∧ R₂ ≤ R₃ ∧ ∀ ρ ∈ F, ‖c - ρ‖ < R₂ → ‖c - ρ‖ ≤ r

decls.name: zero_side
decls.why: The zeros' lower bound on the primes' integral. For a zero `ρ₀` of `riemannZeta` and a real `σ₀ > 1` with `‖σ₀ − ρ₀‖ < σ₀`, there are `r, R, τ, C₁, N₀` with `σ₀ − 1 < r ≤ ‖σ₀ − ρ₀‖`, `r < R`, `τ > 0`, `C₁ ≥ 0`, such that every run of at least `N₀` consecutive naturals contains a `k` with `τ/r^(k+1) − C₁/R^k ≤ Ik σ₀ k / k!`.
decls.proves: ∃ r R τ C₁ : ℝ, ∃ N₀ : ℕ, σ₀ - 1 < r ∧ r ≤ ‖(σ₀ : ℂ) - ρ₀‖ ∧ r < R ∧ 0 < τ ∧ 0 ≤ C₁ ∧ ∀ a N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N → ∃ k ∈ Finset.Ico a (a + N), τ / r ^ (k + 1) - C₁ / R ^ k ≤ LandauPrimeSide.Ik σ₀ k / k.factorial

header: LeftKernel — blocks F2a and F2b of `lean_stage3/design/leftedge.md`. 2026-11-23.

decls.name: cpow_tI
decls.why: For `y > 0`, the turning factor `y^(it)` is the exponential `exp(log y · it)`.

decls.name: norm_exp_tI
decls.why: The exponential `exp(L · it)` of a purely imaginary number has norm one.

decls.name: norm_cpow_tI
decls.why: For `y > 0`, the turning factor `y^(it)` has norm one.

decls.name: osc_by_parts
decls.why: Integration by parts against the turning factor. For `y > 1`, `a ≤ b`, and `h` with derivative `h′` on `[a,b]`, `h′` integrable: `‖∫_a^b y^(it)·h(t) dt‖ ≤ (‖h a‖ + ‖h b‖ + ∫_a^b ‖h′‖)/log y`.
needs: hd : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt h (h' t) t
hi : IntervalIntegrable h' volume a b
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in a..b, ((y:ℂ) ^ ((t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) * h t‖ ≤ (‖h a‖ + ‖h b‖ + ∫ t in a..b, ‖h' t‖) / Real.log y

decls.name: kernel_bound
decls.why: F2a, the kernel. For `y > 1`, `T > 0` and real `a ≠ 0`: `‖∫_{−T}^{T} y^(it)/(a+it) dt‖ ≤ (2/T + π/|a|)/log y`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in (-T)..T, ((y:ℂ) ^ ((t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) / ((a:ℂ) + (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ (2 / T + Real.pi / |a|) / Real.log y

decls.name: vmTerm
decls.why: The `n`-th term of the von Mangoldt series at `5/4`: `Λ(n)·n^(−5/4)`.

decls.name: vmTerm_nonneg
decls.why: Each term `Λ(n)·n^(−5/4)` is nonnegative.

decls.name: vmTerm_summable
decls.why: The series `Σ Λ(n)·n^(−5/4)` converges.

decls.name: Bser
decls.why: The series-side constant: `((1 + 4π)/log 16)·Σ' n, Λ(n)·n^(−5/4)`.

decls.name: series_side
decls.why: F2b, the series side. For `16 ≤ x` and `2 ≤ T`, the Dirichlet-series half of the left edge, `∫_{−T}^{T} ζ'/ζ(5/4 − it)·x^(−1/4+it)/(−1/4+it) dt`, has norm at most `Bser·x^(−1/4)`, with `Bser` free of `x` and `T`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in (-T)..T, (deriv riemannZeta ((5/4:ℂ) - (t:ℂ) * Complex.I) / riemannZeta ((5/4:ℂ) - (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) * ((x:ℂ) ^ (((-1/4 : ℝ):ℂ) + (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) / (((-1/4 : ℝ):ℂ) + (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ Bser * x ^ (-(1:ℝ)/4)

header: LeftSmooth — blocks F2c, F2 and F3 of `lean_stage3/design/leftedge.md`. 2026-11-23.

decls.name: arctan_int_le
decls.why: The arctan integral: for `a > 0`, `∫_{−T}^{T} dt/(a²+t²) ≤ π/a`.

decls.name: kernel_conj
decls.why: The conjugate kernel. For `y > 1`, `T ≥ 0`, `c > 0`: `‖∫_{−T}^{T} y^(it)/(c − it) dt‖ ≤ (2 + π)/(c·log y)`; the endpoint terms are bounded by `1/c`, so the bound does not see `T`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in (-T)..T, ((y:ℂ) ^ ((t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) * ((c:ℂ) - (t:ℂ) * Complex.I)⁻¹‖ ≤ (2 + Real.pi) / (c * Real.log y)

decls.name: cos_sq_le_norm_cos
decls.why: The squared norm of `cos(a + ib)` is at least `cos²a + b²` (it equals `cos²a + sinh²b`).

decls.name: cos_sq_mul_norm_sin_le
decls.why: `cos²a·‖sin(a + ib)‖² ≤ ‖cos(a + ib)‖²`; so `‖tan(a+ib)‖ ≤ 1/|cos a|`.

decls.name: Gs
decls.why: The smooth factor of the functional equation, as a function of `w = 1 − s`: `G(w) = log 2π − ψ(w) + (π/2)·tan(πw/2)`, with `ψ` the digamma function.

decls.name: logDeriv_sum
decls.why: The logarithmic derivative of the functional equation. For `Re w > 1` with `cos(πw/2) ≠ 0`: `ζ(1−w) ≠ 0` and `ζ′/ζ(1−w) + ζ′/ζ(w) = G(w)`.
decls.proves: riemannZeta (1 - w) ≠ 0 ∧ deriv riemannZeta (1 - w) / riemannZeta (1 - w) + deriv riemannZeta w / riemannZeta w = Gs w

decls.name: sL
decls.why: The point `s = −1/4 + it` of the left line.

decls.name: wL
decls.why: The reflected point `w = 5/4 − it = 1 − s`.

decls.name: one_sub_wL
decls.why: `1 − w = s` on the line.

decls.name: norm_sL_sq
decls.why: `‖s‖² = 1/16 + t²` on the line.

decls.name: norm_sL_ge
decls.why: `‖s‖ ≥ 1/4` on the line.

decls.name: sL_ne
decls.why: `s ≠ 0` on the line.

decls.name: arg_wL
decls.why: The tangent's argument on the line: `πw/2 = 5π/8 − i·πt/2`.
decls.proves: (Real.pi:ℂ) * wL t / 2 = ((5 * Real.pi / 8 : ℝ):ℂ) + ((-(Real.pi * t / 2)) : ℝ) * Complex.I

decls.name: kc
decls.why: The cosine constant `κ = |cos(5π/8)|`.

decls.name: norm_cos_wL
decls.why: `‖cos(πw/2)‖² ≥ κ² + t²` on the line.

decls.name: cos_wL_ne
decls.why: `cos(πw/2) ≠ 0` on the line.

decls.name: norm_tan_wL
decls.why: `‖tan(πw/2)‖ ≤ 1/κ` on the line.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_wL
decls.why: `t ↦ w(t)` has derivative `−i`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_sL
decls.why: `t ↦ s(t)` has derivative `i`.

decls.name: continuous_sL
decls.why: `t ↦ s(t)` is continuous.

decls.name: continuous_wL
decls.why: `t ↦ w(t)` is continuous.

decls.name: tanPiece
decls.why: The tangent piece `tan(πw/2)/s` along the line.

decls.name: tanPiece'
decls.why: The derivative of the tangent piece.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_tanPiece
decls.why: The tangent piece has derivative `tanPiece'`.

decls.name: continuous_tan_wL
decls.why: The tangent along the line is continuous.
decls.proves: Continuous fun t : ℝ => Complex.tan ((Real.pi:ℂ) * wL t / 2)

decls.name: continuous_tanPiece'
decls.why: The derivative of the tangent piece is continuous.

decls.name: norm_tanPiece'_le
decls.why: The pointwise bound on the derivative of the tangent piece: `‖h′(t)‖ ≤ 2π/(κ²+t²) + (1/κ)/((1/4)²+t²)`.

decls.name: tan_piece
decls.why: The tangent piece by parts. For `y > 1` and `T ≥ 0`: `‖∫_{−T}^{T} y^(it)·tan(πw/2)/s dt‖ ≤ (8 + 2π² + 4π)/(κ·log y)`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in (-T)..T, ((y:ℂ) ^ ((t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) * tanPiece t‖ ≤ (8 + 2 * Real.pi ^ 2 + 4 * Real.pi) / (kc * Real.log y)

decls.name: dgTerm
decls.why: The digamma-series weight `1/((n+1)(n+5/4))`.

decls.name: dgTerm_nonneg
decls.why: Each weight `1/((n+1)(n+5/4))` is nonnegative.

decls.name: dgTerm_summable
decls.why: The weights `1/((n+1)(n+5/4))` are summable.

decls.name: continuous_digamma_wL

decls.name: continuous_cpow_tI
decls.why: `y^(it)` is continuous in `t` for `y > 0`.

decls.name: digamma_piece
decls.why: The digamma piece by the series. For `y > 1` and `T ≥ 0`: `‖∫_{−T}^{T} y^(it)·(−ψ(w) − γ)/s dt‖ ≤ (Σ' 1/((n+1)(n+5/4)))·(2+π)/log y`. Termwise, `(−ψ(w) − γ)/s = Σ 1/((n+1)(n+w))` since `w − 1 = −s`, and each term is the conjugate kernel.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in (-T)..T, ((y:ℂ) ^ ((t:ℂ) * Complex.I)) * ((-Complex.digamma (wL t) - (Real.eulerMascheroniConstant:ℂ)) * (sL t)⁻¹)‖ ≤ (∑' n : ℕ, dgTerm n) * ((2 + Real.pi) / Real.log y)

decls.name: continuous_tanPiece
decls.why: The tangent piece is continuous.

decls.name: cpow_sL
decls.why: On the line, `x^s = x^(−1/4)·x^(it)` for `x > 0`.

decls.name: c0
decls.why: The constant of the smooth factor's flat part: `log 2π + γ`.

decls.name: Nsm
decls.why: The numerator of the smooth-side constant: `‖log 2π + γ‖·(1+4π) + (Σ' 1/((n+1)(n+5/4)))·(2+π) + (π/2)·(8+2π²+4π)/κ`.

decls.name: Nsm_nonneg
decls.why: The numerator `Nsm` is nonnegative.

decls.name: Bsm
decls.why: The smooth-side constant `Bsm = Nsm / log 16`, free of `x` and `T`.

decls.name: smooth_side
decls.why: F2c, the smooth side. For `16 ≤ x` and `2 ≤ T`, with `s = −1/4 + it` and `w = 5/4 − it`, the integral of `(ζ′/ζ(s) + ζ′/ζ(w))·x^s/s` over `[−T, T]` has norm at most `Bsm·x^(−1/4)`. Inside, the sum of the two logarithmic derivatives is `log 2π − ψ(w) + (π/2)·tan(πw/2)`, and each of its three parts is integrated by parts against `x^(it)` (the digamma part termwise through its series).

decls.name: continuous_logDeriv_path

decls.name: explicit_formula_all

header: MirrorArea — block S1 of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. A mode of the table at base `b` and its mirror, read as the two sides of a rectangle. The sides are `‖b^ρ‖` and `‖b^(1−ρ)‖`. Their product is `b` for every `ρ`: the area is fixed by the base and by nothing else. So one side gives the other at every scale. The rectangle is a square, each side `√b`, exactly when `ρ` is on the line; off the line one side is longer than `√b`. The restoring force of block T4 is the logarithm of the ratio of the sides.
