header: OneChain — block J4 of `lean_stage3/design/closedloop.md`. 2026-11-23. The capstone: Julian's closed loop tied to the tree's main theorems, so that the loop and the tree are one chain of theorems.

decls.name: spiralLink_iff_cells
decls.why: The loop and the table. The spiral link holds exactly when every cell of every dyadic ladder stays at square-root size: a statement about the count of primes with no zero in it.
decls.proves: SpiralLink.SpiralLink ↔ ∃ (C : ℝ) (r₀ : ℤ), CellResidual.CellsSqrt C r₀

decls.name: one_chain
decls.why: One chain. The Riemann hypothesis, the spiral link, one zero at each height, the restoring force at rest at every zero, and every cell of every dyadic ladder at square-root size are one statement.
decls.proves: (RiemannHypothesis ↔ SpiralLink.SpiralLink) ∧ (SpiralLink.SpiralLink ↔ OneAtEachHeight) ∧ (SpiralLink.SpiralLink ↔ ∀ ρ : NontrivialZeros, restoringForce (ρ : ℂ).re = 0) ∧ (SpiralLink.SpiralLink ↔ ∃ (C : ℝ) (r₀ : ℤ), CellResidual.CellsSqrt C r₀)

decls.name: table_of_spiralLink
decls.why: From the loop to the integer table. If the spiral link holds, every cell of the integer table stays within square-root size of the smooth cell.
decls.proves: ∃ (C : ℝ) (r₀ : ℤ), ∀ (d : ℕ) (r : ℤ), r₀ + ((d + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ r → |((Construction.tableFrom TableRoute.rowN r d : ℤ) : ℝ) - Nonvanishing.stencilR (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => Stage3.Li ((2 : ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) r| ≤ C * CellResidual.cellSize r d

decls.name: spiralLink_of_finite
decls.why: From the count's ladder to the loop, finitely many zeros off the line.
needs: hF : ∀ ρ : NontrivialZeros, (ρ : ℂ).re ≠ 1 / 2 → ρ ∈ F
hrows : ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in Filter.atTop, |(Nat.primeCounting ⌊(2:ℝ) ^ r⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li ((2:ℝ) ^ r)| ≤ C * (r : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ r

decls.name: spiralLink_of_attained
decls.why: From the count's ladder to the loop, a largest real part attained.
needs: hrows : ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in Filter.atTop, |(Nat.primeCounting ⌊(2:ℝ) ^ r⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li ((2:ℝ) ^ r)| ≤ C * (r : ℝ) ^ 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ r

decls.name: spiralLink_of_attained_psi
decls.why: From ψ's ladder to the loop, a largest real part attained.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖(Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ)^k) : ℂ) - (((2:ℝ)^k : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k

decls.name: spiralLink_of_finite_accumulation
decls.why: From ψ's ladder to the loop, modes accumulating at finitely many points.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ‖(Chebyshev.psi ((2:ℝ)^k) : ℂ) - (((2:ℝ)^k : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k

hfin : ∀ σ : ℝ, 1/2 < σ → ∃ P : Finset ℂ, (∀ p ∈ P, p ≠ 0) ∧ (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → {z : ℂ | ∃ ρ : NontrivialZeros, σ ≤ (ρ : ℂ).re ∧ (2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ) = z ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, ε ≤ ‖z - p‖}.Finite) ∧ (∀ ρ : NontrivialZeros, σ < (ρ : ℂ).re → (2:ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ) ∉ P)

decls.name: no_exposed_zero
decls.why: The count's ladder excludes an exposed zero. Under the square-root bound on the count at the doublings there is an exponent below the bound on the real parts such that no zero right of it has its mode strictly outside a disc, centred on the ray opposite to it, that holds the mode of every other zero right of the line.
needs: hH : ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → |(Nat.primeCounting ⌊(2:ℝ)^k⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li ((2:ℝ)^k)| ≤ C * (k:ℝ)^2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ k
decls.proves: ∃ E : ℝ, σ ≤ E ∧ E < Θ ∧ ∀ (ρ₁ : NontrivialZeros), E < (ρ₁:ℂ).re → ∀ κ r₀ : ℝ, 0 ≤ κ → r₀ < ‖(2:ℂ)^(ρ₁:ℂ)‖ + κ → (∀ ρ : NontrivialZeros, σ ≤ (ρ:ℂ).re → (2:ℂ)^(ρ:ℂ) ≠ (2:ℂ)^(ρ₁:ℂ) → ‖(2:ℂ)^(ρ:ℂ) + (κ:ℂ) * ((2:ℂ)^(ρ₁:ℂ) / ‖(2:ℂ)^(ρ₁:ℂ)‖)‖ ≤ r₀) → False

header: PerfectFit — block R14 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`. 2026-11-24. Julian, 2026-11-24: the harmonic of the integers absorbs the primes' signs as a perfect fit. For the counts it is exact: at every `N`, the counts `⌊N/k⌋` of the integers with nothing missing, signed by `μ(k)`, add up to exactly one.

decls.name: perfect_fit
decls.why: The perfect fit. The counts of the integers at every scale, signed by the Möbius function, add up to exactly one.
decls.proves: ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 N, ((moebius k : ℤ) : ℝ) * ((N / k : ℕ) : ℝ) = 1

header: # Slice 1a — the truncated Perron kernel bound (hEF's entry point) COMPLETE, 2026-08-29: every branch proved, no sorry. `perron_kernel_truncated` sits at `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. (Build order: entry 257; ledger: CONTEXT.md § hEF, roadmap D. This was hEF's load-bearing unknown — the piece both MediumPNT and StrongPNT were designed to avoid.)

decls.name: perronI
decls.why: The truncated Perron integral `(2πi)⁻¹ ∫_{c-iT}^{c+iT} y^s/s ds`, parametrised on the vertical segment.

decls.name: perronδ
decls.why: The target of the kernel: the indicator of `1 < y`.

decls.name: perronI_eq_VIntegral'
decls.why: `perronI` is PNT+'s right-edge `VIntegral'` of the kernel.
decls.proves: perronI y c T = VIntegral' (fun s : ℂ ↦ (y : ℂ) ^ s / s) c (-T) T

decls.name: kernel_holo
decls.why: The kernel is holomorphic on the open right half-plane.
decls.proves: HolomorphicOn (fun s : ℂ ↦ (y : ℂ) ^ s / s) {s : ℂ | 0 < s.re}

decls.name: rect_subset_right
decls.why: A rectangle with left edge at `c > 0` sits in the right half-plane.
decls.proves: Rectangle ((c : ℂ) - Complex.I * T) ((X : ℂ) + Complex.I * T) ⊆ {s : ℂ | 0 < s.re}

decls.name: perron_kernel_coarse_lt
decls.why: K1, case `y < 1`. A single finite rectangle of width `T`: crude endpoint bounds on all three far edges give `(2/π)·y^c` — no limits.
decls.proves: ‖perronI y c T - perronδ y‖ ≤ y ^ c

decls.name: horiz_bound
decls.why: The shared horizontal-edge estimate: along `Im s = T'` with `|T'| ≥ 1`, the kernel's horizontal integral is controlled by the endpoint powers over `|T'|·|log y|`. Every rectangle in both decay cases consumes this.
decls.proves: ‖∫ σ in a..b, (y : ℂ) ^ ((σ : ℂ) + (T' : ℂ) * Complex.I) / ((σ : ℂ) + (T' : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ max (y ^ a) (y ^ b) / (|T'| * |Real.log y|)

decls.name: perron_kernel_decay_lt
decls.why: K2, case `y < 1`. No pole; rectangles to `+∞` along the naturals, `horiz_bound` on both edges, the far vertical vanishes in the limit.
decls.proves: ‖perronI y c T - perronδ y‖ ≤ y ^ c / (T * |Real.log y|)

decls.name: dslope_kernel_diff
decls.why: The kernel's regular part at the pole: `dslope` of `y^s` at `0` is entire.
decls.proves: Differentiable ℂ (dslope (fun s : ℂ ↦ (y : ℂ) ^ s) 0)

decls.name: rect_residue
decls.why: The pole, crossed once: the rectangle boundary integral of the kernel around `0` is `1` after `(2πi)⁻¹` normalisation.
decls.proves: RectangleIntegral' (fun s : ℂ ↦ (y : ℂ) ^ s / s) (-(X:ℂ) - Complex.I * T) ((c:ℂ) + Complex.I * T) = 1

decls.name: perron_kernel_decay_gt
decls.why: K2, case `y > 1`. The rectangle to `−∞` collects the residue `1 = perronδ y`; `horiz_bound` on both edges, far vertical dies.
decls.proves: ‖perronI y c T - perronδ y‖ ≤ y ^ c / (T * |Real.log y|)

decls.name: perron_kernel_decay
decls.why: K2 — the decay branch, assembled from its two cases.
decls.proves: ‖perronI y c T - perronδ y‖ ≤ y ^ c / (T * |Real.log y|)

decls.name: coarse_gt_ineq
decls.why: The elementary two-variable inequality behind K1's `y > 1` case, in multiplied (division-free) form: for `u = c·log y > 0`, `v = T·log y ∈ (0,1]`, `v·e^u + π − arctan(v/u) ≤ π·e^u`.
decls.proves: v * Real.exp u + Real.pi - Real.arctan (v / u) ≤ Real.pi * Real.exp u

decls.name: seg_inv_integral
decls.why: The segment integral of `1/s`: pure real calculus — the odd part cancels by its antiderivative, the even part is the arctan derivative.
decls.proves: (∫ t in (-T)..T, ((c : ℂ) + Complex.I * t)⁻¹ * Complex.I) = 2 * Real.arctan (T / c) * Complex.I

decls.name: cpow_sub_one_bound
decls.why: Mean-value bound: `‖y^s − 1‖ ≤ ‖s‖·log y·y^(re s)` for `y > 1`.
decls.proves: ‖(y : ℂ) ^ s - 1‖ ≤ ‖s‖ * Real.log y * y ^ s.re

decls.name: perron_kernel_coarse_gt
decls.why: K1, case `y > 1`. For `T·log y ≥ 1` this is the decay branch; below that, split off the exact `∫ ds/s`, mean-value the rest, and close with `coarse_gt_ineq`.
decls.proves: ‖perronI y c T - perronδ y‖ ≤ y ^ c

decls.name: perron_kernel_coarse
decls.why: K1 — the coarse branch, assembled from its two cases.
decls.proves: ‖perronI y c T - perronδ y‖ ≤ y ^ c

decls.name: perron_kernel_truncated
decls.why: Slice 1a — the truncated Perron kernel bound. Assembled from K1 and K2; the two branches are the whole of the missing mathematics.
decls.proves: ‖perronI y c T - perronδ y‖ ≤ y ^ c * min 1 (1 / (T * |Real.log y|))

decls.name: one_sub_two_neg_rpow
decls.why: Geometric-denominator bound: `δ/5 ≤ 1 − 2^(−δ)` for `0 < δ ≤ 1`.

decls.name: vonMangoldt_rpow_partial
decls.why: The dyadic partial-sum bound: any finite piece of `Σ Λ(n)·n^(−c)` sits under `2(log 4 + 4)/(1 − 2^(1−c))`.
decls.proves: ∑ n ∈ s, ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n * (n : ℝ) ^ (-c) ≤ 2 * (Real.log 4 + 4) / (1 - (2:ℝ) ^ (1 - c))

decls.name: vonMangoldt_rpow_tsum
decls.why: The full sum, as a tsum.
decls.proves: ∑' n : ℕ, ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n * (n : ℝ) ^ (-c) ≤ 2 * (Real.log 4 + 4) / (1 - (2:ℝ) ^ (1 - c))

decls.name: vonMangoldt_rpow_summable
decls.why: For `c > 1`, the series of `Λ(n)·n^(−c)` over the natural numbers is summable.
decls.proves: Summable (fun n : ℕ ↦ ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n * (n : ℝ) ^ (-c))

decls.name: far_terms_sum
decls.why: Slice 1b — the far-terms sum.
decls.proves: (∑' n : ℕ, if 1/2 ≤ |Real.log (x / n)| then ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n * (x / n) ^ (1 + 1/Real.log x) / (T * |Real.log (x / n)|) else 0) ≤ 300 * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T

decls.name: near_diagonal_sum
decls.why: Slice 1c — the near-diagonal sum.
decls.proves: (∑' n : ℕ, if 0 < |Real.log (x / n)| ∧ |Real.log (x / n)| < 1/2 then ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n * min 1 (1/(T * |Real.log (x / n)|)) else 0) ≤ 100 * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T + 4 * Real.log x

decls.name: perronI_one_norm
decls.why: The kernel at `y = 1`, directly: `‖perronI 1 c T‖ ≤ 1/2`.

decls.name: kernel_sum_bound
decls.why: Slice 1's analytic composition. The summed kernel error.
decls.proves: ‖(∑' n : ℕ, (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * (perronI (x/n) (1 + 1/Real.log x) T - perronδ (x/n)))‖ ≤ 600 * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T + 12 * Real.log x

decls.name: delta_sum_close
decls.why: The δ-side of the composition: the indicator sum is `ψ` up to one von Mangoldt value at the possible integer point.
decls.proves: ‖(Chebyshev.psi x : ℂ) - ∑' n : ℕ, (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * perronδ (x / n)‖ ≤ Real.log x

decls.name: kernel_diff_summable
decls.why: Summability of the kernel differences, via the crude majorant `Λ(n)·(x/n)^c` — sharp enough for convergence, everywhere.
decls.proves: Summable (fun n : ℕ ↦ (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * (perronI (x/n) (1 + 1/Real.log x) T - perronδ (x/n)))

decls.name: perron_to_psi
decls.why: Slice 1 — the Perron-to-ψ bound. The truncated Perron sum of the von Mangoldt function misses `ψ` by at most `600·x·log(xT)²/T + 13·log x`.
decls.proves: ‖(Chebyshev.psi x : ℂ) - ∑' n : ℕ, (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * perronI (x/n) (1 + 1/Real.log x) T‖ ≤ 600 * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T + 13 * Real.log x

decls.name: tsum_vonMangoldt_div_cpow
decls.why: The Dirichlet-series identity under the integral: at `re s = c > 1`, `Σ Λ(n)·(x/n)^s = (−ζ′/ζ)(s)·x^s`.
decls.proves: (∑' n : ℕ, (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * ((x / n : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ s) = (- deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s) * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ s

decls.name: perron_sum_eq_integral
decls.why: The Fubini. The kernel sum IS the truncated `−ζ′/ζ` contour integral.
decls.proves: (∑' n : ℕ, (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * perronI (x/n) (1 + 1/Real.log x) T) = (2 * (Real.pi:ℂ) * Complex.I)⁻¹ * ∫ t in (-T)..T, (- deriv riemannZeta (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) / riemannZeta (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t)) * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) / (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) * Complex.I

decls.name: explicit_formula_perron
decls.why: hEF, Perron form — the truncated explicit formula at the line `re = c`. `ψ` misses the truncated `−ζ′/ζ` integral by `600·x·log(xT)²/T + 13·log x`.
decls.proves: ‖(Chebyshev.psi x : ℂ) - (2 * (Real.pi:ℂ) * Complex.I)⁻¹ * ∫ t in (-T)..T, (- deriv riemannZeta (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) / riemannZeta (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t)) * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) / (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) * Complex.I‖ ≤ 600 * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T + 13 * Real.log x

header: PerronTwo — block G1 of `lean_stage3/design/floor.md`. 2026-11-23. `PerronKernel.explicit_formula_perron` with the floor lowered from `16 ≤ x` to `2 ≤ x`. Every `x`-free helper of `PerronKernel` is reused unchanged; the lemmas below are copies of the originals with the lines that used the floor rewritten. `PerronKernel.lean` is untouched.

decls.name: one_sub_two_neg_rpow'
decls.why: Geometric-denominator bound on the wider range: `δ/5 ≤ 1 − 2^(−δ)` for `0 < δ ≤ 5/2`. Below `1` it is `PerronKernel.one_sub_two_neg_rpow`; above, `2^(−δ) ≤ 1/2`.

decls.name: inv_log_le_of_two_le
decls.why: `1/log x ≤ 3/2` from `x ≥ 2` (`1/log 2 < 3/2`): the abscissa `c = 1 + 1/log x` sits at most `5/2`.

decls.name: far_terms_sum_two
decls.why: Slice 1b from `x = 2` — the far-terms sum. The terms with `|log(x/n)| ≥ 1/2` sum to at most `300·x·log(xT)²/T`, for `x ≥ 2`, `T ≥ 2`.
decls.proves: (∑' n : ℕ, if 1/2 ≤ |Real.log (x / n)| then ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n * (x / n) ^ (1 + 1/Real.log x) / (T * |Real.log (x / n)|) else 0) ≤ 300 * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T

decls.name: near_diagonal_sum_two
decls.why: Slice 1c from `x = 2` — the near-diagonal sum. The terms with `0 < |log(x/n)| < 1/2`, each weighted by `min(1, 1/(T·|log(x/n)|))`, sum to at most `100·x·log(xT)²/T + 4·log x`, for `x ≥ 2`.
decls.proves: (∑' n : ℕ, if 0 < |Real.log (x / n)| ∧ |Real.log (x / n)| < 1/2 then ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n * min 1 (1/(T * |Real.log (x / n)|)) else 0) ≤ 100 * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T + 4 * Real.log x

decls.name: kernel_sum_bound_two
decls.why: Slice 1's analytic composition from `x = 2`. The summed kernel error `‖Σ Λ(n)·(perronI(x/n) − δ(x/n))‖` is at most `700·x·log(xT)²/T + 17·log x`, for `x ≥ 2`, `T ≥ 2`. The near-diagonal factor is `(x/n)^c ≤ e^(5/4) ≤ 4`.
decls.proves: ‖(∑' n : ℕ, (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * (perronI (x/n) (1 + 1/Real.log x) T - perronδ (x/n)))‖ ≤ 700 * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T + 17 * Real.log x

decls.name: delta_sum_close_two
decls.why: The δ-side of the composition from `x > 1`: the indicator sum is `ψ` up to one von Mangoldt value at the possible integer point.
decls.proves: ‖(Chebyshev.psi x : ℂ) - ∑' n : ℕ, (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * perronδ (x / n)‖ ≤ Real.log x

decls.name: kernel_diff_summable_two
decls.why: Summability of the kernel differences from `x > 1`, via the crude majorant `Λ(n)·(x/n)^c` — sharp enough for convergence, everywhere.
decls.proves: Summable (fun n : ℕ ↦ (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * (perronI (x/n) (1 + 1/Real.log x) T - perronδ (x/n)))

decls.name: perron_to_psi_two
decls.why: Slice 1 from `x = 2` — the Perron-to-ψ bound. The truncated Perron sum of the von Mangoldt function misses `ψ` by at most `700·x·log(xT)²/T + 18·log x`, for `x ≥ 2`, `T ≥ 2`.
decls.proves: ‖(Chebyshev.psi x : ℂ) - ∑' n : ℕ, (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * perronI (x/n) (1 + 1/Real.log x) T‖ ≤ 700 * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T + 18 * Real.log x

decls.name: perron_sum_eq_integral_two
decls.why: The Fubini from `x > 1`. The kernel sum is the truncated `−ζ′/ζ` contour integral on the line `re s = 1 + 1/log x`.
decls.proves: (∑' n : ℕ, (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ) * perronI (x/n) (1 + 1/Real.log x) T) = (2 * (Real.pi:ℂ) * Complex.I)⁻¹ * ∫ t in (-T)..T, (- deriv riemannZeta (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) / riemannZeta (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t)) * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) / (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) * Complex.I

decls.name: explicit_formula_perron_two
decls.why: hEF, Perron form from `x = 2` — the truncated explicit formula at the line `re = c`, `c = 1 + 1/log x`. For `x ≥ 2`, `T ≥ 2`, `ψ` misses the truncated `−ζ′/ζ` integral by at most `700·x·log(xT)²/T + 18·log x`.
decls.proves: ‖(Chebyshev.psi x : ℂ) - (2 * (Real.pi:ℂ) * Complex.I)⁻¹ * ∫ t in (-T)..T, (- deriv riemannZeta (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) / riemannZeta (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t)) * ((x:ℝ):ℂ) ^ (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) / (((1 + 1/Real.log x : ℝ):ℂ) + Complex.I * t) * Complex.I‖ ≤ 700 * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T + 18 * Real.log x

header: PiFixedRow — block F4 of `lean_stage3/design/leftedge.md`. 2026-11-23. The integer count at a fixed `x` with the height of the zero sum taken to infinity. `PiZeros.pi_eq_zero_sum` is an identity at every height; what has to be bounded free of the height is `tr (efRem T) x`, the passage of the explicit formula's remainder. Above `16` the explicit formula at every height does it. On `[2, 16]` each zero is integrated by parts in `t`, which gains a factor `1/|ρ+1|`, and the zeros weighted by `m/|ρ|²` have a sum bounded…

decls.name: sum_sq_div_pow_eq
decls.why: The closed form behind `Σ_j (j+2)²/2^j ≤ 22`: the partial sum plus a vanishing tail is exactly `22`.

decls.name: sum_sq_div_pow_le
decls.why: The partial sums of `(j+2)²/2^j` are at most `22`.

decls.name: zinv_dyadic_le
decls.why: The sum of `m(ρ)/|ρ|` over the zeros below `2^(j+1)` is at most `Mlow·3000·(j+2)²`.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ ZF ((2 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1)), ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) * ‖(ρ : ℂ)‖⁻¹ ≤ Mlow * (3000 * ((j : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2)

decls.name: Z2
decls.why: The constant bounding the zeros weighted by `m/|ρ|²`: `66000·Mlow²`.

decls.name: Z2_nonneg
decls.why: The constant `Z2` is nonnegative.

decls.name: sum_order_inv_sq_le
decls.why: The zeros weighted by `m/|ρ|²` are bounded free of the height. For every `T`, the sum over the zeros below `T` of `m(ρ)·(1/|ρ|)²` is at most `Z2`.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) * (‖(ρ : ℂ)‖⁻¹) ^ 2 ≤ Z2

decls.name: w
decls.why: The weight `1/(t·log²t)` as a real function.

decls.name: wd
decls.why: The derivative of the real weight: `−(log t + 2)/(t²·log³t)`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_w
decls.why: For `t > 1` the real weight has derivative `wd t`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_wt
decls.why: For `t > 1` the weight, read as complex, has derivative `wd t`.
decls.proves: HasDerivAt wt ((wd t : ℝ) : ℂ) t

decls.name: continuousOn_wd
decls.why: On `[2, 16]` the derivative of the weight is continuous.

decls.name: w_le_two
decls.why: For `t ≥ 2` the weight is at most `2`.

decls.name: w_pos
decls.why: For `t ≥ 2` the weight is positive.

decls.name: abs_wd_le
decls.why: On `[2, 16]` the derivative of the weight is at most `4` in size.

decls.name: norm_le_norm_add_one
decls.why: For `ρ` with `0 < Re ρ`, `|ρ| ≤ |ρ + 1|`.

decls.name: norm_integral_cpow_wt_le
decls.why: One zero on `[2, 16]`, integrated by parts. For `0 < Re ρ < 1`, the integral of `t^ρ` against the weight over `[2, 16]` is at most `15360/|ρ + 1|`.

decls.name: norm_zero_term_le
decls.why: One zero's term on `[2, 16]`: for `0 < Re ρ < 1`, the integral of `t^ρ/ρ` against the weight is at most `15360/|ρ|²`.

decls.name: Clow
decls.why: The constant bounding the low integral: `294 + 15360·Z2`.

decls.name: Clow_nonneg
decls.why: The constant `Clow` is nonnegative.

decls.name: norm_low_integral_le
decls.why: The low integral is bounded free of the height. For every `T`, the integral of the explicit formula's remainder against the weight over `[2, 16]` is at most `Clow`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in (2:ℝ)..16, efRem T t * wt t‖ ≤ Clow

decls.name: Api
decls.why: The constant of the count at a fixed row: `2·(c3n + Bleft) + Clow`.

decls.name: Api_nonneg
decls.why: The constant `Api` is nonnegative.

decls.name: one_le_log_of_16
decls.why: For `x ≥ 16`, `log x ≥ 1`.

decls.name: norm_high_integral_le
decls.why: The high integral at a fixed height. For `16 ≤ x` and `T ≥ 2`, the integral of the remainder against the weight over `[16, x]` is at most `c1n·(x − 16)·log²(xT)/T + (c3n + Bleft)·log(x/16)`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ t in (16:ℝ)..x, efRem T t * wt t‖ ≤ (x - 16) * (Glue.c1n * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T) + (Glue.c3n + LeftSmooth.Bleft) * Real.log (x / 16)

decls.name: norm_tr_efRem_le_height
decls.why: The passage of the remainder at a fixed row and a finite height. For `16 ≤ x` and `T ≥ 2`, `‖tr (efRem T) x‖ ≤ Api·log x + 2·c1n·x·log²(xT)/T`.
decls.proves: ‖tr (efRem T) x‖ ≤ Api * Real.log x + 2 * Glue.c1n * x * Real.log (x * T) ^ 2 / T

decls.name: tr_efRem_fixed
decls.why: The passage of the remainder at a fixed row, the height to infinity. For `16 ≤ x` and every `ε > 0`, for all large heights `T`, `‖tr (efRem T) x‖ ≤ Api·log x + ε`.
decls.proves: ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in Filter.atTop, ‖tr (efRem T) x‖ ≤ Api * Real.log x + ε

decls.name: pi_fixed_row
decls.why: The count at a fixed row, the height to infinity. For `16 ≤ x` and every `ε > 0`, for all large heights `T`, the count minus `Li`, plus each zero's part below `T`, plus the higher prime powers, is at most `Api·log x + ε`.
decls.proves: ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in Filter.atTop, ‖(((Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li x : ℝ) : ℂ) + ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * piMode (ρ : ℂ) x + tr psiTheta x‖ ≤ Api * Real.log x + ε

decls.name: table_cell_fixed_row
decls.why: The integer table's cell at a fixed row, the height to infinity. For `d + 6 ≤ r` and every `ε > 0`, for all large heights `T`, the cell `(r, d)` of the table of the prime count along the doublings, less the smooth cell, plus each zero's part below `T` under the stencil, plus the stencil of the higher prime powers, is at most `2^(d+1)·(Api·log 2·r) + ε`.
decls.proves: ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in Filter.atTop, ‖((((Construction.tableFrom TableRoute.rowN (r : ℤ) d : ℤ) : ℝ) - Nonvanishing.stencilR (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => Stage3.Li ((2 : ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) (r : ℤ) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * CellZeros.stencil (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => piMode (ρ : ℂ) ((2:ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) (r : ℤ) + CellZeros.stencil (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => tr psiTheta ((2:ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) (r : ℤ)‖ ≤ 2 ^ (d + 1) * (Api * Real.log 2 * r) + ε

header: PiRemainder — block T2b of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-23. The passage of the explicit formula's remainder is of square-root size, with no hypothesis on the zeros. Take the height equal to `x` and split the integral in `tr (efRem x) x` at `√x`. Above `√x` the explicit formula holds and bounds the remainder by a constant times `log²x`; against the weight this is at most a constant times `√x`. Below `√x` the remainder is at most `(7 + W)·t`, where `W` is the sum of `m(ρ)/|ρ|` over the zeros below `x`; aga…

decls.name: Mlow
decls.why: A constant that is at least `2` and at least the reciprocal size of every zero of height below one.

decls.name: two_le_Mlow
decls.why: The constant `Mlow` is at least `2`.

decls.name: inv_norm_le_Mlow
decls.why: A zero of height below one has reciprocal size at most `Mlow`.

decls.name: inv_norm_le_dyadic
decls.why: Any zero below `2^(K+1)` has reciprocal size at most `Mlow` times the dyadic weights.
decls.proves: ‖(ρ : ℂ)‖⁻¹ ≤ Mlow * ∑ j ∈ range (K + 1), ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)⁻¹ * (if |(ρ : ℂ).im| < 2 ^ (j + 1) then 1 else 0)

decls.name: sum_order_inv_le
decls.why: All the zeros, weighted by reciprocal size, below a height. The sum of `m(ρ)/|ρ|` over the zeros below `2^(K+1)` is at most `Mlow` times the dyadic count.
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ ZF ((2 : ℝ) ^ (K + 1)), ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) * ‖(ρ : ℂ)‖⁻¹ ≤ Mlow * ∑ j ∈ range (K + 1), ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)⁻¹ * (2 * |riemannZeta.N ((2 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1))| + weightedZeroHeightBucket)

decls.name: zinv
decls.why: The sum of `m(ρ)/|ρ|` over the zeros below a height.

decls.name: zinv_nonneg
decls.why: The sum `zinv T` is nonnegative.

decls.name: zinv_le_log
decls.why: The zeros below `x`, weighted by reciprocal size, are at most a constant times `log²x`. For `x ≥ 4` the constant is `39000·Mlow`.

decls.name: norm_zeroPartialSum_le
decls.why: For `t ≥ 1` the zero sum below any height is at most `t` times `zinv` of that height.

decls.name: norm_psi_sub_le
decls.why: For `t ≥ 0`, Chebyshev's bound gives `|ψ t − t| ≤ 7·t`.

decls.name: norm_efRem_le_low
decls.why: The remainder below the explicit formula's range. For `t ≥ 1` the remainder at any height `T` is at most `(7 + zinv T)·t`.

decls.name: Chigh
decls.why: The constant of the remainder inside the explicit formula's range.

decls.name: Chigh_nonneg
decls.why: The constant `Chigh` is nonnegative.

decls.name: norm_efRem_le_high
decls.why: The remainder inside the explicit formula's range. For `16 ≤ t ≤ x ≤ t²` and `log x ≥ 1`, the remainder at height `x` is at most `Chigh·log²x`.

decls.name: integrable_efRem
decls.why: For `x ≥ 2` the remainder of the explicit formula at any height is integrable on `[2, x]`.

decls.name: Arem
decls.why: The constant of the main bound.

decls.name: Arem_nonneg
decls.why: The constant `Arem` is nonnegative.

decls.name: norm_tr_efRem_le_of
decls.why: The passage of the remainder is of square-root size, explicitly. For `x ≥ 256`, with the height equal to `x`, the passage of the explicit formula's remainder is at most `Arem·√x·log²x`.
decls.proves: ‖tr (efRem x) x‖ ≤ Arem * Real.sqrt x * Real.log x ^ 2

decls.name: norm_tr_efRem_le
decls.why: The passage of the explicit formula's remainder is of square-root size. There are constants `A ≥ 0` and `x₀` such that for every `x ≥ x₀`, with the height equal to `x`, the passage of the remainder is at most `A·√x·log²x`. No hypothesis on the zeros of ζ is made.
decls.proves: ∃ A x₀ : ℝ, 0 ≤ A ∧ ∀ x : ℝ, x₀ ≤ x → ‖PiZeros.tr (PiZeros.efRem x) x‖ ≤ A * Real.sqrt x * Real.log x ^ 2

header: PiToPsi — block T5 of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`, first part. 2026-11-22. From the count `π` back to `ψ`. `PsiToPi` carries a bound on `ψ` to a bound on `π − Li`; this module carries it back, by upstream's Abel summation `Chebyshev.theta_eq_primeCounting_mul_log_sub_integral` and the matching identity for `Li`. With `VonKoch.RH_iff_psiWeak` the Riemann hypothesis is then equivalent to the square-root bound on `π − Li` itself.

decls.name: Li_two
decls.why: At two the smooth count is `2 / log 2`: its integral part is empty there.

decls.name: continuousOn_Li
decls.why: The smooth count `Li` is continuous past one, because it has a derivative there.

decls.name: uIcc_two_subset
decls.why: Every point between two and `x` is past one, where `Li` and `log` behave.

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_Li_div
decls.why: `Li t / t` can be integrated from two to `x`.
decls.proves: IntervalIntegrable (fun t : ℝ => Stage3.Li t / t) volume 2 x

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_pi_div
decls.why: The count over `t` can be integrated from two to `x`: the count only steps upward.
decls.proves: IntervalIntegrable (fun t : ℝ => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊t⌋₊ : ℝ) / t) volume 2 x

decls.name: Li_mul_log_sub_integral
decls.why: `Li` undone. `Li x · log x` minus the integral of `Li t / t` from two is exactly `x`. This is the smooth side of the passage from the count back to `θ`.
decls.proves: Stage3.Li x * Real.log x - ∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, Stage3.Li t / t = x

decls.name: relRes
decls.why: The residual of the count against `Stage3.Li`, relative to `t`.

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_relRes
decls.why: The relative residual can be integrated from two to `x`.

decls.name: theta_sub_id_eq
decls.why: `θ` from `π`, with `Stage3.Li` taken off both sides.
decls.proves: θ x - x = ((Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li x) * Real.log x - ∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, relRes t

decls.name: relRes_tail_le
decls.why: The tail of `∫ |relRes|` under the `π`-side bound.
needs: h : StmtSchoenfeldWeak C 1 x₀ (fun x => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ)) Stage3.Li
decls.proves: (∫ t in x₀..x, |relRes t|) ≤ 2 * (C * Real.log x) * Real.sqrt x

decls.name: psiWeak_of_schoenfeldWeak
decls.why: From the count to `ψ`. The square-root bound on `π − Stage3.Li` gives the bound on `ψ` at two more logarithms.
needs: h : StmtSchoenfeldWeak C 1 x₀ (fun x => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ)) Stage3.Li
decls.proves: ∃ C' > 0, ∃ x₁ : ℝ, StmtPsiWeak C' 3 x₁

decls.name: RH_of_schoenfeldWeak
decls.why: The square-root bound on the count gives the Riemann hypothesis.
needs: h : StmtSchoenfeldWeak C 1 x₀ (fun x => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ)) Stage3.Li

decls.name: RH_iff_schoenfeldWeak
decls.why: The Riemann hypothesis is the square-root bound on the count.
decls.proves: RiemannHypothesis ↔ ∃ C x₀ : ℝ, StmtSchoenfeldWeak C 1 x₀ (fun x => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ)) Stage3.Li

header: PiZeros — block T2 of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. Joint T1 in the integer table: the count of primes in place of the log-weighted count, zero by zero. The passage from one to the other is linear: `tr f x` is `f x / log x` plus the integral of `f` against `1/(t·log²t)` from `2`, and `Stage3.pi_sub_Li_eq` says the count minus its smooth part is `tr (θ − id)`. Write `θ − id` as the explicit formula's remainder at a height, minus the sum over the zeros below it, minus the higher prime powers `ψ − θ`. Th…

decls.name: wt
decls.why: The weight of the passage from the log-weighted count to the count.

decls.name: tr
decls.why: The passage from the log-weighted count to the count, applied to any function: its value over the logarithm, plus its integral against the weight.

decls.name: wt_continuousOn
decls.why: For `x ≥ 2` the weight is continuous on `[2, x]`.

decls.name: integrable_mul_wt
decls.why: For `x ≥ 2`, a function integrable on `[2, x]` stays integrable when multiplied by the weight.
decls.proves: IntervalIntegrable (fun t => f t * wt t) volume 2 x

decls.name: tr_sub
decls.why: The passage of a difference of two integrable functions is the difference of their passages.
decls.proves: tr (fun t => f t - g t) x = tr f x - tr g x

decls.name: tr_const_mul
decls.why: A constant factor passes through the passage.
decls.proves: tr (fun t => c * f t) x = c * tr f x

decls.name: tr_sum
decls.why: The passage of a finite sum of integrable functions is the sum of their passages.
needs: hf : ∀ i ∈ s, IntervalIntegrable (f i) volume 2 x
decls.proves: tr (fun t => ∑ i ∈ s, f i t) x = ∑ i ∈ s, tr (f i) x

decls.name: pi_sub_Li_eq_tr
decls.why: The count minus its smooth part is the passage applied to `θ − id`.
decls.proves: (((Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li x : ℝ) : ℂ) = tr (fun t => ((θ t - t : ℝ) : ℂ)) x

decls.name: piMode
decls.why: One zero's part of the count: the passage applied to `t^ρ/ρ`.

decls.name: efRem
decls.why: The remainder of the explicit formula at a height.

decls.name: psiTheta
decls.why: The prime powers above the first: `ψ − θ`.

decls.name: zeroPartialSum_eq_sum
decls.why: The zero sum below a height, written as a sum over the finite set of zeros below it.
decls.proves: Stage3.zeroPartialSum t T = ∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * ((t : ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ) / (ρ : ℂ))

decls.name: integrable_ofReal_of_monotone
decls.why: A monotone real function, read as complex, is integrable on `[2, x]`.
decls.proves: IntervalIntegrable (fun t => ((f t : ℝ) : ℂ)) volume 2 x

decls.name: integrable_cpow
decls.why: For `x ≥ 2` the function `t ↦ t^ρ/ρ` is integrable on `[2, x]`.
decls.proves: IntervalIntegrable (fun t : ℝ => (t : ℂ) ^ ρ / ρ) volume 2 x

decls.name: pi_eq_zero_sum
decls.why: The count as a sum over the zeros, exactly. For every `x ≥ 2` and every height `T`: the count minus its smooth part is minus the sum over the zeros below `T` of each zero's part, plus the passage of the explicit formula's remainder, minus the passage of the higher prime powers.
decls.proves: (((Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) - Stage3.Li x : ℝ) : ℂ) = -∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * piMode (ρ : ℂ) x + tr (efRem T) x - tr psiTheta x

decls.name: norm_tr_psiTheta_le
decls.why: The higher prime powers are of square-root size.

decls.name: stencil_congr
decls.why: Two rows that agree on the entries a stencil reads have the same stencil.
needs: h : ∀ j ∈ range (n + 1), a (r - j) = b (r - j)
decls.proves: CellZeros.stencil n a r = CellZeros.stencil n b r

decls.name: stencil_neg
decls.why: The stencil of the negative of a row is the negative of its stencil.
decls.proves: CellZeros.stencil n (fun m => -a m) r = -CellZeros.stencil n a r

decls.name: stencilR_cast
decls.why: The real stencil of a row, read as complex, is the complex stencil of the row read as complex.
decls.proves: ((Nonvanishing.stencilR n g r : ℝ) : ℂ) = CellZeros.stencil n (fun m => ((g m : ℝ) : ℂ)) r

decls.name: table_cell_eq_zero_sum
decls.why: The integer table's cell as a sum over the zeros, exactly. The cell `(r, d)` of the table of the prime count along the doublings, less the smooth cell, is minus the sum over the zeros below any height of each zero's part under the stencil, plus the stencil of the explicit formula's remainder passed to the count, minus the stencil of the higher prime powers.
decls.proves: ((((Construction.tableFrom TableRoute.rowN r d : ℤ) : ℝ) - Nonvanishing.stencilR (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => Stage3.Li ((2 : ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) r : ℝ) : ℂ) = -∑ ρ ∈ ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * CellZeros.stencil (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => piMode (ρ : ℂ) ((2:ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) r + CellZeros.stencil (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => tr (efRem T) ((2:ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) r - CellZeros.stencil (d + 1) (fun m : ℤ => tr psiTheta ((2:ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))) r

header: PsiToPi — step 3: the transfer from ψ-error to π−Li error. The classical chain: Mathlib's Abel-summation bridge (`Chebyshev.primeCounting_eq_theta_div_log_add_integral`) writes π(⌊x⌋) = θ(x)/log x + ∫₂ˣ θ(t)/(t·log²t) dt, and the same identity for the logarithmic integral turns any bound on |θ − id| into a bound on |π − Li|. Mathlib carries no li, so this module defines its own:

decls.name: Li
decls.why: The offset logarithmic integral: `Li x = x/log x + ∫₂ˣ dt/log²t`. Differs from the literature's `li` by the constant `2/log 2 − li(2) ≈ 1.840`.

decls.name: continuousOn_inv_log_sq
decls.why: `1/log²t` is continuous on any interval right of `2`.
decls.proves: ContinuousOn (fun t : ℝ => 1 / Real.log t ^ 2) (Set.uIcc a x)

decls.name: continuousOn_inv_mul_log_sq
decls.why: `(t·log²t)⁻¹` is continuous on any interval right of `2`.
decls.proves: ContinuousOn (fun t : ℝ => (t * Real.log t ^ 2)⁻¹) (Set.uIcc a x)

decls.name: integrable_theta_term
decls.why: `θ(t)/(t·log²t)` is interval integrable on `[2, x]`: `θ` is monotone, the cofactor is continuous.
decls.proves: IntervalIntegrable (fun t => θ t / (t * Real.log t ^ 2)) volume a x

decls.name: integrable_err_term
decls.why: `(θ(t) − t)/(t·log²t)` is interval integrable on `[2, x]`.
decls.proves: IntervalIntegrable (fun t => (θ t - t) / (t * Real.log t ^ 2)) volume a x

decls.name: pi_sub_Li_eq
decls.why: The exact decomposition — an identity, from Mathlib's Abel-summation bridge and the definition of `Li`: `π(⌊x⌋) − Li x = (θx − x)/log x + ∫₂ˣ (θt − t)/(t·log²t) dt`.
decls.proves: (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) - Li x = (θ x - x) / Real.log x + ∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, (θ t - t) / (t * Real.log t ^ 2)

decls.name: abs_pi_sub_Li_le
decls.why: The envelope transfer: a pointwise bound on `|θ − id|` becomes a bound on `|π − Li|`, top term plus envelope integral.
needs: hEnv : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (2 : ℝ) x, |θ t - t| ≤ env t
hEnvInt : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => env t / (t * Real.log t ^ 2)) volume 2 x
decls.proves: |(Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ) - Li x| ≤ |θ x - x| / Real.log x + ∫ t in (2 : ℝ)..x, env t / (t * Real.log t ^ 2)

decls.name: integral_A_rpow_le
decls.why: The workhorse envelope integral: `∫₂ˣ A·t^(−1/2) dt ≤ 2A·√x`.
decls.proves: (∫ t in a..x, A * t ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / 2)) ≤ 2 * A * Real.sqrt x

decls.name: theta_err_of_psi
decls.why: `θ`-error from `ψ`-error, by Mathlib's `|ψ − θ| ≤ 2√x·log x`.
decls.proves: |θ x - x| ≤ E + 2 * Real.sqrt x * Real.log x

decls.name: StmtPsiWeak
decls.why: The ψ-side of the weak family: what stage 5's assembly (hRH + hEF + hNT) delivers. `ψ` is Mathlib's Chebyshev function.

decls.name: abs_theta_sub_le_linear
decls.why: Crude linear bound below the family floor: `|θ − id| ≤ (1 + log 4)·t`, from `0 ≤ θ t ≤ log 4 · t`.

decls.name: one_add_log_four_le
decls.why: The numeric fact carrying the low-range constant: `1 + log 4 ≤ 5·log²2`, i.e. `(1 + log 4)/log²2 ≤ 5`.

decls.name: rpow_neg_half_mul
decls.why: `t^(−1/2)` times the denominator is the √t envelope: `t^(−1/2)·(t·log²t) = √t·log²t` on `t > 0`.
decls.proves: t ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / 2) * (t * Real.log t ^ 2) = Real.sqrt t * Real.log t ^ 2

decls.name: schoenfeldWeak_of_psiWeak
decls.why: The capstone of step 3: the transfer. A ψ-side weak bound `(C, k, x₀)` with `k ≥ 2, x₀ ≥ 2` delivers the π-side weak bound with `C′ = 3C + 13`, exponent `k − 1`, floor `max(x₀², 9)` — one log dropped, the constant inflated explicitly — and the conclusion is literally `StmtSchoenfeldWeak`, so Statement.lean's window bridge applies to it.

header: RateBelow — block R9 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`, the staircase. 2026-11-23.

decls.name: rain_psi
decls.why: The rain comes. At a zero `ρ₀`, for every exponent `θ` below its real part, the staircase exceeds `C·x^θ·log^k x` at points beyond any `x₀`.
decls.proves: ∃ x : ℝ, x₀ ≤ x ∧ C * x ^ θ * Real.log x ^ k < |Chebyshev.psi x - x|

header: ReZetaCount — block H2 of `lean_stage3/design/hnt.md`, "The count: zeros of Re ζ on the segment, and Re ζ > 0 on the line Re s = 2".

decls.name: G
decls.why: The symmetrised local model's numerator: `ζ(2z+2+iT) + ζ(2z+2−iT)`.

decls.name: F
decls.why: The normalised model, `1` at the centre.

decls.name: reZeroSet
decls.why: The zeros of `x ↦ Re ζ(x + iT)` on the open segment `(1/2, 2)`.

decls.name: norm_zeta_sub_one_le
decls.why: The Dirichlet tail on `Re s = 2`. `‖ζ(s) − 1‖ ≤ π²/6 − 1 < 1`.

decls.name: re_zeta_two_line_ge
decls.why: The vertical leg's sign, quantitative. `Re ζ(2+it) ≥ 2 − π²/6`.

decls.name: re_zeta_two_line_pos
decls.why: T3, discharged. `Re ζ(2+it) > 0`.

decls.name: G_zero_eq

The primes and the composites split it by adding: `P + C = T`. A zero and its mirror split it by multiplying: their modes have sizes `T^β` and `T^(1−β)`, whose product is `T`. On the multiplying side the table is one line, the exponent from `0` to `1`, and the real part of a zero is the share of the total its mode takes there. The two meet in the middle exactly at one half, where…

header: # Stage3.SieveExact — the sieve of Legendre, exactly Block R2 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md` ("The sieve, exactly"). An exploratory run (unit 0475) checked on rows 10..24 that the number of primes up to `2^r` is given exactly by the sieve of Legendre from the primes up to `2^(r/2)`. This module proves that identity for every `N`, with nothing computed.

decls.name: smallPrimes
decls.why: The primes up to the square root of `N`.

decls.name: survivors
decls.why: The integers from 1 to `N` that no prime up to `√N` divides.

decls.name: prime_of_mem_smallPrimes
decls.why: Every member of `smallPrimes N` is prime.

decls.name: forall_dvd_iff_prod_dvd
decls.why: For a set of primes, all of them divide `n` exactly when their product does.

decls.name: card_filter_not_dvd
decls.why: Inclusion and exclusion over any finite set `A`: the members of `A` that no prime of `s` divides, counted as an alternating sum of the members that the products of subsets of `s` divide.
decls.proves: ((A.filter (fun n => ∀ p ∈ s, ¬ p ∣ n)).card : ℤ) = ∑ T ∈ s.powerset, (-1 : ℤ) ^ T.card * ((A.filter (fun n => (∏ p ∈ T, p) ∣ n)).card : ℤ)

decls.name: card_multiples
decls.why: The multiples of `d` in `[1, N]` number `N / d`.
decls.proves: ((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun n => d ∣ n)).card = N / d

decls.name: sieve_sum
decls.why: Inclusion and exclusion: the survivors of the sieve number the alternating sum, over the sets `T` of primes up to `√N`, of `⌊N / ∏ T⌋`.
decls.proves: ((survivors N).card : ℤ) = ∑ T ∈ (smallPrimes N).powerset, (-1 : ℤ) ^ T.card * ((N / ∏ p ∈ T, p : ℕ) : ℤ)

decls.name: survivors_eq
decls.why: For `2 ≤ N`, the survivors of the sieve are `1` and the primes above `√N` up to `N`.
decls.proves: survivors N = insert 1 ((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun n => Nat.Prime n ∧ Nat.sqrt N < n))

decls.name: card_survivors
decls.why: For `2 ≤ N`, the survivors together with the primes up to `√N` number one more than the primes up to `N`.

decls.name: pi_by_sieve
decls.why: For `2 ≤ N`, the number of primes up to `N` from the primes up to `√N` alone: `π(N) = π(√N) - 1 + Σ_T (-1)^|T| ⌊N / ∏ T⌋`.

decls.name: row_by_sieve
decls.why: The ladder: `pi_by_sieve` at `N = 2 ^ r`, the table's row `r`.

decls.name: sieve_by_level
decls.why: The sieve's sum arranged by level: the sets `T` grouped by their size `k`.
decls.proves: ∑ T ∈ (smallPrimes N).powerset, (-1 : ℤ) ^ T.card * ((N / ∏ p ∈ T, p : ℕ) : ℤ) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range ((smallPrimes N).card + 1), ∑ T ∈ (smallPrimes N).powersetCard k, (-1 : ℤ) ^ T.card * ((N / ∏ p ∈ T, p : ℕ) : ℤ)

decls.name: sieve_by_level_sign
decls.why: The sum by level with the sign of each level pulled out: level `k` carries `(-1)^k`.
decls.proves: ∑ T ∈ (smallPrimes N).powerset, (-1 : ℤ) ^ T.card * ((N / ∏ p ∈ T, p : ℕ) : ℤ) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range ((smallPrimes N).card + 1), (-1 : ℤ) ^ k * ∑ T ∈ (smallPrimes N).powersetCard k, ((N / ∏ p ∈ T, p : ℕ) : ℤ)

decls.name: level_card
decls.why: The number of terms at level `k` is a binomial coefficient: a row of Pascal.

decls.name: smoothPart
decls.why: The exact-fraction part of the sieve's sum.

decls.name: netRounding
decls.why: The net of the roundings, with their signs.

decls.name: roundingMass
decls.why: The roundings added in size.

decls.name: natDiv_eq_sub_fract
decls.why: A natural quotient is the exact fraction less its fractional part.
decls.proves: ((n / d : ℕ) : ℚ) = (n : ℚ) / (d : ℚ) - Int.fract ((n : ℚ) / (d : ℚ))

decls.name: sieve_split
decls.why: The survivors' count is the exact-fraction part less the net of the roundings.
decls.proves: ((survivors N).card : ℚ) = smoothPart N - netRounding N

decls.name: smoothPart_eq_prod
decls.why: The exact-fraction part is `N` times the product of `1 - 1/p` over the primes up to `√N`.
decls.proves: smoothPart N = (N : ℚ) * ∏ p ∈ smallPrimes N, (1 - 1 / (p : ℚ))

decls.name: abs_netRounding_le
decls.why: The net of the roundings is at most their mass in size.

decls.name: roundingMass_nonneg
decls.why: The rounding mass is nonnegative.

decls.name: netRounding_eq
decls.why: The net of the roundings, exactly. For `N ≥ 2` the net rounding is the closed product less the count the sieve produces: `N·Π(1 − 1/p)` over the primes up to `√N`, less `1 + π(N) − π(√N)`.
decls.proves: netRounding N = (N : ℚ) * ∏ p ∈ smallPrimes N, (1 - 1 / (p : ℚ)) - (1 + (Nat.primeCounting N : ℚ) - (Nat.primeCounting (Nat.sqrt N) : ℚ))

header: SieveIdem — block R12 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`. 2026-11-23. Julian, 2026-11-23: the settling happens one slot at a time because of idempotence; every step is the same `f`, and it scales at any `x`.

decls.name: sieveStep_idem
decls.why: Idempotent. A step done twice is done once.
decls.proves: sieveStep p (sieveStep p A) = sieveStep p A

decls.name: sieveStep_comm
decls.why: Order-free. Two primes' steps give the same set in either order.
decls.proves: sieveStep p (sieveStep q A) = sieveStep q (sieveStep p A)

decls.name: mem_sieveStep
decls.why: No size in the rule. A number survives a step exactly when it was there and the prime does not divide it, at every size.
decls.proves: m ∈ sieveStep p A ↔ m ∈ A ∧ ¬ p ∣ m

decls.name: sieveBelow_idem
decls.why: The whole sieve below `p` is idempotent too.
decls.proves: sieveBelow p (sieveBelow p A) = sieveBelow p A

decls.name: sieveBelow_succ
decls.why: One slot at a time. Past a prime `p`, the sieve grows by exactly `p`'s step.
decls.proves: sieveBelow (p + 1) A = sieveStep p (sieveBelow p A)

decls.name: sieveBelow_succ_of_not_prime
decls.why: Past a number that is not prime, the sieve does not change.

decls.name: rough_eq_card
decls.why: JOIN. The counts of `CompositeSplit.rough` are the sieve below `p` of the numbers up to `N/p`.

decls.name: settles_on_prime
decls.why: It settles on a prime. A number from two up that no prime below it divides is prime: the first slot no earlier prime reaches.
needs: h : ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → q < m → ¬ q ∣ m

header: SieveResidual — block R3 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`. 2026-11-23. The roundings of the sieve and the residual of the table are tied exactly.

decls.name: smoothNet
decls.why: The smooth part of the net rounding: the closed product, less the unit, less the smooth count at `N`, plus the smooth count at `√N`.

decls.name: cast_netRounding
decls.why: The net rounding, as a real number, is the product less the count the sieve produces.
decls.proves: ((netRounding N : ℚ) : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) * ∏ p ∈ smallPrimes N, (1 - 1 / (p : ℝ)) - (1 + (Nat.primeCounting N : ℝ) - (Nat.primeCounting (Nat.sqrt N) : ℝ))

decls.name: net_wobble
decls.why: The roundings' wobble is the table's residual, at the row less at its square root. For `N ≥ 2`, the net rounding less its smooth part is minus the residual of the count at `N` less the residual at `√N`.
decls.proves: ((netRounding N : ℚ) : ℝ) - smoothNet N = -(((Nat.primeCounting N : ℝ) - Stage3.Li (N : ℝ)) - ((Nat.primeCounting (Nat.sqrt N) : ℝ) - Stage3.Li ((Nat.sqrt N : ℕ) : ℝ)))

decls.name: sqrt_two_pow
decls.why: The square root of an even power of two is the power of half the exponent.

decls.name: net_wobble_rows
decls.why: The row and its half. At the doubling of an even row `2m`, the net rounding less its smooth part is minus the residual of the table at row `2m` less the residual at row `m`.
decls.proves: ((netRounding (2 ^ (2 * m)) : ℚ) : ℝ) - smoothNet (2 ^ (2 * m)) = -(((Nat.primeCounting (2 ^ (2 * m)) : ℝ) - Stage3.Li (((2 ^ (2 * m) : ℕ) : ℝ))) - ((Nat.primeCounting (2 ^ m) : ℝ) - Stage3.Li (((2 ^ m : ℕ) : ℝ))))

header: SpiralLink — block J2 of `lean_stage3/design/closedloop.md`. 2026-11-23. The link of Julian's paper, §6.3 ("The Phasor Mechanism"), stated in Lean:

decls.name: mirror_mem
decls.why: The mirror point `1 − conj ρ` of a nontrivial zero is a nontrivial zero.

decls.name: mirrorZ
decls.why: The mirror of a zero, as a zero.

decls.name: mirrorZ_im
decls.why: The mirror of a zero is at the same height.

decls.name: mirrorZ_re
decls.why: The mirror of a zero has its real part reflected in one half.

decls.name: mirrorZ_eq_iff
decls.why: A zero is its own mirror exactly on the line.

decls.name: mirror_pair_area
decls.why: The pair keeps pace. At any base, the size of a zero's mode times the size of its mirror's mode is the base.
decls.proves: ‖(b : ℂ) ^ (ρ : ℂ)‖ * ‖(b : ℂ) ^ ((mirrorZ ρ : NontrivialZeros) : ℂ)‖ = b

decls.name: off_line_is_two
decls.why: Off the line a zero is two. A nontrivial zero off the line has a mirror that is a different zero at the same height, and the handshake fails at both.
decls.proves: mirrorZ ρ ≠ ρ ∧ ((mirrorZ ρ : NontrivialZeros) : ℂ).im = (ρ : ℂ).im ∧ ¬ isHermitianHandshake (ρ : ℂ).re ∧ ¬ isHermitianHandshake ((mirrorZ ρ : NontrivialZeros) : ℂ).re

decls.name: SpiralLink
decls.why: The spiral link (Julian's paper, §6.3): the walk closes only where the closed loop is at rest. The Hermitian handshake holds at every nontrivial zero of zeta.

decls.name: OneAtEachHeight
decls.why: There is one zero. No two nontrivial zeros share a height.

decls.name: rh_iff_spiralLink
decls.why: The Riemann hypothesis is the spiral link.

decls.name: rh_iff_one_at_each_height
decls.why: The Riemann hypothesis is that there is one zero at each height.

decls.name: spiralLink_iff_one
decls.why: The spiral link and "one zero at each height" are the same statement.

header: SquareMean — block C5a of `lean_stage3/design/carlson.md`. 2026-11-23. An analytic function cannot be small in mean square on a square around a point where it has size one. For `f` complex differentiable on an open set containing the closed square of half-side `δ` about `c`, the iterated integral of `‖f‖²` over the square is at least `π·δ²·‖f c‖²`. The proof takes the mean value property of `f²` on each circle of radius `r < δ`, which gives `2π‖f c‖² ≤ ∫ ‖f‖²` over the circle; multiplies by `r` and integrates in po…

decls.name: circle_sq_mean
decls.why: If `f` is complex differentiable on `U` and the closed disc of radius `r > 0` about `c` lies in `U`, then `2π‖f c‖²` is at most the integral of `‖f‖²` over the circle of radius `r`, parametrized by the angle in `(−π, π)`.
decls.proves: 2 * π * ‖f c‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∫ θ in Ioo (-π) π, ‖f (c + (r : ℂ) * ((Real.cos θ : ℂ) + (Real.sin θ : ℂ) * Complex.I))‖ ^ 2

decls.name: ball_subset_sq
decls.why: The closed disc of radius `δ` about `c` lies in the closed square of half-side `δ` about `c`.
decls.proves: closedBall c δ ⊆ (Icc (c.re - δ) (c.re + δ)) ×ℂ (Icc (c.im - δ) (c.im + δ))

decls.name: norm_polar
decls.why: The norm of `r(cos θ + i sin θ)` is `|r|`.
decls.proves: ‖(r : ℂ) * ((Real.cos θ : ℂ) + (Real.sin θ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ = |r|

decls.name: disc_sq_mean
decls.why: If `f` is complex differentiable on an open `U` containing the closed disc of radius `δ` about `c`, then `π δ² ‖f c‖²` is at most the integral over `ℂ` of `‖f‖²` cut off to the open disc.
decls.proves: π * δ ^ 2 * ‖f c‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∫ z, (ball c δ).indicator (fun z => ‖f z‖ ^ 2) z

decls.name: sq_set_integral
decls.why: For `F` continuous on the closed square of half-side `δ` about `c`, the area integral of `F` over the square equals the iterated integral, outer over the real part and inner over the imaginary part.
needs: hF : ContinuousOn F ((Icc (c.re - δ) (c.re + δ)) ×ℂ (Icc (c.im - δ) (c.im + δ)))
decls.proves: ∫ z in (Icc (c.re - δ) (c.re + δ)) ×ℂ (Icc (c.im - δ) (c.im + δ)), F z = ∫ u in (c.re - δ)..(c.re + δ), ∫ t in (c.im - δ)..(c.im + δ), F ((u : ℂ) + Complex.I * (t : ℂ))

decls.name: sq_mean_lower
decls.why: An analytic function is not small in mean square on a square about a point where it is large: for `f` complex differentiable on an open set containing the closed square of half-side `δ` about `c`, the iterated integral of `‖f‖²` over the square is at least `π δ² ‖f c‖²`.
needs: hsub : (Icc (c.re - δ) (c.re + δ)) ×ℂ (Icc (c.im - δ) (c.im + δ)) ⊆ U
decls.proves: π * δ ^ 2 * ‖f c‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∫ u in (c.re - δ)..(c.re + δ), ∫ t in (c.im - δ)..(c.im + δ), ‖f ((u : ℂ) + Complex.I * (t : ℂ))‖ ^ 2

header: Statement — step 2: the weak bound family, and the bridges between shapes. O68 (entry 118) measured the tolerance: the census survives bounds of the shape C·√x·(log x)^k far weaker than Schoenfeld's — depth 10 at C = 1, k = 2; depth 6 at C = 1000. This module gives that family its Lean name and proves the bridges:

decls.name: StmtSchoenfeldWindow
decls.why: Character-level copy of `Nonvanishing.StmtSchoenfeldWindow` from the bench tree (lean/Nonvanishing.lean). The weld: utilities/check_weld.py verifies the two definition bodies are textually identical.

decls.name: StmtSchoenfeld
decls.why: Character-level copy of `Schoenfeld.StmtSchoenfeld` from the bench tree (lean/Schoenfeld.lean). The weld: utilities/check_weld.py verifies the two definition bodies are textually identical.

decls.name: StmtSchoenfeldWeak
decls.why: The weak family (O68's grid, as a Prop): `|pi − li| ≤ C·√x·(log x)^k` from `x₀` on. The census survives members far weaker than Schoenfeld's: depth 10 at `C = 1, k = 2`, depth 6 at `C = 1000, k = 2` (entry 118).

decls.name: StmtWeakWindow
decls.why: The weak bound translated to the dyadic window: at `x = 2^(r−j)` the bound reads `C·(log 2·(r−j))^k·2^((r−j)/2)`.

decls.name: schoenfeld_iff_weak
decls.why: Schoenfeld is a member of the family: Corollary 1 is exactly `C = 1/(8π), k = 1, x₀ = 2657`.
decls.proves: StmtSchoenfeld pi li ↔ StmtSchoenfeldWeak (1 / (8 * Real.pi)) 1 2657 pi li

decls.name: weak_anti_x₀
decls.why: A lower floor only strengthens the hypothesis.
needs: h : StmtSchoenfeldWeak C k x₀ pi li
decls.proves: StmtSchoenfeldWeak C k x₀' pi li

decls.name: weak_mono
decls.why: A larger constant only weakens the hypothesis (needs `1 ≤ x₀` so the envelope `√x·(log x)^k` is nonnegative on the range).
needs: h : StmtSchoenfeldWeak C k x₀ pi li
decls.proves: StmtSchoenfeldWeak C' k x₀ pi li

decls.name: weakWindow_of_global
decls.why: The bridge, weak form: the global weak bound implies the window bound whenever the window bottom clears the floor: `x₀ ≤ 2^(r−n)`. The translation is `√(2^y) = 2^(y/2)` and `log(2^y) = y·log 2`, exactly as in the bench's special case.
needs: hpi : StmtSchoenfeldWeak C k x₀ pi li
hf : ∀ m : ℤ, f m = pi ((2 : ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))
hL : ∀ m : ℤ, L m = li ((2 : ℝ) ^ (m : ℝ))
decls.proves: StmtWeakWindow C k f L r n

decls.name: weakWindow_at_schoenfeld
decls.why: At Schoenfeld's parameters the weak window is the bench's window: `C = 1/(8π), k = 1` recovers `StmtSchoenfeldWindow`'s bound character for character.
decls.proves: StmtWeakWindow (1 / (8 * Real.pi)) 1 f L r n ↔ StmtSchoenfeldWindow f L r n

header: StencilWeil — block T4 of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22. The table's stencil inside Weil's form, and the restoring force read off a mode of the table. In the variable `u = log x` one doubling is the shift by `log 2`; `stencilTest d φ` is the depth-`d` stencil applied to a test function `φ` along the doublings. It is again a test function, its transform is the symbol to the depth times `φ`'s, and so each zero of ζ enters Weil's form on it with weight the symbol at the zero times the symbol at its mirror…

decls.name: stencilTest
decls.why: The depth-`d` stencil applied to a test function along the doublings, in the variable `u = log x`.

decls.name: restoringForce
decls.why: The imbalance between a mode of the table and its mirror, in logarithms.

decls.name: laplace_shift
decls.why: Shifting a function multiplies its transform by an exponential.
decls.proves: laplace (fun u => φ (u + a)) z = Complex.exp (z * (a : ℂ)) * laplace φ z

decls.name: integrable_shift_term
decls.why: A shifted test function against the transform's kernel is integrable.
decls.proves: Integrable (fun u : ℝ => φ (u + a) * Complex.exp (-(z * (u : ℂ))))

decls.name: laplace_stencilTest
decls.why: The stencil's transform is the symbol to the depth.
decls.proves: laplace (stencilTest d φ) z = (1 - (2 : ℂ) ^ z) ^ d * laplace φ z

decls.name: stencilTest_zero_outside
decls.why: The stencil of a test function vanishes off the widened window.

decls.name: isTest_stencilTest
decls.why: The stencil of a test function is a test function, on a window wider by the stencil's reach.

decls.name: zeroForm_stencilTest
decls.why: Weil's form on the stencil, zero by zero. Each zero enters with the symbol at the zero times the symbol at its mirror point, to the depth.
decls.proves: zeroForm (stencilTest d φ) = riemannZeta.zeroes_sum (Set.Ioo 0 1) (Set.univ : Set ℝ) (fun ρ => ((1 - (2 : ℂ) ^ (-ρ)) * (1 - (2 : ℂ) ^ (-(1 - ρ)))) ^ d * (laplace φ (-ρ) * laplace φ (-(1 - ρ))))

decls.name: mirror_symbol_on_line
decls.why: On the line the handshake holds. The symbol at a zero times the symbol at its mirror point is the square of the symbol's size.

decls.name: restoringForce_eq
decls.why: The restoring force, in closed form: twice the displacement from one half, times the logarithm of the base.

decls.name: restoringForce_eq_zero_iff
decls.why: The force is zero exactly on the line.

decls.name: handshake_iff
decls.why: The handshake. A mode of the table and its mirror have the same size exactly when the zero is on the line.

decls.name: restoringForce_mono
decls.why: Stiffer further out. At a larger base the same displacement gives a larger force.
decls.proves: restoringForce b ρ ≤ restoringForce c ρ

decls.name: zeroForm_stencilTest_eq_primeSide
decls.why: The form on the stencil is its prime side, given the bridge.
decls.proves: zeroForm (stencilTest d φ) = WeilBridgeLeaf.primeSideM (WeilBridgeLeaf.kOfM (stencilTest d φ))

decls.name: zeroForm_stencilTest_nonneg_of_RH
decls.why: Under the Riemann hypothesis the form on the stencil is nonnegative.

header: StepsBelow — block R9 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`, the turned steps. 2026-11-23.

decls.name: tent

decls.name: Bk

decls.name: eqOn_zero_of_agree
decls.why: V3, for any continuation. An `F` analytic on `{re > θ} \ {1}` that is `−ζ'/ζ` right of `X ≥ 1` satisfies `F·ζ + ζ′ = 0` on the whole region.
needs: heq : ∀ z : ℂ, X < z.re → F z = -deriv ζ z / ζ z
decls.proves: Set.EqOn (fun z : ℂ ↦ F z * ζ z + deriv ζ z) 0 (Stage3.regionθ θ)

decls.name: zeta_ne_zero_of_agree
decls.why: V4, for any continuation. Under the hypotheses of V3, no zero of `ζ` has real part above `θ`. `ThetaConverse.no_zero_right_of_theta` with `F` abstract.
needs: heq : ∀ z : ℂ, X < z.re → F z = -deriv ζ z / ζ z

decls.name: zeta_ne_zero_of_steps_bound
decls.why: The converse for the turned steps. A bound `‖S(N,s) − K(1)‖ ≤ C·N^δ` from `N₁` on, `δ ≥ 0`, leaves no zero of `ζ` with real part above `Re s + δ`.
needs: H : ∀ N : ℕ, N₁ ≤ N → ‖S N s - K N s 1‖ ≤ C * (N:ℝ) ^ δ

decls.name: rain_steps
decls.why: The rain comes. At a zero `ρ₀`, the turned steps to a cutoff, less their smooth term, exceed `C·N^δ` at cutoffs beyond any `N₀`, for every `0 ≤ δ < Re ρ₀ − Re s`.
decls.proves: ∃ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N ∧ 2 ≤ N ∧ C * (N : ℝ) ^ δ < ‖StepsPeak.S N s - StepsPeak.K N s 1‖

header: StepsPeak — block R5 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`. 2026-11-23. The first size of unit 0472: the turned steps up to a cutoff `N`, with the ramp `1 − n/N`, stand at height `m·log N` at a zero of order `m`.

decls.name: ramp
decls.why: The ramp `f(u) = u^(−s)·(1 − u/N)`.

decls.name: slope
decls.why: Minus its slope, `g(u) = s·u^(−s−1) − (s−1)·u^(−s)/N`.

decls.name: S
decls.why: The turned steps to the cutoff `N`, with the ramp: `S(N,s) = Σ_{n ≤ N} Λ(n)·n^(−s)·(1 − n/N)`.

decls.name: K
decls.why: The kernel of a power, `K(a) = ∫_2^N u^a·g(u) du`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_ramp
decls.proves: HasDerivAt (ramp N s) (-slope N s u) u

decls.name: cont_cpow
decls.why: A power is continuous right of `0`.

decls.name: S_eq_integral
decls.why: Partial summation. `f(N) = 0`, so `S(N,s) = ∫_2^N g·ψ`.
decls.proves: S N s = ∫ u in (2:ℝ)..(N:ℝ), slope N s u * ((ψ u : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: peak_identity
decls.why: The identity. With `E(u,T) = ψ(u) − u + Σ_{|γ|<T} m·u^ρ/ρ` the remainder of the explicit formula, `S(N,s) = K(1) − Σ_{|γ|<T} (m/ρ)·K(ρ) + ∫_2^N E·g`.
decls.proves: S N s - K N s 1 + ∑ ρ ∈ FiniteOffLine.ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) / (ρ : ℂ) * K N s (ρ : ℂ) = ∫ u in (2:ℝ)..(N:ℝ), slope N s u * PiZeros.efRem T u

decls.name: C1
decls.why: The constant of the error, a function of `σ = Re s` alone: `C₁(σ) = (c3t·(2/σ) + Bleft2)·(2/σ)`.

decls.name: norm_integrand_le
decls.why: The integrand of the error, pointwise on `[2, N]`.
decls.proves: ‖slope N s u * PiZeros.efRem T u‖ ≤ (‖s‖ + ‖s - 1‖) * (ExplicitTwo.c1t * Real.log ((N:ℝ) * T) ^ 2 / T + (ExplicitTwo.c3t * (2 / s.re) + ExplicitTwo.Bleft2) * u ^ (-s.re / 2 - 1))

decls.name: norm_error_le
decls.why: The error. `‖∫_2^N E·g‖ ≤ (‖s‖+‖s−1‖)·(c1t·N·log²(NT)/T + C₁(σ))`.
decls.proves: ‖∫ u in (2:ℝ)..(N:ℝ), slope N s u * PiZeros.efRem T u‖ ≤ (‖s‖ + ‖s - 1‖) * (ExplicitTwo.c1t * N * Real.log ((N:ℝ) * T) ^ 2 / T + C1 s.re)

decls.name: peak_formula
decls.why: The height of the peak, as a formula. For `Re s > 0`, `N ≥ 2`, `T ≥ 2`: `‖S(N,s) − K(1) + Σ_{|γ|<T} (m/ρ)·K(ρ)‖ ≤ (‖s‖+‖s−1‖)·(c1t·N·log²(NT)/T + C₁(Re s))`.
decls.proves: ‖S N s - K N s 1 + ∑ ρ ∈ FiniteOffLine.ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) / (ρ : ℂ) * K N s (ρ : ℂ)‖ ≤ (‖s‖ + ‖s - 1‖) * (ExplicitTwo.c1t * N * Real.log ((N:ℝ) * T) ^ 2 / T + C1 s.re)

decls.name: K_eq
decls.why: The kernel in closed form, for `a ≠ s` and `a ≠ s − 1`.

decls.name: K_self
decls.why: The kernel at `a = s`: `K(s) = s·(log N − log 2) − (s−1)·(N−2)/N`.
decls.proves: K N s s = s * ((Real.log N - Real.log 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) - (s - 1) * ((N:ℂ) - 2) / N

decls.name: peak_at_zero
decls.why: The peak at a zero. At `s = ρ₀`, a nontrivial zero of order `m₀` below the height `T`, its own term is `−m₀·log N + m₀·log 2 + m₀·(ρ₀−1)·(N−2)/(ρ₀·N)` and the sum runs over the other zeros below `T`.
decls.proves: ‖S N ρ₀ - K N ρ₀ 1 - (-((riemannZeta.order (ρ₀ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * (Real.log N : ℂ) + ((riemannZeta.order (ρ₀ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * (Real.log 2 : ℂ) + ((riemannZeta.order (ρ₀ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * ((ρ₀ : ℂ) - 1) * ((N : ℂ) - 2) / ((ρ₀ : ℂ) * N)) + ∑ ρ ∈ (FiniteOffLine.ZF T).erase ρ₀, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) / (ρ : ℂ) * K N ρ₀ (ρ : ℂ)‖ ≤ (‖(ρ₀ : ℂ)‖ + ‖(ρ₀ : ℂ) - 1‖) * (ExplicitTwo.c1t * N * Real.log ((N:ℝ) * T) ^ 2 / T + C1 (ρ₀ : ℂ).re)

decls.name: norm_K_le
decls.why: Another zero's kernel, free of `N`. For `a ≠ s`, `a ≠ s − 1` and `Re a ≤ Re s`: `‖K(a)‖ ≤ (‖s‖/‖a−s‖ + ‖s−1‖/‖a−s+1‖)·2`.

decls.name: norm_order
decls.why: The norm of a zero's order, read in `ℂ`.
decls.proves: ‖((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ)‖ = ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ)

decls.name: peak_height
decls.why: The height of the peak. If no zero below `T` lies right of `ρ₀`, then `S(N,ρ₀) − K(1)` stands at `−m₀·log N`, up to `m₀·log 2 + m₀·‖ρ₀−1‖/‖ρ₀‖`, a sum over the other zeros below `T` free of `N`, and the error of `peak_formula`.
needs: hright : ∀ ρ ∈ FiniteOffLine.ZF T, (ρ : ℂ).re ≤ (ρ₀ : ℂ).re
decls.proves: ‖S N ρ₀ - K N ρ₀ 1 + ((riemannZeta.order (ρ₀ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℂ) * (Real.log N : ℂ)‖ ≤ ((riemannZeta.order (ρ₀ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) * Real.log 2 + ((riemannZeta.order (ρ₀ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) * ‖(ρ₀ : ℂ) - 1‖ / ‖(ρ₀ : ℂ)‖ + ∑ ρ ∈ (FiniteOffLine.ZF T).erase ρ₀, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) / ‖(ρ : ℂ)‖ * ((‖(ρ₀ : ℂ)‖ / ‖(ρ : ℂ) - ρ₀‖ + ‖(ρ₀ : ℂ) - 1‖ / ‖(ρ : ℂ) - ρ₀ + 1‖) * 2) + (‖(ρ₀ : ℂ)‖ + ‖(ρ₀ : ℂ) - 1‖) * (ExplicitTwo.c1t * N * Real.log ((N:ℝ) * T) ^ 2 / T + C1 (ρ₀ : ℂ).re)

header: StepsPole — block R4 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`. 2026-11-23. Unit 0472 turned the steps of the staircase and saw them line up at the heights of the zeros. The exact core: the sum of the turned steps is the logarithmic derivative of zeta, and it has a pole at every nontrivial zero, whose weight is the zero's order over the zero, the same weight the zero carries in the table's residual.

decls.name: steps_sum
decls.why: The turned steps. Right of the line `Re s = 1` the sum over the integers of the step `Λ(n)` turned and weighed by `n^(−s)` is minus the logarithmic derivative of zeta.
decls.proves: LSeries (fun n => (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ)) s = - deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s

decls.name: order_pos
decls.why: A nontrivial zero has order at least one.

decls.name: steps_pole
decls.why: The pole at a zero. At a nontrivial zero `ρ` of order `m`, the turned steps' sum over `s`, times the distance `s − ρ`, tends to `−m/ρ`.
decls.proves: Tendsto (fun s : ℂ => (s - (ρ : ℂ)) * (- deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s / s)) (𝓝[≠] (ρ : ℂ)) (𝓝 (-(analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta (ρ : ℂ) : ℂ) / (ρ : ℂ)))

decls.name: steps_pole_ne_zero
decls.why: The pole is there: its weight is not zero.

decls.name: steps_regular
decls.why: No pole away from the zeros. Where zeta does not vanish, and away from `1`, the logarithmic derivative of zeta is analytic.
decls.proves: AnalyticAt ℂ (fun t : ℂ => deriv riemannZeta t / riemannZeta t) s

header: StepsRate — block R8 of `lean_stage3/design/runs.md`. 2026-11-23. The second size of unit 0472: the size rate. Away from the zeros the turned steps to a cutoff `N`, less their smooth term, grow no faster than `N` to the power of the largest real part of a zero below the height less the real part of the point.

decls.name: norm_K_le_pow
decls.why: A zero's kernel grows at most as the cutoff to the gap of the real parts.

decls.name: rate_upper
decls.why: The size rate, from above. At a point `s` with `0 < Re s ≤ 1` that is not a zero, if every zero below the height `T` has real part at most `Θ` and `Re s ≤ Θ`, the turned steps to the cutoff `N` less their smooth term are at most a sum over the zeros below `T`, free of `N`, times `N^(Θ − Re s)`, plus the error of `peak_formula`.
needs: hΘ : ∀ ρ ∈ FiniteOffLine.ZF T, (ρ : ℂ).re ≤ Θ
hne : ∀ ρ ∈ FiniteOffLine.ZF T, (ρ : ℂ) ≠ s
decls.proves: ‖S N s - K N s 1‖ ≤ (∑ ρ ∈ FiniteOffLine.ZF T, ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) / ‖(ρ : ℂ)‖ * ((‖s‖ / ‖(ρ : ℂ) - s‖ + ‖s - 1‖ / ‖(ρ : ℂ) - s + 1‖) * 2)) * (N : ℝ) ^ (Θ - s.re) + (‖s‖ + ‖s - 1‖) * (ExplicitTwo.c1t * N * Real.log ((N:ℝ) * T) ^ 2 / T + C1 s.re)

header: Stirling — the phase construction: θ as the digamma integral. Entry 132 made the continuous phase part of the Stirling half's discharge. This module constructs it. The classical θ(T) is `Im log Γ(1/4 + iT/2) − (T/2)·log π` along the continuous branch, and the continuous branch IS the integral of the derivative:

decls.name: phasePoint
decls.why: The phase integrand: `Re ψ(1/4 + it/2)`, the derivative of the continuous `Im log Γ` along the quarter-line.

decls.name: phaseTheta
decls.why: The continuous phase, by construction: the integral of the derivative, anchored at `θ(0) = 0 = arg Γ(1/4)`.

decls.name: continuous_phasePoint
decls.why: The integrand is continuous: the quarter-line stays in `re > 0`, where the dependency's digamma continuity holds sorry-free.

decls.name: intervalIntegrable_phasePoint
decls.why: Hence integrable on every interval.

decls.name: phaseTheta_zero
decls.why: The anchor: `θ(0) = 0`.

decls.name: integral_log_half
decls.why: The main-term integral, by FTC (avoiding `t = 0` entirely): `∫₁ᵀ log(t/2) dt = T·log(T/2) − T + 1 + log 2`. The antiderivative is `t·log(t/2) − t`.
decls.proves: (∫ t in (1 : ℝ)..T, Real.log (t / 2)) = T * Real.log (T / 2) - T + 1 + Real.log 2

decls.name: StmtDigammaLog
decls.why: The last analytic fact of the Stirling half: the digamma comparison. Component one: `|Re ψ(1/4 + it/2) − log(t/2)| ≤ C/t` for `t ≥ 1` — the textbook `ψ(z) = log z + O(1/|z|)` on the quarter-line. Component two: `|Re ψ| ≤ C` on `[0, 1]` — boundedness on the compact piece. Both classical; the discharge route is the dependency's sorry-free `digamma_eq_tsum` series.

decls.name: backlundPhase_of_digammaLog
decls.why: The Stirling half, reduced to the digamma comparison: `StmtDigammaLog C` gives `StmtBacklundPhase phaseTheta C (C + 1)`. The proof splits the phase integral at `1`, bounds the compact piece by `C`, integrates the `C/t` band to `C·log T`, evaluates the main term by `integral_log_half`, and watches the `T`-terms cancel exactly against the RvM main term — the `7/8` mismatch and the integration constants land inside `C + 1`.

decls.name: digamma_term_norm_le
decls.why: Per-term bound for the digamma series on the quarter-line segment: `‖1/(n+1) − 1/(n+z)‖ ≤ 4/(n+1)²` whenever `re z = 1/4` and `‖z−1‖ ≤ 1`.

decls.name: phasePoint_compact_le
decls.why: Component two of `StmtDigammaLog`, discharged with an explicit constant: `|Re ψ(1/4 + it/2)| ≤ 8` on `[0, 1]`. From the sorry-free series: `|ψ| ≤ γ + Σ 4/(n+1)² = γ + 4·π²/6 < 8`.

decls.name: log_norm_z_le
decls.why: The norm-vs-`t/2` log ratio on the quarter-line: `|log‖z_t‖ − log(t/2)| ≤ 1/(4t)` for `t ≥ 1` — from `log(1 + 1/(4t²)) ≤ 1/(4t²)`.

decls.name: inv_quadratic_tsum_le
decls.why: The quadratic tail sum on the quarter-line: `Σ' 1/((n+1/4)² + (t/2)²) ≤ 12/t` for `t ≥ 1`. Head (`n < ⌊t⌋+1`) by the `(t/2)²` floor, tail by the dependency's sorry-free `tsum_one_div_natCast_add_add_one_sq_le`.

decls.name: re_sub_log_norm_le
decls.why: The per-term log-Taylor bound — the telescope's engine: for `w` in the open right half-plane with `‖w‖ ≤ 2`, `|Re w − log‖1 + w‖| ≤ 8‖w‖²`. Both sides come from `log y ≤ y − 1` alone (applied at `1+u` and at `(1+u)⁻¹`). The `≤ 2` radius admits the `n = 0` term of the telescope at every `t ≥ 1`.

decls.name: zq
decls.why: The quarter-line point, named: `zq t = 1/4 + it/2`.

decls.name: phasePoint_eq
decls.why: The phase integrand at `t` is the real part of the digamma function at the quarter-line point `zq t`.

decls.name: normSq_add_zq
decls.why: Norm-square along the shifted quarter-line: `‖n + zq t‖² = (n + 1/4)² + (t/2)²`.

decls.name: add_zq_ne_zero
decls.why: The shifted point is never zero (its real part is `n + 1/4`).

decls.name: a_term_le
decls.why: The per-term telescope bound: each digamma-series step tracks the log-norm step to within `8/((n+1/4)² + (t/2)²)` on `t ≥ 1`.

decls.name: re_digamma_sub_log_le
decls.why: The harmonic-γ limit assembly — component 1 of the digamma comparison: `|Re ψ(zq t) − log‖zq t‖| ≤ 96/t` for `t ≥ 1`. The digamma series telescopes against log-norm steps; the partial sums of the telescope converge to `log‖z‖ − Re ψ(z)` through Mathlib's `tendsto_eulerMascheroniSeq`, and every partial sum is bounded by `8 · Σ' 1/((n+1/4)² + (t/2)²) ≤ 96/t`.

decls.name: stmtDigammaLog_holds
decls.why: THE DIGAMMA COMPARISON, DISCHARGED: `StmtDigammaLog 97` holds. Component 1 composes the limit assembly (`96/t`) with the log ratio (`1/(4t) ≤ t/(4t) = 1/4·(1/t)`); component 2 is the compact bound `8 ≤ 97`. A named leaf falls.

decls.name: backlundPhase_holds
decls.why: THE STIRLING HALF OF BACKLUND, DISCHARGED: `StmtBacklundPhase phaseTheta 97 98` — the continuous phase tracks the Riemann–von Mangoldt main term with explicit crude constants, proved end to end from the digamma series. The hNT leaf ledger shrinks to `StmtArgCrude` alone.
