header: The Euler Factor Chain, as a chain. Companion to papers/Euler-Factor-Chain.md.

decls.name: Sym
decls.why: The reciprocal Euler factor at `b`.

decls.name: mode
decls.why: A mode on the ladder, indexed by `r`.

decls.name: bdiff
decls.why: Backward differencing in the ladder index.

decls.name: h
decls.why: The Weil test function of order `N`.

decls.name: StmtA1
decls.why: A1. One backward difference multiplies a mode by the symbol.

decls.name: StmtA2
decls.why: A2. Euler's product. It is a statement about *all* primes at once, so it carries no base index `b`, and it holds only where the product converges — hence the `1 < s.re` hypothesis, which is Euler's own content and not a technicality.

decls.name: StmtA3
decls.why: A3. The single-base reading, with the `b` index kept. Two conjuncts. The first says the chain's `Sym` at a prime base is the Euler product's factor at that prime. It is definitional — `Sym b s` unfolds to `1 - b^(-s)` and the only content is the `ℕ → ℝ → ℂ` cast — and it is stated rather than dressed up, because the paper's A3 ("therefore `1 − b^(−s)` is the reciprocal Euler factor at `b`") is precisely a renaming, not an inference.

decls.name: StmtA4
decls.why: A4. `N` differences multiply a mode by the `N`-th power of the symbol.

decls.name: StmtB4
decls.why: B4. On the critical line the Weil function is the symbol's modulus to the `2N`.

decls.name: StmtB5
decls.why: B5. The depth-`N` transfer gain and the Weil weight are one quantity.

decls.name: StmtC1
decls.why: C1. The squared modulus on the critical line, expanded.

decls.name: StmtC2
decls.why: C2. The gain is bounded by `1 ± b^(-1/2)`.

decls.name: StmtC3
decls.why: C3. No mode's depth-`N` gain escapes those bounds.

decls.name: StmtC3lower
decls.why: C3, the other half. The paper's C3 reads "no mode grows *or decays* without bound under depth". `StmtC3` is the growth half only. This is the decay half, and the ingredient was already present and unused: `StmtC2`'s FIRST conjunct bounds the gain below, `C2_of_C1` proves it, and `C3_of_A4_C2` calls only `.2`.

decls.name: bdiff_smul
decls.why: `bdiff` is homogeneous: scalars pass through.
decls.proves: bdiff (fun r => k * f r) = fun r => k * bdiff f r

decls.name: A4_of_A1
decls.why: A1 → A4. The arrow that turns one difference into `N`, by induction. This is the paper's A3–A4 step and it uses A1 essentially.

decls.name: B5_of_A4_B4
decls.why: A4 ∧ B4 → B5. The payoff arrow: the depth gain *is* the Weil weight. Lean needs only `hB4`. The proof rewrites by it, then moves the exponent inside the norm — `‖Sym‖^(2N) = ‖Sym^N‖^2`, which is `norm_pow` and nothing else. `hA4` is carried to mirror the paper's stated dependency, not because the proof consumes it: the `have` binding it is inert, and it is instantiated at `r = 1`, which appears nowhere in the goal.
needs: hA4 : StmtA4 b ((1 : ℂ)/2 + γ * I)

decls.name: C2_of_C1
decls.why: C1 → C2. The bound follows from the expansion and `|cos| ≤ 1`.

decls.name: C3_of_A4_C2
decls.why: A4 ∧ C2 → C3. Depth cannot escape the bound. Uses A4 to name the depth-`N` multiplier and C2 to bound it.
needs: hA4 : ∀ γ : ℝ, StmtA4 b ((1 : ℂ)/2 + γ * I)

decls.name: C3lower_of_A4_C2
decls.why: A4 ∧ C2 → C3 (decay half). A strict mirror of `C3_of_A4_C2`, reading `(hC2 γ).1` where that reads `.2`.
needs: hA4 : ∀ γ : ℝ, StmtA4 b ((1 : ℂ)/2 + γ * I)

decls.name: A2
decls.why: A2, proved rather than assumed, from `EulerFactorChain.euler_product_riemannZeta` (Mathlib's `riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod`). No base index, and the convergence hypothesis travels with it.

decls.name: A3
decls.why: A3, proved rather than assumed. The first conjunct is `EulerFactorChain.sym_natCast`, which is a cast lemma; the second is `EulerFactorChain.euler_product_sym`, i.e. A2 with `Sym` substituted in.

decls.name: C1
decls.why: C1, proved rather than assumed. The expansion is `EulerFactorChain.gain_sq_on_critical_line`, the law of cosines with sides `1` and `b^(-1/2)`. Needs only `0 < b`.

decls.name: C2
decls.why: C2, now unconditional. Same arrow as `C2_of_C1`, with its hypothesis supplied by `C1`; the implication is still the thing Lean checks.

decls.name: A1
decls.why: A1, proved rather than assumed, from `EulerFactorChain.symbol_of_backward_difference`. Needs only `b ≠ 0`.

decls.name: A4
decls.why: A4, now unconditional. Same arrow as `A4_of_A1`, with its hypothesis supplied by `A1`.

decls.name: B4
decls.why: B4, proved rather than assumed, from `EulerFactorChain.h_eq_gain_pow_on_critical_line`. Needs only `0 < b`.

decls.name: B5
decls.why: B5, now unconditional. Same arrow as `B5_of_A4_B4`, with both hypotheses supplied. The depth gain *is* the Weil weight, with nothing assumed.

decls.name: C3
decls.why: C3, now unconditional. Same arrow as `C3_of_A4_C2`, with `A4` and `C2` supplied. No mode's depth-`N` gain escapes the bound, with nothing assumed.

decls.name: C3lower
decls.why: C3's decay half, unconditional. Same arrow as `C3lower_of_A4_C2` with both hypotheses supplied. With `C3` this is the paper's C3 in full: a mode's depth-`N` amplitude is trapped between `|1 − b^(−1/2)|^N` and `(1 + b^(−1/2))^N` times its undifferenced amplitude, at every rung and every `γ`.

decls.name: tableFrom_eq_bdiff_iter
decls.why: The weld. `Construction.tableFrom` and `bdiff` are the same operation on two domains. If `g : ℂ → ℂ` agrees with the integer row `N` at every integer, the table's cell at `(r,d)` IS `bdiff` iterated `d` times on `g` at `r`.
needs: hag : ∀ n : ℤ, ((N n : ℤ) : ℂ) = g (n : ℂ)
decls.proves: ((Construction.tableFrom N r d : ℤ) : ℂ) = (bdiff^[d]) g (r : ℂ)

decls.name: tableFrom_mode
decls.why: The chain, welded. An integer row agreeing with a mode across the window a cell reads: the cell is the symbol to the `d`, times the mode.
needs: hag : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ d → ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℂ) = mode b ρ ((r : ℂ) - k)
decls.proves: ((Construction.tableFrom N r d : ℤ) : ℂ) = (Sym b ρ) ^ d * mode b ρ (r : ℂ)

decls.name: tableFrom_norm_on_critical_line
decls.why: The table on the critical line. The cell's modulus is `‖Sym‖^d` times the mode's — which is what `StmtC2` and `StmtC3` bound, and what the periodicity below makes an angle.
needs: hag : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ d → ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℂ) = mode b ((1 : ℂ)/2 + γ * I) ((r : ℂ) - k)
decls.proves: ‖((Construction.tableFrom N r d : ℤ) : ℂ)‖ = ‖Sym b ((1 : ℂ)/2 + γ * I)‖ ^ d * ‖mode b ((1 : ℂ)/2 + γ * I) (r : ℂ)‖

decls.name: sym_eq_zero_iff
decls.why: The pole lattice. `Sym b s = 0` exactly on `s ∈ (2πi / log b)·ℤ`.
decls.proves: Sym b s = 0 ↔ ∃ k : ℤ, s = (k : ℂ) * (2 * Real.pi * I / Real.log b)

decls.name: sym_periodic
decls.why: The symbol is periodic with the lattice period. One step along the pole lattice returns `Sym` to itself, because `b^(−2πi/log b) = exp(−2πi) = 1`. This is the origin of the circle.
decls.proves: Sym b (s + 2 * Real.pi * I / Real.log b) = Sym b s

decls.name: gain_sq_periodic
decls.why: The circle. The gain on the critical line is periodic in `γ` with period `2π / log b`.
decls.proves: Function.Periodic (fun γ : ℝ => ‖Sym b ((1 : ℂ)/2 + γ * I)‖ ^ 2) (2 * Real.pi / Real.log b)

decls.name: period_vacuous_at_one
decls.why: The trap `gain_sq_periodic`'s `b ≠ 1` closes: at `b = 1` the period is zero and the statement holds for any function whatsoever.

decls.name: sq_rpow_half
decls.why: Helper: for `b > 0`, the square of `b^(−1/2)` is `b^(−1)`.

decls.name: gain_sq_at_floor
decls.why: D1, floor half. Where `cos(γ log b) = 1` the gain is the floor of C2.

decls.name: gain_sq_at_ceiling
decls.why: D1, ceiling half. Where `cos(γ log b) = −1` the gain is the ceiling.

decls.name: C2_floor_attained
decls.why: D2. The smooth term has `γ = 0`, so it sits exactly ON the floor. This is why differencing dissipates it fastest of anything in the band.

decls.name: C2_ceiling_attained
decls.why: C2's upper bound is ATTAINED. `StmtC2` proves containment; this exhibits a `γ` that reaches the ceiling. Witness `γ = π / log b`.

decls.name: ceiling_base
decls.why: D4. The bases placing `γ` exactly at the ceiling are `exp(π(2k+1)/γ)`. For `γ₁` the paper lists `1.2489, 1.948, 3.039, 4.741, 7.395 …`; `1.2489` is the O45 locked family's `k = 2`.

decls.name: ceiling_dominates_floor
decls.why: D3. Differencing amplifies ceiling modes strictly more than floor modes. That is the power iteration, as an inequality — and it needs only `0 < b`, not `b ≠ 1`, because the proof does not consume one.

decls.name: joint_gain_periodic_of_commensurate
decls.why: The collapse. Each base contributes a circle of period `2π / log b`. If the two periods are commensurate — an integer multiple of one equals an integer multiple of the other — the joint gain is periodic in a SINGLE variable and the two circles are one.
needs: hcomm : (m : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi / Real.log b₁) = (n : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi / Real.log b₂)
decls.proves: Function.Periodic (fun γ : ℝ => ‖Sym b₁ ((1 : ℂ)/2 + γ * I)‖ ^ 2 * ‖Sym b₂ ((1 : ℂ)/2 + γ * I)‖ ^ 2) ((m : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi / Real.log b₁))

decls.name: second_ladder_winds_densely
decls.why: The torus. Take the `b₁`-ladder's circle. The `b₂`-ladder steps around it by its own period. Those steps are DENSE — the second ladder winds forever without closing — exactly when `log b₁ / log b₂` is irrational. Rational, and the orbit is finite and the two circles collapse, which is the theorem above.
decls.proves: DenseRange (fun k : ℤ => k • ((2 * Real.pi / Real.log b₂ : ℝ) : AddCircle (2 * Real.pi / Real.log b₁))) ↔ Irrational (Real.log b₁ / Real.log b₂)

header: Construction — the table has no free parameter, so the zeros were not placed. `Zeros.lean` records that nothing predicts WHERE the four exact zeros are. That is true and stays true. This file proves the complementary thing, which is what makes them structural rather than arbitrary:

decls.name: tableFrom
decls.why: The table built from a depth-0 row by repeated backward differencing.

decls.name: IsTableOf
decls.why: The defining recurrence, as a property a function may or may not have.

decls.name: tableFrom_isTableOf
decls.why: `tableFrom` satisfies its own recurrence.

decls.name: unique_of_isTableOf
decls.why: Uniqueness. Any function satisfying the recurrence with the same depth-0 row IS the table. There is no choice at any cell — fix the row and the entire table, to every depth, is determined.
decls.proves: ∀ r d, f r d = tableFrom N r d

decls.name: eq_of_same_row
decls.why: Two tables over the same row agree everywhere.
decls.proves: ∀ r d, f r d = g r d

decls.name: zero_determined_by_row
decls.why: A zero is determined by the row. If two counting functions agree on the window a cell reads, that cell is the same for both — in particular one vanishes exactly when the other does. Nothing outside the window can move it, and nothing inside the construction can either.
needs: h : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ d → N (r - k) = M (r - k)
decls.proves: tableFrom N r d = tableFrom M r d

decls.name: tableFrom_add
decls.why: Differencing is linear, at every depth. The operator carries no parameter to tune — this is what forces Pascal's weights rather than selecting them.
decls.proves: tableFrom (fun x => N x + M x) r d = tableFrom N r d + tableFrom M r d

decls.name: tableFrom_smul
decls.why: Scalars pass through the table: the table of `c·N` is `c` times the table of `N`. The other half of linearity, beside `tableFrom_add`.
decls.proves: tableFrom (fun x => c * N x) r d = c * tableFrom N r d

decls.name: measured_zeros
decls.why: The four exact zeros. Determined by pi through a parameter-free construction; located by nothing. `results/O16_run2.log`.

header: Euler Factor Chain — the algebraic core, formalised. Companion to papers/Euler-Factor-Chain.md (statements A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B4, C1).

decls.name: sym
decls.why: The reciprocal Euler factor at `b`, as a function of `s`.

decls.name: symbol_of_backward_difference
decls.why: A1. Backward differencing the mode `r ↦ b^(r*ρ)` on the ladder multiplies it by `1 - b^(-ρ)`. The symbol of `Δ` is the reciprocal Euler factor.

decls.name: diagonal_gain
decls.why: The diagonal gain. `b^ρ · sym b ρ = b^ρ − 1`.
decls.proves: (b : ℂ) ^ ρ * sym b ρ = (b : ℂ) ^ ρ - 1

decls.name: diagonal_cell
decls.why: The cell value along a diagonal in closed form: with `r = d + c`, the mode's `b^(rρ)·(sym b ρ)^d` collapses to `b^(cρ)·(b^ρ − 1)^d`.

decls.name: diagonal_over_column
decls.why: dia/col = `b^ρ`. The ratio of the diagonal gain to the column gain.
decls.proves: ((b : ℂ) ^ ρ - 1) / sym b ρ = (b : ℂ) ^ ρ

decls.name: diagonal_over_column_at_half
decls.why: At `ρ = 1/2` that ratio is `√b`. The critical line, read as the table's own geometry: moving along a diagonal outruns moving down a column by exactly `√b`, which at `b = 2` is 1.414214.

decls.name: symbol_at_one
decls.why: A1 at `ρ = 1`. Moved here from `PairIdentity` when that module went Mathlib-free; it is the only ℂ-valued statement that file had. A1 at `ρ = 1`. `symbol_of_backward_difference` says backward differencing the mode `b^(rρ)` multiplies it by `1 − b^(−ρ)`. At `ρ = 1` the multiplier is `1 − b⁻¹`. Stated here only to name the instance the rest of this file uses; it carries no content of its own.

decls.name: euler_product_riemannZeta
decls.why: A2. Euler's product, 1737, in the form Mathlib proves it: over *all* primes at once, and only in the half-plane where the product converges. The hypothesis `1 < s.re` is not decoration — it is the honest content of the statement, and it excludes the whole `sym b s = 0` lattice on which the old `(sym s)⁻¹ * sym s = 1` reading of A2 was false. Cited from `riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod`, not reproved.

decls.name: sym_natCast
decls.why: The chain's `sym` at a natural-number base, written the way the Euler product writes its factors. This is definitional: `sym` unfolds to `1 - b^(-s)` and the only work is the `ℕ → ℝ → ℂ` cast. It is stated as a lemma solely so that `euler_product_sym` below can be written in the chain's own vocabulary.

decls.name: euler_product_sym
decls.why: A3, the single-base reading with the `b` index retained. For a prime `p`, `sym ↑p` is exactly the factor A2 inverts: substituting the chain's symbol into Euler's product leaves the product unchanged and still equal to `ζ s`.
decls.proves: ∏' p : Nat.Primes, (sym ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) s)⁻¹ = riemannZeta s

decls.name: h
decls.why: The Weil test function built from an order-`N` stencil.

decls.name: h_functional_equation
decls.why: B2a. `h` is symmetric under `s ↦ 1 - s`: the functional equation.
decls.proves: h b N (1 - s) = h b N s

decls.name: h_zero
decls.why: B2b. `h` vanishes at `s = 0`: the stencil annihilates constants.

decls.name: h_one
decls.why: B2b. `h` vanishes at `s = 1`, so there is no pole contribution.

decls.name: conj_factor_on_critical_line
decls.why: On the critical line the second factor is the conjugate of the first.

decls.name: h_eq_gain_pow_on_critical_line
decls.why: B4. On the critical line, `h = ‖1 - b^(-s)‖^(2N)` — real, non-negative, and equal to the depth-transfer gain raised to the `2N`.

decls.name: cpow_rect_on_critical_line
decls.why: Rectangular form of the Euler factor's reciprocal on the critical line. Writing `θ = γ · log b`, `b^(-(1/2 + γi)) = b^(-1/2)·(cos θ - i sin θ)`.
decls.proves: (b : ℂ) ^ (-((1 : ℂ)/2 + γ * I)) = ((b ^ (-(1:ℝ)/2) * Real.cos (γ * Real.log b) : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((-(b ^ (-(1:ℝ)/2) * Real.sin (γ * Real.log b)) : ℝ) : ℂ) * I

decls.name: gain_sq_on_critical_line
decls.why: C1. On the critical line `s = 1/2 + γi`, the squared modulus of the reciprocal Euler factor expands as the law of cosines with sides `1` and `b^(-1/2)` and included angle `θ = γ · log b`:

header: Expansion — stage 2b: the derivative of 2^x/x, explicitly, and its floor. `MainTerm.lean` reduced O67's main-term hypothesis to `hD`: a floor on the `(d+1)`-th derivative of the li-interpolant on the window — equivalently, on the `d`-th derivative of `2^x/x`. This module supplies both halves:

decls.name: c
decls.why: The expansion coefficients: `C(d,j)·(log 2)^(d−j)·(−1)^j·j!`. `Nat.choose` vanishes past the diagonal, so no `ite` is needed.

decls.name: S
decls.why: The rational part of the `d`-th derivative of `2^x/x`.

decls.name: F
decls.why: The `d`-th derivative of `2^x/x`, in closed form.

decls.name: f2x
decls.why: The function itself, in the exp form the calculus uses.

decls.name: F_zero
decls.why: `F 0` is the function itself.

decls.name: c_rec
decls.why: The coefficient recurrence — Pascal with the factorial absorbed; the `j = 0` edge dies against the `−j` factor.
decls.proves: c (d + 1) j = Real.log 2 * c d j + (-(j : ℝ)) * c d (j - 1)

decls.name: hasDerivAt_S
decls.why: `S` differentiates term-by-term into the pre-recombination sum.
decls.proves: HasDerivAt (S d) (∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), c d j * (-(j : ℝ) - 1) * x ^ (-(j + 2 : ℤ))) x

decls.name: hasDerivAt_F
decls.why: The expansion advances: `F d` has derivative `F (d+1)` at `x ≠ 0`. Product rule, the coefficient recurrence, and one `sum_range_succ'` reindex.

decls.name: iteratedDeriv_f2x
decls.why: `iteratedDeriv d` of `2^x/x` IS `F d`, on `(0,∞)`. Induction; the step replaces `iteratedDeriv d f2x` by `F d` through `EventuallyEq.deriv_eq` on the open half-line, then advances by `hasDerivAt_F`.
decls.proves: ∀ x ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ), iteratedDeriv d f2x x = F d x

decls.name: t
decls.why: The unsigned term of `S`.

decls.name: t_nonneg
decls.why: Every unsigned term is nonnegative on `x > 0`.

decls.name: S_eq_alt
decls.why: `S` is the alternating sum of the unsigned terms.
decls.proves: S d x = ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ j * t d j x

decls.name: choose_factorial_step
decls.why: The choose-ratio identity, in ℕ where it is clean: `C(d,j+1)·(j+1)! = C(d,j)·j!·(d−j)`.

decls.name: t_halves
decls.why: The terms halve in the wedge `2d ≤ (log 2)·x`: `t (j+1) ≤ t j / 2`.
decls.proves: t d (j + 1) x ≤ t d j x / 2

decls.name: B
decls.why: The downward tail `B k = Σ_{j<d+1−k} (−1)^j t(k+j)`.

decls.name: B_peel
decls.why: Peeling the head of the tail: `B k = t k − B (k+1)` for `k ≤ d`.
decls.proves: B d x k = t d k x - B d x (k + 1)

decls.name: B_bounds
decls.why: The tail bound `0 ≤ B k ≤ t k`, by downward induction on the tail length, using only that the terms halve.
decls.proves: ∀ m k, k + m = d → 0 ≤ B d x k ∧ B d x k ≤ t d k x

decls.name: t_zero
decls.why: The leading term: `t 0 = (log 2)^d / x`.
decls.proves: t d 0 x = Real.log 2 ^ d * x⁻¹

decls.name: S_floor
decls.why: The floor on `S`: in the wedge, `S d x ≥ t₀/2 = (log 2)^d/(2x)`.
decls.proves: Real.log 2 ^ d / (2 * x) ≤ S d x

decls.name: F_floor
decls.why: The full floor on the closed form: `F d x ≥ (1/2)·2^x·(log 2)^d/x`.
decls.proves: (2 : ℝ) ^ x * (Real.log 2 ^ d / (2 * x)) ≤ F d x

decls.name: hD_of_window
decls.why: `hD` discharged. On the window `[r−(d+1), r]` with the window bottom positive and the wedge holding there, the `(d+1)`-th derivative of any smooth interpolant whose derivative is `2^x/x` on `(0,∞)` clears `Mlow`. The chain: `iteratedDeriv (d+1) G = iteratedDeriv d (2^x/x) = F d ≥ floor ≥ Mlow`.
needs: hG' : ∀ x ∈ Ioi ((1 : ℝ) / 2), HasDerivAt G (f2x x) x
decls.proves: ∀ y ∈ Icc ((r : ℝ) - (d + 1)) r, Nonvanishing.Mlow r d ≤ iteratedDeriv (d + 1) G y

decls.name: tableFrom_ne_zero_of_li
decls.why: O67's conditional theorem, with the analysis discharged. The hypotheses are now exactly: the interpolant and its derivative structure (what "li" means here), Schoenfeld on the window (stage 3), the row agreement, the gap arithmetic, and the wedge/positivity arithmetic. The MVT, the alternating series, the expansion of `2^x/x` — all under the kernel.
needs: hG' : ∀ x ∈ Ioi ((1 : ℝ) / 2), HasDerivAt G (f2x x) x
hrow : ∀ k ∈ range (d + 2), ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℝ) = Nonvanishing.bdiffZ f (r - k)
hS : Nonvanishing.StmtSchoenfeldWindow f (fun k : ℤ => G k) r (d + 1)
hgap : Nonvanishing.Ehigh r (d + 1) < Nonvanishing.Mlow r d

header: Interpolant — the smooth interpolant of the main term, constructed. Block C1 of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`. 2026-11-22.

decls.name: F
decls.why: The antiderivative of `2^x/x` through the value `2/log 2` at `x = 1`.

decls.name: liRow
decls.why: The interpolant: `F` cut off smoothly below one half.

decls.name: f2x_contDiffOn
decls.why: Helper: the integrand `f2x` (`2^x/x`) is smooth on the positive half-line.

decls.name: f2x_continuousOn
decls.why: Helper: the integrand `f2x` is continuous on the positive half-line.

decls.name: F_hasDerivAt
decls.why: For `x > 0`, the antiderivative `F` has derivative `f2x x` at `x`.

decls.name: F_contDiffOn
decls.why: The antiderivative `F` is smooth on the positive half-line.

decls.name: liRow_contDiff
decls.why: The interpolant `liRow` is smooth on the whole real line.

decls.name: liRow_eq
decls.why: For `x ≥ 1/2`, the interpolant equals the antiderivative: `liRow x = 2/log 2 + ∫ t in 1..x, f2x t`.
decls.proves: liRow x = 2 / Real.log 2 + ∫ t in (1 : ℝ)..x, Expansion.f2x t

decls.name: liRow_hasDerivAt
decls.why: For `x > 1/2`, the interpolant `liRow` has derivative `f2x x` at `x`.

decls.name: tableFrom_ne_zero_of_relErr_liRow
decls.why: The gate with nothing assumed about the main term.
needs: hrow : ∀ k ∈ Finset.range (d + 2), ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℝ) = Nonvanishing.bdiffZ f (r - k)
hS : RelativeGate.StmtRelErrWindow f (fun k : ℤ => liRow k) r (d + 1) ρ

header: MainTerm — stage 2: the difference calculus that discharges hM's structure. `Nonvanishing.lean` proved the arrow of O67's theorem with three named hypotheses. This module attacks `hM` — the main-term floor `Mlow ≤ |stencil of li|` — by formalising the calculus O67 verified numerically: the MVT step, replaced by something better.

decls.name: bdiffR
decls.why: Unit backward differencing on real functions of a real variable.

decls.name: iter_bdiffR_eq_fwdDiff
decls.why: The ℝ-domain twin of `Nonvanishing.iter_bdiffZ_eq_fwdDiff`.
decls.proves: (bdiffR^[n]) g x = (-1 : ℝ) ^ n * (fwdDiff (-1 : ℝ))^[n] g x

decls.name: iter_bdiffR_eq_sum
decls.why: `n` unit differences are the stencil, on the real line. At an integer point this meets `Nonvanishing.stencilR` (the bridge below).
decls.proves: (bdiffR^[n]) g x = ∑ k ∈ range (n + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * (n.choose k) * g (x - k)

decls.name: stencilR_eq_iter
decls.why: The bridge to `Nonvanishing.stencilR`. At an integer point, the real iterate reads the same values the ℤ-indexed stencil reads.
decls.proves: Nonvanishing.stencilR n (fun k : ℤ => G k) r = (bdiffR^[n]) G r

decls.name: deriv_bdiffR
decls.why: Δ commutes with d/dx. Needs differentiability of `g`; the shift is `HasDerivAt.comp` with `x ↦ x − 1`.

decls.name: contDiff_bdiffR
decls.why: Δ preserves smoothness.

decls.name: iteratedDeriv_bdiffR
decls.why: Δ commutes with iterated derivatives.
decls.proves: iteratedDeriv n (bdiffR g) = bdiffR (iteratedDeriv n g)

decls.name: bdiffR_lb
decls.why: The single step: derivative floor ⟹ difference floor. Shift by `m·y` and cite monotonicity-from-derivative on `[x−1, x]`.
needs: hm : ∀ y ∈ Icc (x - 1) x, m ≤ deriv g y

decls.name: iter_bdiffR_lb
decls.why: The induction: MVT retired. If the `n`-th derivative clears `m` on `[x−n, x]`, the `n`-fold difference does.
needs: hm : ∀ y ∈ Icc (x - n) x, m ≤ iteratedDeriv n g y

decls.name: stencilR_ge_of
decls.why: The floor, on the stencil. If the `(d+1)`-th derivative of the interpolant clears `c > 0` on the window, the stencil clears `c` — and hence its absolute value does, which is `hM`'s shape.
needs: hD : ∀ y ∈ Icc ((r : ℝ) - (d + 1)) r, c ≤ iteratedDeriv (d + 1) G y
decls.proves: c ≤ |Nonvanishing.stencilR (d + 1) (fun k : ℤ => G k) r|

decls.name: tableFrom_ne_zero_of_deriv
decls.why: The arrow, with hM discharged into a derivative bound. `Nonvanishing.tableFrom_ne_zero_of` again, but the main-term hypothesis is now about the `(d+1)`-th derivative of a smooth interpolant of li — the difference calculus between them is proved. What remains: the expansion of that derivative (stage 2b) and Schoenfeld (stage 3).
needs: hrow : ∀ k ∈ range (d + 2), ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℝ) = Nonvanishing.bdiffZ f (r - k)
hS : Nonvanishing.StmtSchoenfeldWindow f (fun k : ℤ => G k) r (d + 1)
hD : ∀ y ∈ Icc ((r : ℝ) - (d + 1)) r, Nonvanishing.Mlow r d ≤ iteratedDeriv (d + 1) G y
hgap : Nonvanishing.Ehigh r (d + 1) < Nonvanishing.Mlow r d

header: Nonvanishing — the arrow of O67's conditional theorem, in the house pattern. `papers/The-Four-Zeros.md` § I states: under RH, `cell(r,d) ≠ 0` for every `r ≥ R(d)`, which with O43's census makes the four zeros complete at every depth `d ≤ 15`. The proof has two analytic inputs and one arithmetic gap condition; everything joining them is algebra. Following `Chain.lean`'s design — take the antecedents as HYPOTHESES, prove the arrows, let the kernel check that the "therefore" is real — this module proves the joins:

decls.name: bdiffZ
decls.why: Backward differencing on ℤ-indexed real sequences — `Chain.bdiff`'s twin one level down (ℤ index, ℝ values).

decls.name: stencilR
decls.why: The real alternating binomial stencil of order `n` on `g`, read at `r` downward. The ℝ twin of `Zeros.stencil`.

decls.name: iter_bdiffZ_eq_fwdDiff
decls.why: Backward differencing is `(−1)·fwdDiff` at step `−1` — the ℝ copy of `Zeros.tableFrom_eq_fwdDiff`'s bridge.
decls.proves: (bdiffZ^[n]) g r = (-1 : ℝ) ^ n * (fwdDiff (-1 : ℤ))^[n] g r

decls.name: iter_bdiffZ_eq_stencilR
decls.why: `n` differences are the stencil. `Zeros.tableFrom_eq_stencil` transplanted to ℝ: Mathlib's `fwdDiff_iter_eq_sum_shift` does the binomial bookkeeping.
decls.proves: (bdiffZ^[n]) g r = stencilR n g r

decls.name: stencilR_row
decls.why: The Pascal step. The depth-`d` stencil on the row `x ↦ g(x) − g(x−1)` is the depth-`(d+1)` stencil on `g`. One more iterate, nothing else.
decls.proves: stencilR d (bdiffZ g) r = stencilR (d + 1) g r

decls.name: stencilR_sub
decls.why: Linearity. Splitting `π = li + (π − li)` under the stencil.
decls.proves: stencilR n (fun x => f x - L x) r = stencilR n f r - stencilR n L r

decls.name: Ehigh
decls.why: The error ceiling: `(log 2 · r / 8π) · 2^(r/2) · (1 + 2^(−1/2))^(n)`.

decls.name: StmtSchoenfeldWindow
decls.why: Schoenfeld on the window, as a statement: each of the `n+1` values the stencil reads obeys the RH bound at `x = 2^(r−k)`, where `√x = 2^((r−k)/2)` and `log x = (r−k)·log 2`. This is the hypothesis Schoenfeld's theorem would discharge; it is not discharged here.

decls.name: window_term_le
decls.why: Each windowed Schoenfeld bound is at most the top-of-window bound times `2^(−k/2)`: `(r−k) ≤ r` handles the linear factor and `rpow_add` splits the power. Needs `0 ≤ r − k` inside the window, supplied by `hr`.

decls.name: error_bound
decls.why: The error bound. Triangle inequality, the per-term comparison, and the binomial theorem `Σ C(n,k) t^k = (1+t)^n` at `t = 2^(−1/2)`.
needs: hS : StmtSchoenfeldWindow f L r n
decls.proves: |stencilR n (fun x => f x - L x) r| ≤ Ehigh r n

decls.name: Mlow
decls.why: The main-term floor `0.5 · 2^(r−d−1) · (log 2)^d / r`. O67's step 3.

decls.name: nonvanishing_of
decls.why: The arrow. If Schoenfeld holds on the window (`hS`), the smooth main term clears its floor (`hM` — stage 2's target), and the floor beats the error ceiling (`hgap` — O67's `r ≥ R(d)` table), then the depth-`(d+1)` stencil of the counting function does not vanish.
needs: hM : Mlow r d ≤ |stencilR (d + 1) L r|
hgap : Ehigh r (d + 1) < Mlow r d

decls.name: tableFrom_ne_zero_of
decls.why: Onto the integer table. If the integer row is the backward difference of a counting function `f` across the window a cell reads (cast to ℝ), then the cell's vanishing is the depth-`(d+1)` stencil of `f` vanishing — so the arrow above forbids it. The cast bridge is `Zeros.tableFrom_eq_stencil` plus `push_cast`.
needs: hrow : ∀ k ∈ range (d + 2), ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℝ) = bdiffZ f (r - k)
hM : Mlow r d ≤ |stencilR (d + 1) L r|
hgap : Ehigh r (d + 1) < Mlow r d

header: RelativeGate — the census gate, stated without assuming an error shape. WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `Nonvanishing.lean` states the census gate in the RH shape: `StmtSchoenfeldWindow` carries `√x·log x/(8π)` per value, and `Ehigh` accumulates it into `2^(r/2)·(1+2^(−1/2))^n`. Every downstream tolerance study (O68, entry 118) then swept the family `C·√x·(log x)^k` — every row RH-strength. Whether the gate NEEDS that shape was never asked, and the answer was assumed rather than derived.

decls.name: StmtRelErrWindow
decls.why: Relative error on the window. Each of the `n+1` values the stencil reads sits within `ρ` times its own scale `2^m`. No functional form is assumed — this is the weakest hypothesis the gate can consume.

decls.name: EhighRel
decls.why: The accumulated ceiling under a relative-error hypothesis: `ρ·2^r·(3/2)^n`. The per-value scale halves down the window, so the binomial sum contributes `Σ C(n,k) 2^(−k) = (3/2)^n` — the exact analogue of `Ehigh`'s `(1+2^(−1/2))^n`, with `2^(−1/2)` replaced by `2^(−1)`.

decls.name: relWindow_term_le
decls.why: Each windowed relative bound is the top-of-window scale times `2^(−k)`.

decls.name: relError_bound
decls.why: The error bound, shape-free. Triangle inequality, the per-term scale, and the binomial theorem at `t = 1/2`.
needs: hS : StmtRelErrWindow f L r n ρ
decls.proves: |stencilR n (fun x => f x - L x) r| ≤ EhighRel r n ρ

decls.name: relGate_iff
decls.why: THE GATE, REDUCED. The census condition against a relative-error ceiling is a bound on `ρ` alone — the scale `2^r` appears on both sides and cancels. What survives is
decls.proves: EhighRel r (d + 1) ρ < Mlow r d ↔ ρ < Real.log 2 ^ d / (2 * r * 3 ^ (d + 1))

decls.name: relGate_eps
decls.why: The threshold as a single constant divided by `log x`: with `log x = r·log 2`, the gate reads `ρ < ε_d / log x` where `ε_d = 0.5·(log 2/3)^(d+1)`. The constant falls by `3/log 2 ≈ 4.33` per unit of depth.

decls.name: nonvanishing_of_relErr
decls.why: The arrow, with no assumption on the error's shape.
needs: hS : StmtRelErrWindow f L r (d + 1) ρ
hM : Mlow r d ≤ |stencilR (d + 1) L r|
hgap : EhighRel r (d + 1) ρ < Mlow r d

decls.name: tableFrom_ne_zero_of_relErr
decls.why: Onto the integer table, shape-free. Mirrors `Nonvanishing.tableFrom_ne_zero_of` with the relative-error hypothesis in place of the Schoenfeld one.
needs: hrow : ∀ k ∈ range (d + 2), ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℝ) = bdiffZ f (r - k)
hS : StmtRelErrWindow f L r (d + 1) ρ
hM : Mlow r d ≤ |stencilR (d + 1) L r|
hgap : EhighRel r (d + 1) ρ < Mlow r d

decls.name: schoenfeldWindow_relErr
decls.why: The weld to the RH layer. `Nonvanishing.StmtSchoenfeldWindow` is an instance of the shape-free hypothesis. The relative error is worst at the window BOTTOM — `√x/x = 2^(−m/2)` grows as `m` falls — so the witness is `ρ = (log 2·r/(8π))·2^(−(r−n)/2)`, not the top-of-window value. Both factors are then bounded termwise: `r−k ≤ r` for the linear one, `k ≤ n` for the exponential one.
needs: hS : Nonvanishing.StmtSchoenfeldWindow f L r n
decls.proves: StmtRelErrWindow f L r n ((Real.log 2 * r / (8 * Real.pi)) * (2 : ℝ) ^ (-((r : ℝ) - n) / 2))

decls.name: powerSaving_relErr
decls.why: The power-saving instance. A bound `|f − L| ≤ A·x^θ` at `x = 2^m` gives relative error `A·2^(m(θ−1))`, worst at the window bottom when `θ ≤ 1`. So the witness is `ρ = A·2^((r−n)(θ−1))`, and the gate becomes a statement about the exponent `θ` alone.
decls.proves: StmtRelErrWindow f L r n (A * (2 : ℝ) ^ (((r : ℝ) - n) * (θ - 1)))

header: RelativeLi — the relative-error gate with its main term discharged. `RelativeGate.tableFrom_ne_zero_of_relErr` makes a cell nonzero from a relative error on a window of rows, a floor `hM` under the main term's stencil, and the gap. `Expansion.hD_of_window` with `MainTerm.stencilR_ge_of` proves that floor for a smooth interpolant `G` of `li` along the doublings (`G' = 2^x/x`). Nothing composed them: the Schoenfeld-shaped gate had its composition (`Expansion.tableFrom_ne_zero_of_li`), the shape-free gate did not. Thi…

decls.name: tableFrom_ne_zero_of_relErr_li
decls.why: The shape-free gate on the table, main term discharged.
needs: hG' : ∀ x ∈ Ioi ((1 : ℝ) / 2), HasDerivAt G (Expansion.f2x x) x
hrow : ∀ k ∈ range (d + 2), ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℝ) = Nonvanishing.bdiffZ f (r - k)
hS : RelativeGate.StmtRelErrWindow f (fun k : ℤ => G k) r (d + 1) ρ
hgap : RelativeGate.EhighRel r (d + 1) ρ < Nonvanishing.Mlow r d

decls.name: tableFrom_ne_zero_of_relErr_li'
decls.why: The same with the gap reduced to a bound on `ρ` alone.
needs: hG' : ∀ x ∈ Ioi ((1 : ℝ) / 2), HasDerivAt G (Expansion.f2x x) x
hrow : ∀ k ∈ range (d + 2), ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℝ) = Nonvanishing.bdiffZ f (r - k)
hS : RelativeGate.StmtRelErrWindow f (fun k : ℤ => G k) r (d + 1) ρ

decls.name: tableFrom_ne_zero_of_powerSaving
decls.why: From a power bound on the rows. `|f(m) − G(m)| ≤ A·(2^m)^θ` on the window with `θ ≤ 1`, and `A·2^((r−d−1)(θ−1))` under the gate's threshold.
needs: hG' : ∀ x ∈ Ioi ((1 : ℝ) / 2), HasDerivAt G (Expansion.f2x x) x
hrow : ∀ k ∈ range (d + 2), ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℝ) = Nonvanishing.bdiffZ f (r - k)

header: RouteCell — block E9 of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`, the table tree's half. The gate (`Interpolant.tableFrom_ne_zero_of_relErr_liRow`) at depth six, on the statement the other tree's explicit-formula route proves under RH.

decls.name: cell_ne_zero_of_route
decls.why: If `80 ≤ r`, the integer rows `N (r - k)` for `k ≤ 7` equal the backward differences of `f`, and `f` sits within relative error `ρ < (log 2)^6/(2·r·3^7)` of the main term on the window of `8` rows ending at `r`, then the table cell `tableFrom N r 6` at depth six is nonzero.
needs: hrow : ∀ k ∈ Finset.range (6 + 2), ((N (r - k) : ℤ) : ℝ) = Nonvanishing.bdiffZ f (r - k)
hroute : ∃ ρ : ℝ, RelativeGate.StmtRelErrWindow f (fun m : ℤ => 2 / Real.log 2 + ∫ t in (1 : ℝ)..(m : ℝ), Real.exp (Real.log 2 * t) / t) r (6 + 1) ρ ∧ ρ < Real.log 2 ^ 6 / (2 * r * 3 ^ (6 + 1))

header: Superposition — the missing licence for building the residual from the zeros. `Chain.A4_of_A1` gives the depth-N gain for a SINGLE mode. Every use of it on the bench applies it to a SUM over zeta zeros (O34, O35). Nothing so far permits that step. This file supplies it, and nothing else.

decls.name: modeSum
decls.why: A finite superposition of ladder modes.

decls.name: bdiff_sum
decls.why: `bdiff` distributes over a finite sum.
decls.proves: bdiff (fun r => ∑ i ∈ s, f i r) = fun r => ∑ i ∈ s, bdiff (f i) r

decls.name: A4_sum_of_A1
decls.why: The licence. If A1 holds for every mode in the family, then `N` differences act on the superposition by acting on each mode separately. This is what permits applying the depth gain to a sum over zeros.
needs: hA1 : ∀ i ∈ s, StmtA1 b (ρ i)
decls.proves: ∀ (N : ℕ) (r : ℂ), (bdiff^[N]) (modeSum b ρ c s) r = ∑ i ∈ s, c i * (Sym b (ρ i)) ^ N * mode b (ρ i) r

decls.name: depth_reweights_each_mode
decls.why: Corollary — the falsifiable form. Every mode is scaled by its own gain, so the depth-`N` superposition is the depth-0 one with each term reweighted by `(Sym b ρᵢ)^N`. The measured fractions in O34 test this model; they are not inputs to it.
needs: hA1 : ∀ i ∈ s, StmtA1 b (ρ i)
decls.proves: (bdiff^[N]) (modeSum b ρ c s) r = modeSum b ρ (fun i => c i * (Sym b (ρ i)) ^ N) s r

decls.name: tableFrom_eq_modeSum_reweighted
decls.why: The table is a superposition, reweighted by depth. An integer row agreeing at every integer with a finite superposition of ladder modes: its cell at `(r,d)` is that superposition with each mode carrying its own `(Sym b ρᵢ)^d`.
needs: hA1 : ∀ i ∈ s, StmtA1 b (ρ i)
hag : ∀ n : ℤ, ((N n : ℤ) : ℂ) = modeSum b ρ c s (n : ℂ)
decls.proves: ((Construction.tableFrom N r d : ℤ) : ℂ) = modeSum b ρ (fun i => c i * (Sym b (ρ i)) ^ d) s (r : ℂ)

header: Zeros — what is provable about the four exact zeros, and what is not. THE MEASUREMENT (results/O16_run2.log): over r <= 62, d <= 61 the dyadic prime difference table has exactly four exact zeros — (2,1), (4,1), (8,3), (20,6) — and no others. The centered table has none at all.

decls.name: IsTable
decls.why: The table recurrence: each cell is the difference of the two above it. Depth is carried in ℕ. An earlier version quantified `d` over ℤ, which is satisfiable but not by the bench's table: `Construction.tableFrom` has type `ℤ → ℕ → ℤ` and cannot be passed at all, and the obvious `toNat` adapter makes the recurrence at `d = -1` read `N r = N r - N (r-1)`, forcing `N (r-1) = 0` at every rung. So the theorem below was quantified over a class the object it is about is not in.

decls.name: tableFrom_isTable
decls.why: The bench's table is one. The hypothesis of `zero_iff_repeat` now has a witness: it is the second conjunct of `Construction.tableFrom_isTableOf`, which itself depends on no axioms.

decls.name: zero_iff_repeat
decls.why: A zero is exactly a repeat one depth up. This is definitional, and it is the only characterisation of a zero the chain supplies.
decls.proves: f r (d + 1) = 0 ↔ f r d = f (r - 1) d

decls.name: neg_below_zero
decls.why: A zero puts its left neighbour, negated, directly beneath it. With the cell above vanishing, the recurrence has nothing to subtract from.

decls.name: pair_shares_diagonal
decls.why: And those two cells share a diagonal. The left neighbour sits at `(r-1, d)` and the copy at `(r, d+1)`, and `r - d` is the same for both. So every zero places a `±v` pair as adjacent cells on the diagonal one in -- `±343` at `(20,6)`, `±5` at `(8,3)`, both measured in `The-Fold.md` § C3.

decls.name: window_shared_of_composite_exponent
decls.why: The (8,3) window is shared. Depth 3 spans `2^4 = 4^2`, so base 4 reaches it at depth 1. Against `Zeros.window_exclusive_of_prime_exponent`, which puts base 2 alone in the (20,6) window, the two deep zeros are different kinds of object.

decls.name: measured_zeros
decls.why: The four exact zeros, `(r, d)`, over `r <= 62`, `d <= 61`. `results/O16_run2.log`. Unexplained: no theorem above predicts these — their LOCATION is not derived, and nothing here changes that.

decls.name: pi2
decls.why: `π(2^n)` for `n = 0…20`, read from `pi2n_cache.json`. This is the only measured input to anything below — 21 integers, and no other data enters.

decls.name: dyadicRow
decls.why: The depth-0 row `N(r) = π(2^r) − π(2^(r−1))`: the primes in `(2^(r−1), 2^r]`.

decls.name: zero_2_1
decls.why: `(2,1)` vanishes: `1·1 − 1·1 = 0`, computed by the kernel from `pi2`.

decls.name: zero_8_3
decls.why: `(8,3)` vanishes: `23 − 3·13 + 3·7 − 5 = 0`, four values of `π`.

decls.name: zero_20_6
decls.why: `(20,6)` vanishes: the depth-6 stencil on seven values of `π`, spanning `2^13` to `2^20`. The deep zero, computed.

decls.name: measured_zeros_all_vanish
decls.why: The list's own claim, as a theorem. Every cell `measured_zeros` names vanishes on the dyadic row.
decls.proves: ∀ c ∈ measured_zeros, Construction.tableFrom dyadicRow (c.1 : ℤ) c.2 = 0

decls.name: nonzero_7_3
decls.why: A non-zero neighbour, so the check can fail.

decls.name: nonzero_19_6
decls.why: The `+343` of `papers/The-Fold.md` § C3, the partner of the `−343` that a zero at `(20,6)` forces onto `(20,7)`.

decls.name: measured_repeat_20_6
decls.why: The repeats that produce the two deep zeros. `results/joint_dyadic_triadic_table.csv`, rows 19/20 at d5 and rows 7/8 at d2.

decls.name: measured_centered_zero_count
decls.why: The centered (skew-adjoint) table has no exact zeros at all, `r <= 62`, `d <= 30`. `results/O16_run2.log`.

decls.name: four_zeros_only
decls.why: Four zeros in 1953 cells. Recorded, not derived.

decls.name: zero_at_20_6_of_repeat
decls.why: The measured repeat gives the deep zero, through the theorem. `O27` reads `d5` at `r = 19` and `r = 20` as both 623; `zero_iff_repeat` turns that into `(20,6) = 0` without computing anything. The measurement is the input and the vanishing is the output, which is the only direction this file supports.

decls.name: zero_at_8_3_of_repeat
decls.why: The same for the other deep zero, where the repeated value is 4.

header: ZerosStencil — the Mathlib-dependent half of `Zeros.lean`. Split out of `Zeros.lean` on 2026-08-26. The classification is by axiom pin, not by subject: these are exactly the fifteen theorems whose `#print axioms` carries `Classical.choice`, and every one of them acquires it from Mathlib — `Finset.range` and the alternating-sum lemmas for the stencil family, `Nat.factorization` and `Nat.dvd_prime_pow` for the four ladder results. Notes entries 59, 66 and 187 are the record; 66 predicted this exact list two weeks bef…

decls.name: tableFrom_eq_fwdDiff
decls.why: The table's `d`-fold backward difference is `(-1)^d` times Mathlib's `d`-fold forward difference at step `-1`. The bridge exists so that `tableFrom_eq_stencil` can borrow Mathlib's binomial theorem rather than redo the index bookkeeping.
decls.proves: Construction.tableFrom N r d = (-1 : ℤ) ^ d * (fwdDiff (-1 : ℤ))^[d] N r

decls.name: stencil
decls.why: The `N`-fold alternating binomial functional — the stencil that produces a cell at depth `N-1` from `N+1` values of the counting function.

decls.name: tableFrom_eq_stencil
decls.why: The operator IS Pascal. The cell at `(r,d)` — `d` backward differences of the row — equals the alternating binomial stencil of order `d` applied to the `d+1` row values in its window.
decls.proves: Construction.tableFrom N r d = stencil d (fun k => N (r - k))

decls.name: stencil_add
decls.why: The stencil is linear in the sampled values. So a zero is a single linear equation on the `N+1` values of `pi` inside its window — one condition, hence codimension one. Nothing here says when it is satisfied.
decls.proves: stencil N (fun k => g k + h k) = stencil N g + stencil N h

decls.name: stencil_smul
decls.why: And scalars pass through — linearity's other half, beside `stencil_add`.
decls.proves: stencil N (fun k => c * g k) = c * stencil N g

decls.name: stencil_annihilates_const
decls.why: The stencil's positive and negative arms carry equal total weight. For `N = 7` each arm sums to 64: the balance is exact by construction, not by anything about the primes.

decls.name: wingPlus
decls.why: The `+` wing: the even-index arm of the stencil, unsigned.

decls.name: wingMinus
decls.why: The `−` wing: the odd-index arm, unsigned.

decls.name: stencil_eq_wings
decls.why: The fold is an identity, not a test. `cell = wing⁺ − wing⁻`, always.
decls.proves: stencil N g = wingPlus N g - wingMinus N g

decls.name: stencil_eq_zero_iff_wings
decls.why: A zero is where the wings balance.
decls.proves: stencil N g = 0 ↔ wingPlus N g = wingMinus N g

decls.name: tableFrom_eq_zero_iff_wings
decls.why: The cell, folded. Through `tableFrom_eq_stencil`: the table's cell at `(r,d)` vanishes exactly when the two wings of its window balance.
decls.proves: Construction.tableFrom N r d = 0 ↔ wingPlus d (fun k => N (r - k)) = wingMinus d (fun k => N (r - k))

decls.name: repeat_iff_wings
decls.why: Two readings of one fact. `zero_iff_repeat` says a cell vanishes iff the row repeats at the depth below. This says it vanishes iff the wings balance. The repeat reading and the fold reading are the same statement, and until now nothing in the tree connected them.
decls.proves: Construction.tableFrom N r d = Construction.tableFrom N (r - 1) d ↔ wingPlus (d + 1) (fun k => N (r - k)) = wingMinus (d + 1) (fun k => N (r - k))

decls.name: stencil_weights_antisymm
decls.why: The stencil is antisymmetric when its order is odd. Reflecting an index about the midpoint negates its weight, because `(N-k) + k = N` is odd and so the two indices have opposite parity.

decls.name: stencil_arms_eq
decls.why: The two arms weigh the same. `stencil_annihilates_const` says the signed weights cancel; written as two sums, that is the positive-index arm equalling the negative-index arm. `(1 + (-1)^k)` is twice the indicator of even `k` and `(1 - (-1)^k)` twice the indicator of odd `k`, so this is the split with the division cleared.
decls.proves: (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), (1 + (-1 : ℤ) ^ k) * (N.choose k)) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), (1 - (-1 : ℤ) ^ k) * (N.choose k)

decls.name: stencil_arm_doubled
decls.why: And each arm is `2^(N-1)`. Doubled, an arm is the whole row, `2^N`. With `stencil_arms_eq` that fixes both at half the row -- 64 and 64 at `N = 7`, 8 and 8 at `N = 4`, which is what `The-Fold.md` § B1 reports.
decls.proves: (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), (1 + (-1 : ℤ) ^ k) * (N.choose k)) = 2 ^ N

decls.name: window_exclusive_of_prime_exponent
decls.why: The (20,6) window is base-2 exclusive. Depth 6 spans a ratio of `2^7`. Since 7 is prime, no integer base `b >= 2` reaches that window at any integer depth `k >= 2`. Base 2 at depth 6 is the only way to look through it.

decls.name: LaddersMeet
decls.why: Two ladders share a rung above `x = 1` exactly when some power of one is a power of the other. `Commensurate-Ladders.md` § A2 states the real-log form, `log b / log c` rational; this is the same condition in ℕ, which is where the rungs actually sit and which needs no transcendence.

decls.name: base_of_meets_two
decls.why: Only powers of two reach a dyadic window. If any positive power of `b` equals a power of 2, then `b` is itself a power of 2. So the ladders meeting base 2 are exactly `2, 4, 8, 16, …` and no others -- which is the general form of `window_exclusive_of_prime_exponent`, stated for every window rather than for `2^7`.

decls.name: factorization_proportional
decls.why: Two ladders that meet have proportional exponents. If some power of `b` equals some power of `c`, then at every prime the two exponents stand in the ratio `m : n`. This is the "shared lineage" of `Commensurate-Ladders.md` § A2 in exact form -- not that `b` and `c` are related somehow, but that their prime signatures are one vector scaled two ways.
decls.proves: n * b.factorization p = m * c.factorization p

decls.name: primeFactors_eq_of_meets
decls.why: And they are built from the same primes. Proportionality with both exponents nonzero forces the supports to agree, so ladders that meet are made of one prime set. Bases 2 and 3 meet nowhere above `x = 1` for exactly this reason -- there is no common ancestor because there is no common prime.

header: TableRoute — block E10 of `lean_stage3/design/joints.md`: the join between the two trees, closed for the explicit-formula route. 2026-11-22.

decls.name: rowN
decls.why: The table's row: the number of primes in the dyadic block `(2^(m−1), 2^m]`.

decls.name: cell_ne_zero_of_RH
decls.why: Under RH, depth six has no zero from row 80 on.

header: Target — the one open statement of the chain, fixed. 2026-11-24. Julian, 2026-11-24: the target is not to move. It is the window bound on `G` (`LandauWindow.WindowBound`, the ramp sum of the von Mangoldt function less its main terms) at every `θ` in `(1/2, 1)`: upper side only, on windows `[Y, Y^(1+δ)]` for arbitrarily large `Y`. Proved, it gives Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` by `LandauCriterion.rh_of_windows`.

decls.name: Target
decls.why: The target. For every `θ` in `(1/2, 1)` there are `δ > 0` and `C` with `G y ≤ C·y^θ` on windows `[Y, Y^(1+δ)]` for arbitrarily large `Y`.

decls.name: rh_of_target
decls.why: The target gives the Riemann hypothesis.

header: ThetaConverse — the Landau converse of the θ-dial. 2026-09-01. `ThetaPsi.psi_weak_of_theta` and `ThetaPi.schoenfeldWeakTheta_of_zeroFree` run one way: a zero-free half-plane `re s > θ` gives `|ψ − x| ≤ C·x^θ·log^k x`. This file runs the other way:

decls.name: regionθ
decls.why: The working region at abscissa `θ`: right of `θ`, minus the pole. `VonKoch.region` is the `θ = 1/2` case.

decls.name: regionθ_half
decls.why: At `θ = 1/2` the working region `regionθ` is `VonKoch.region`.

decls.name: isOpen_regionθ
decls.why: For every `θ`, the working region `regionθ θ` is open.

decls.name: preconnected_regionθ
decls.why: The region is connected, for every `θ`. For `θ < 1`: four convex pieces — upper half, lower half, the strip `θ < re < 1`, and `re > 1` — glued at `((θ+1)/2, ±1)` and `(2, 1)`; this is `VonKoch.preconnected_region` with the gluing point `3/4` replaced by `(θ+1)/2`. For `θ ≥ 1` the pole is already outside the half-plane and the region is the convex set `{re > θ}`.

decls.name: zeta_analyticOnNhd_regionθ
decls.why: For every `θ`, `ζ` is analytic on the working region `regionθ θ`.

decls.name: log_pow_isBigO_rpow
decls.why: `(log t)^k = O(t^δ)` at `∞` for every `δ > 0` and every `k`. The `k = 0` case is `1 ≤ t^δ`; for `k ≥ 1`, `log = o(t^(δ/k))` raised to the `k`.
decls.proves: (fun t : ℝ ↦ (Real.log t) ^ k) =O[Filter.atTop] (fun t : ℝ ↦ t ^ δ)

decls.name: F_differentiableAt_theta
decls.why: V1 at `θ`. `E = O(t^(θ+δ))` at `∞` for `δ := (re s − θ)/2 > 0`, and `Etr = 0` below `1`, so `mellin Etr` is differentiable at `−s`. This is `VonKoch.F_differentiableAt` with `t^θ·log^k t` for `√t·log³ t`; the hypothesis is consumed here and nowhere else.
needs: h : StmtPsiWeakTheta θ C k x₀

decls.name: F_analyticOnNhd_theta
decls.why: Given the bound `StmtPsiWeakTheta θ C k x₀` on the error of `ψ`, the function `VonKoch.F` is analytic on the working region `regionθ θ`.
needs: h : StmtPsiWeakTheta θ C k x₀

decls.name: anchor_mem_regionθ
decls.why: The anchor `max θ 1 + 1`: in the region, with `re > 1`, for every `θ`. `VonKoch` used `2`, which leaves the region once `θ ≥ 2`.
decls.proves: ((max θ 1 + 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) ∈ regionθ θ ∧ 1 < ((max θ 1 + 1 : ℝ) : ℂ).re

decls.name: F_mul_zeta_add_deriv_eqOn_zero_theta
decls.why: The load-bearing identity: `F·ζ + ζ′` vanishes on the whole region.
needs: h : StmtPsiWeakTheta θ C k x₀
decls.proves: Set.EqOn (fun s : ℂ ↦ VonKoch.F s * ζ s + deriv ζ s) 0 (regionθ θ)

decls.name: no_zero_right_of_theta
decls.why: V4 at `θ`. At a hypothetical zero `ρ` with `re ρ > θ`, factor `ζ = (z−ρ)^(k+1)·g` with `g ρ ≠ 0`. The identity `F·ζ + ζ′ = 0` factors as `(z−ρ)^k · [(k+1)·g + (z−ρ)·(F·g + g′)] = 0`; off `ρ` the power is nonzero, so the bracket vanishes on the punctured neighbourhood — yet it is continuous at `ρ` with value `(k+1)·g ρ ≠ 0`. Order `⊤` would make `ζ` vanish identically on the region, against `ζ ≠ 0` at the anchor. `VonKoch.no_zero_right_of_half`, with the region at `θ`.
needs: h : StmtPsiWeakTheta θ C k x₀

decls.name: zeroFreeRight_of_psiWeakTheta
decls.why: The Landau converse of the θ-dial. A ψ-bound at exponent `θ` — any `C`, any `k`, any floor `x₀` — forces `ζ ≠ 0` on `re s > θ`, `s ≠ 1`. No side hypothesis: `θ`, `C`, `x₀` are unconstrained, because the bound is only read through `‖·‖` above `max x₀ 1`, and the region is connected for every `θ`.
needs: h : StmtPsiWeakTheta θ C k x₀

decls.name: zeroFreeRight_iff_psiWeakTheta
decls.why: The abscissa of ψ's error is the supremum of the zeros' real parts. For `θ ∈ [1/2, 1)`: a zero-free half-plane at `θ` holds iff ψ has a `C·t^θ·log³ t` bound. Forward is `ThetaPsi.psi_weak_of_theta` (which is where `[1/2, 1)` is needed); the converse is this file, and holds for every `θ`.
decls.proves: StmtZeroFreeRight θ ↔ ∃ C > 0, ∃ x₀ : ℝ, StmtPsiWeakTheta θ C 3 x₀

decls.name: RH_of_psiWeakTheta_half
decls.why: The weld at `θ = 1/2`: `VonKoch.RH_of_psiWeak`'s statement through the dial, via `Abscissa`'s `StmtZeroFreeRight (1/2)` and V5's reflection.

decls.name: zeroFreeRight_one_of_chebyshev
decls.why: The primes are a subset of the numbers, so `ψ(x) ≤ c·x` (`Chebyshev.psi_le_const_mul_self`, `c = log 4 + 4`), so the count's fluctuation is at most `x`, so no zero has real part above `1`. The Euler-product wall as a corollary of the converse: this is the `θ = 1`, `k = 0` instance, with `C = log 4 + 5` and floor `1`; the hypothesis is genuinely opened at `θ = 1` since the region `{re > 1}` is convex.

header: ThetaLine — the vertical-line bound on `ζ'/ζ`, at a general abscissa `θ`. WHAT THIS PORTS. `RHPull.integrand_norm_le` (`LineBound.lean:1096`) draws its line bound from `Slice4b.logDerivZeta_line` (`:801`), which splits on `|t| ≤ 2`:

decls.name: logDerivZeta_compact_theta
decls.why: The compact patch at a general zero-free abscissa. `|t| ≤ 2`, `θ < σ₁ ≤ (1+θ)/2`: `‖ζ'/ζ (σ₁ + it)‖ ≤ 14530 + 2/(1−θ) + 212/(σ₁ − θ)`. `Slice4.logDerivZeta_compact` is the `θ = 1/2` instance (where the pole term is `4` and `14534 ≤ 14535`).

decls.name: logDerivZeta_sq_at_X_theta
decls.why: `logDerivZeta_sq_at_X` at general `θ`. On `σ₁ = θ + 1/log X` the denominator `σ₁ − θ` is `1/log X` for EVERY `θ`, so `11100` survives unchanged. `Slice3.logDerivZeta_sq_at_X` is the `θ = 1/2` instance.
decls.proves: ‖deriv ζ (((θ + 1/Real.log X : ℝ)) + I * (t : ℂ)) / ζ (((θ + 1/Real.log X : ℝ)) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ 11100 * (Real.log X) ^ 2

decls.name: logDerivZeta_line_theta
decls.why: The vertical line at abscissa `θ`, uniform in `|t| ≤ X`. On `σ₁ = θ + 1/log X` with `log X ≥ 2/(1−θ)` and `|t| ≤ X`: `‖ζ'/ζ‖ ≤ 11100 (log X)²`.
decls.proves: ‖deriv ζ (((θ + 1/Real.log X : ℝ)) + I * (t : ℂ)) / ζ (((θ + 1/Real.log X : ℝ)) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ 11100 * (Real.log X) ^ 2

decls.name: logDerivZeta_line_half
decls.why: The weld at `θ = 1/2`. Under RH the general line bound is `Slice4b.logDerivZeta_line`'s statement, with `2/(1 − 1/2) = 4`.
decls.proves: ‖deriv ζ (((1/2 + 1/Real.log X : ℝ)) + I * (t : ℂ)) / ζ (((1/2 + 1/Real.log X : ℝ)) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ 11100 * (Real.log X) ^ 2

header: ThetaPi — the ψ → π transfer at a general abscissa θ. `PsiToPi.schoenfeldWeak_of_psiWeak` is hardwired to exponent `1/2`: `StmtPsiWeak` carries a literal `Real.sqrt t`, and the envelope integral `integral_A_rpow_le` integrates `t^(−1/2)` to `2A·√x`. This file is the same proof with `x^θ` in place of `√x`, for `θ ∈ [1/2, 1)`:

decls.name: StmtPsiWeakTheta
decls.why: The ψ-side weak bound at exponent `θ`. `StmtPsiWeak` is the `θ = 1/2` member, `√t` written as `t^(1/2)`.

decls.name: StmtSchoenfeldWeakTheta
decls.why: The π-side weak bound at exponent `θ`.

decls.name: stmtPsiWeak_iff_theta_half
decls.why: The ψ-side weak bound `StmtPsiWeak C k x₀` is equivalent to `StmtPsiWeakTheta` at exponent `θ = 1/2` with the same `C`, `k`, `x₀`.
decls.proves: StmtPsiWeak C k x₀ ↔ StmtPsiWeakTheta (1/2) C k x₀

decls.name: stmtSchoenfeldWeak_iff_theta_half
decls.why: The π-side weak bound `StmtSchoenfeldWeak C k x₀ pi li` is equivalent to `StmtSchoenfeldWeakTheta` at exponent `θ = 1/2` with the same data.
decls.proves: StmtSchoenfeldWeak C k x₀ pi li ↔ StmtSchoenfeldWeakTheta (1/2) C k x₀ pi li

decls.name: sqrt_le_rpow_theta
decls.why: `√x ≤ x^θ` for `x ≥ 1`, `θ ≥ 1/2`. This is where `1/2 ≤ θ` enters the transfer: Mathlib's `|ψ − ϑ| ≤ 2√x·log x` folds under the `x^θ` envelope.

decls.name: integral_A_rpow_theta_le
decls.why: The envelope integral at `θ`: `∫ₐˣ A·t^(θ−1) dt ≤ 2A·x^θ`. The exact value is `A·(x^θ − a^θ)/θ`; `1/θ ≤ 2` keeps PsiToPi's constant.

decls.name: theta_err_of_psi_theta
decls.why: `ϑ`-error from `ψ`-error at `θ`, by Mathlib's `|ψ − ϑ| ≤ 2√x·log x` and `√x ≤ x^θ`.
decls.proves: |ϑ x - x| ≤ E + 2 * x ^ θ * Real.log x

decls.name: rpow_theta_sub_one_mul
decls.why: `t^(θ−1)` times the denominator is the `t^θ` envelope: `t^(θ−1)·(t·log²t) = t^θ·log²t` on `t > 0`.
decls.proves: t ^ (θ - 1) * (t * Real.log t ^ 2) = t ^ θ * Real.log t ^ 2

decls.name: schoenfeldWeakTheta_of_psiWeakTheta
decls.why: The transfer at `θ`. A ψ-side weak bound `(C, k, x₀)` at exponent `θ ≥ 1/2` with `k ≥ 2, x₀ ≥ 2` delivers the π-side weak bound at the same exponent with `C′ = 3C + 13`, exponent `k − 1`, floor `max(x₀², 9)`. The proof is `PsiToPi.schoenfeldWeak_of_psiWeak` with `x^θ` for `√x`.
needs: h : StmtPsiWeakTheta θ C k x₀
decls.proves: StmtSchoenfeldWeakTheta θ (3 * C + 13) (k - 1) (max (x₀ ^ 2) 9) (fun x => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ)) Li

decls.name: schoenfeldWeak_of_psiWeak_half
decls.why: `PsiToPi.schoenfeldWeak_of_psiWeak` recovered through the dial.

decls.name: schoenfeldWeakTheta_of_zeroFree
decls.why: From a zero-free half-plane to the π-side bound. `StmtZeroFreeRight θ` for `θ ∈ [1/2, 1)` gives `|π(⌊x⌋) − Li x| ≤ C·x^θ·(log x)²` beyond some `x₀`. Constant `3C_ψ + 13` with `C_ψ` from `psi_weak_of_theta`.
decls.proves: ∃ C > 0, ∃ x₀ : ℝ, StmtSchoenfeldWeakTheta θ C 2 x₀ (fun x => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ)) Li

decls.name: schoenfeldWeak_of_RH_half
decls.why: The same under RH at `θ = 1/2`: `|π − Li| ≤ C·√x·(log x)²`.
decls.proves: ∃ C > 0, ∃ x₀ : ℝ, StmtSchoenfeldWeak C 2 x₀ (fun x => (Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋₊ : ℝ)) Li

header: ThetaPsi — `|ψ(X) − X| ≤ C·X^θ·log³X` from a zero-free half-plane `re > θ`. WHAT THIS PORTS. The last stretch of `RHPull` (`LineBound.lean`):

decls.name: inv_log_le_theta
decls.why: If `θ < 1` and `2/(1 − θ) ≤ log X`, then `1/log X ≤ (1 − θ)/2`.

decls.name: σθ_lt_one
decls.why: If `θ < 1` and `2/(1 − θ) ≤ log X`, then the abscissa `σθ θ X = θ + 1/log X` is below `1`.

decls.name: lt_σθ
decls.why: If `0 < log X`, then `θ` is strictly below the abscissa `σθ θ X = θ + 1/log X`.

decls.name: horiz_length_theta
decls.why: The horizontal segment has length exactly `1 − θ`.
decls.proves: (1 + 1 / Real.log X) - σθ θ X = 1 - θ

decls.name: holo_logDerivZeta_theta
decls.why: The holomorphy hypothesis is free right of a zero-free abscissa.
decls.proves: HolomorphicOn (deriv riemannZeta / riemannZeta) (Set.Icc σ₁ 2 ×ℂ Set.Icc (-T) T \ {1})

decls.name: pull_at_theta_abscissa
decls.why: The pull, instantiated at abscissa `θ`. `RHPull.pull_at_RH_abscissa` with `σθ θ X` for `σRH X`.
needs: mass_one : ∫ x in Set.Ioi 0, SmoothingF x / x = 1
decls.proves: SmoothedChebyshev SmoothingF ε X = I₁ SmoothingF ε X T - I₂ SmoothingF ε T X (σθ θ X) + I₃₇ SmoothingF ε T X (σθ θ X) + I₈ SmoothingF ε T X (σθ θ X) + I₉ SmoothingF ε X T + mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 SmoothingF ε x : ℂ)) 1 * X

decls.name: integrand_norm_le_horiz_theta
decls.why: Pointwise bound on the upper horizontal segment, from the crude bound at `θ`. Every numeral is `RHPull.integrand_norm_le_horiz`'s.
needs: hMel : ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σ : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ M
decls.proves: ‖SmoothedChebyshevIntegrand ν ε X ((σ : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ (1996 * Real.log (84 * t) + (29 * Real.log t + 129) * Real.log X) * M * X ^ σ

decls.name: integrand_norm_le_horiz_neg_theta
decls.why: Pointwise bound on the lower horizontal segment, through the conjugate symmetry `Slice4b.logDerivZeta_norm_neg`.
needs: hMel : ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σ : ℂ) - (T : ℂ) * I)‖ ≤ M
decls.proves: ‖SmoothedChebyshevIntegrand ν ε X ((σ : ℂ) - (T : ℂ) * I)‖ ≤ (1996 * Real.log (84 * T) + (29 * Real.log T + 129) * Real.log X) * M * X ^ σ

decls.name: I8_norm_le_theta
decls.why: I₈ bounded at abscissa `θ` — the upper horizontal segment, length `1 − θ`.
needs: hMel : ∀ σ : ℝ, σθ θ X ≤ σ → σ ≤ 1 + 1 / Real.log X → ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σ : ℂ) + I * (T : ℂ))‖ ≤ M
decls.proves: ‖I₈ ν ε T X (σθ θ X)‖ ≤ (1 / (2 * Real.pi)) * (1 - θ) * ((1996 * Real.log (84 * T) + (29 * Real.log T + 129) * Real.log X) * M * X ^ (1 + 1 / Real.log X))

decls.name: I2_norm_le_theta
decls.why: I₂ bounded at abscissa `θ` — the lower horizontal segment, length `1 − θ`.
needs: hMel : ∀ σ : ℝ, σθ θ X ≤ σ → σ ≤ 1 + 1 / Real.log X → ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σ : ℂ) - (T : ℂ) * I)‖ ≤ M
decls.proves: ‖I₂ ν ε T X (σθ θ X)‖ ≤ (1 / (2 * Real.pi)) * (1 - θ) * ((1996 * Real.log (84 * T) + (29 * Real.log T + 129) * Real.log X) * M * X ^ (1 + 1 / Real.log X))

decls.name: mellin_vert_le_theta
decls.why: For `1/2 ≤ θ < 1`, a `C¹` bump `ν` supported in `[1/2, 2]` whose Mellin transform is bounded by `B` on `0 < Re w ≤ 2`, `0 < ε < 1` and `2/(1 − θ) ≤ log X`: the Mellin transform of the smoothed bump at the point `s = σθ θ X + i·t` of the line has norm at most `B·‖s‖⁻¹`.
needs: hB : ∀ w : ℂ, 0 < w.re → w.re ≤ 2 → ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (ν x : ℂ)) w‖ ≤ B
decls.proves: ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σθ θ X : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ B * ‖((σθ θ X : ℂ)) + I * (t : ℂ)‖⁻¹

decls.name: contour_at_instantiation_theta
decls.why: Every contour piece summed at abscissa `θ`. `RHPull.contour_at_instantiation` with `X^θ` for `√X` on the vertical piece and `1 − θ` for `1/2` on the horizontal lengths.
needs: mass_one : ∫ x in Set.Ioi 0, ν x / x = 1
hB1 : ‖I₁ ν ε X T‖ ≤ B₁
hB9 : ‖I₉ ν ε X T‖ ≤ B₉
hMel37 : ∀ t : ℝ, ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σθ θ X : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ B * ‖((σθ θ X : ℂ)) + I * (t : ℂ)‖⁻¹
hMel8 : ∀ σ : ℝ, σθ θ X ≤ σ → σ ≤ 1 + 1 / Real.log X → ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σ : ℂ) + I * (T : ℂ))‖ ≤ M₈
hMel2 : ∀ σ : ℝ, σθ θ X ≤ σ → σ ≤ 1 + 1 / Real.log X → ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σ : ℂ) - (T : ℂ) * I)‖ ≤ M₂
decls.proves: ‖SmoothedChebyshev ν ε X - mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) 1 * X‖ ≤ B₁ + B₉ + (66600 * Real.exp 1 * B / Real.pi) * X ^ θ * (Real.log X) ^ 3 + (1 / (2 * Real.pi)) * (1 - θ) * ((1996 * Real.log (84 * T) + (29 * Real.log T + 129) * Real.log X) * M₈ * X ^ (1 + 1 / Real.log X)) + (1 / (2 * Real.pi)) * (1 - θ) * ((1996 * Real.log (84 * T) + (29 * Real.log T + 129) * Real.log X) * M₂ * X ^ (1 + 1 / Real.log X))

decls.name: theta_instantiation_arithmetic
decls.why: The instantiation arithmetic at `θ`. With `ε = X^(θ−1)` and `T = X`, `ε·X = X^θ`, and every error piece lands under `c·X^θ·log³X`:
decls.proves: c * (X ^ (1 - θ))⁻¹ * X * Real.log X ≤ c * X ^ θ * (Real.log X) ^ 3 ∧ c * X * Real.log X / ((X ^ (1 - θ))⁻¹ * X) ≤ c * X ^ θ * (Real.log X) ^ 3 ∧ c * ((X ^ (1 - θ))⁻¹ * X) ≤ c * X ^ θ * (Real.log X) ^ 3

decls.name: psi_weak_of_theta
decls.why: `|ψ X − X| ≤ C·X^θ·log³X` from a zero-free half-plane `re > θ`. `RHPull.psi_weak_of_RH` with `StmtZeroFreeRight θ` for RH, `ε = X^(θ−1)` for `X^(−1/2)`, `T = X` as before. Every constant is obtained: `B` from `mellin_bump_bounded`, `Cclose` from `SmoothedChebyshevClose`, `C₁`/`C₉` from `I1Bound`/`I9Bound`, `Cmain` from `MellinOfSmooth1c`.
decls.proves: ∃ C > 0, ∃ x₀ : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, x₀ ≤ t → |ψ t - t| ≤ C * t ^ θ * (Real.log t) ^ 3

decls.name: psi_weak_of_RH_half
decls.why: `psi_weak_of_RH` recovered. At `θ = 1/2` under RH, the general bound is `RHPull.psi_weak_of_RH`'s statement, `√t` included.
decls.proves: ∃ C > 0, ∃ x₀ : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, x₀ ≤ t → |ψ t - t| ≤ C * Real.sqrt t * (Real.log t) ^ 3

decls.name: stmtPsiWeak_of_RH_half
decls.why: `StmtPsiWeak` at `k = 3` from RH, through the `θ`-dial. Same statement as `RHPull.stmtPsiWeak_of_RH`.
decls.proves: ∃ C > 0, ∃ x₀ : ℝ, Stage3.StmtPsiWeak C 3 x₀

header: ThetaPull — the vertical segment `I₃₇` at a general abscissa `θ`. WHAT THIS PORTS. `RHPull` (`LineBound.lean:1085` onward) bounds the vertical segment of the Perron contour at `σRH X = 1/2 + 1/log X`:

decls.name: half_lt_σθ
decls.why: If `1/2 ≤ θ` and `0 < log X`, then the abscissa `σθ θ X = θ + 1/log X` exceeds `1/2`.

decls.name: four_le_log_of_theta
decls.why: `4 ≤ log X` follows from the `θ`-hypothesis whenever `θ ≥ 1/2`.

decls.name: kernel_le_theta
decls.why: The Cauchy kernel on the line is dominated by `4/(1+t²)`, at any `θ ≥ 1/2`.

decls.name: norm_line_ge_theta
decls.why: If `1/2 ≤ θ` and `0 < log X`, then the point `σθ θ X + i·t` of the line has norm at least `(1 + |t|)/3`.

decls.name: integrand_norm_le_theta
decls.why: Pointwise bound on the pull integrand at abscissa `θ`.
needs: hMel : ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σθ θ X : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ M
decls.proves: ‖SmoothedChebyshevIntegrand ν ε X ((σθ θ X : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ 11100 * (Real.log X) ^ 2 * M * X ^ (σθ θ X)

decls.name: I37_norm_le_decay_theta
decls.why: I₃₇, T-free, at abscissa `θ`.
needs: hMel : ∀ t : ℝ, ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σθ θ X : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ C * (ε * ((σθ θ X) ^ 2 + t ^ 2))⁻¹
decls.proves: ‖I₃₇ ν ε T X (σθ θ X)‖ ≤ (1 / (2 * Real.pi)) * Real.pi * (11100 * (Real.log X) ^ 2 * (4 * C / ε) * X ^ (σθ θ X))

decls.name: I37_power_form_theta
decls.why: The vertical segment in `X^θ log²X` form. `RHPull.I37_sqrt_form` with `X^θ` where it had `√X`.
needs: hMel : ∀ t : ℝ, ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σθ θ X : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ C * (ε * ((σθ θ X) ^ 2 + t ^ 2))⁻¹
decls.proves: ‖I₃₇ ν ε T X (σθ θ X)‖ ≤ (22200 * Real.exp 1 * C / ε) * X ^ θ * (Real.log X) ^ 2

decls.name: I37_norm_le_epsfree_theta
decls.why: I₃₇ with the ε-free Mellin bound, at abscissa `θ`.
needs: hMel : ∀ t : ℝ, ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σθ θ X : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ B * ‖((σθ θ X : ℂ)) + I * (t : ℂ)‖⁻¹
decls.proves: ‖I₃₇ ν ε T X (σθ θ X)‖ ≤ (1 / (2 * Real.pi)) * (6 * Real.log (1 + T)) * (11100 * (Real.log X) ^ 2 * B * X ^ (σθ θ X))

decls.name: I37_power_log3_theta
decls.why: The vertical segment at `X^θ log³X`, ε-free. `RHPull.I37_sqrt_log3` with `X^θ` where it had `√X`. The `66600 = 6·11100` is untouched by `θ`.
needs: hMel : ∀ t : ℝ, ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((σθ θ X : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ B * ‖((σθ θ X : ℂ)) + I * (t : ℂ)‖⁻¹
decls.proves: ‖I₃₇ ν ε T X (σθ θ X)‖ ≤ (66600 * Real.exp 1 * B / Real.pi) * X ^ θ * (Real.log X) ^ 3

decls.name: I37_sqrt_log3_half
decls.why: `I37_sqrt_log3` recovered. Under RH, at `θ = 1/2`, the general bound is `RHPull.I37_sqrt_log3`'s statement — `σθ (1/2) X` is `σRH X` by `rfl`, and `X^(1/2) = √X`.
needs: hMel : ∀ t : ℝ, ‖mellin (fun x ↦ (Smooth1 ν ε x : ℂ)) ((RHPull.σRH X : ℂ) + I * (t : ℂ))‖ ≤ B * ‖((RHPull.σRH X : ℂ)) + I * (t : ℂ)‖⁻¹
decls.proves: ‖I₃₇ ν ε T X (RHPull.σRH X)‖ ≤ (66600 * Real.exp 1 * B / Real.pi) * Real.sqrt X * (Real.log X) ^ 3

header: # Von Koch converse — roadmap B1, COMPLETE (∃ C x₀, ∀ t ≥ x₀, |ψ t − t| ≤ C·√t·(log t)³) → RiemannHypothesis

decls.name: E
decls.why: The error function.

decls.name: F
decls.why: The completed right-hand object: `s/(s−1) + s·∫₁^∞ E(x)·x^(−s−1) dx`.

decls.name: Etr
decls.why: The truncated error, as a function on `(0,∞)`: `E` on `(1,∞)`, zero below.

decls.name: measurable_psi'
decls.why: Helper: the Chebyshev function `ψ` is measurable as a function of a real variable.

decls.name: Etr_measurable
decls.why: Helper: the truncated error `Etr` is measurable.

decls.name: E_le_linear
decls.why: Crude bound, no hypothesis: `|E t| ≤ (log 4 + 5)·t` for `t ≥ 0`.

decls.name: E_integral_eq_mellin
decls.why: The E-integral IS the Mellin transform of `Etr` at `-s` — as raw integrals, no convergence needed.
decls.proves: ∫ x in Set.Ioi (1:ℝ), (E x : ℂ) * (x : ℂ) ^ (-s - 1) = mellin Etr (-s)

decls.name: Etr_locallyIntegrable
decls.why: `Etr` is locally integrable on `(0,∞)`.

decls.name: F_differentiableAt
decls.why: V1 — F is differentiable on `re s > 1/2`, given the von Koch bound. The hypothesis is consumed here: `E = O(t^{1/2+δ})` at infinity makes the Mellin transform of `Etr` differentiable at `-s` whenever `re s > 1/2 + δ`.
needs: hbound : ∀ t : ℝ, x₀ ≤ t → |ψ t - t| ≤ C * Real.sqrt t * (Real.log t) ^ 3

decls.name: sum_Icc_vonMangoldt
decls.why: The partial sums of `Λ` over `Icc 1 n` are `ψ n`.
decls.proves: ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt k = ψ n

decls.name: psi_partial_bigO
decls.why: ψ is O(x) unconditionally, in big-O form on ℕ.
decls.proves: (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt k) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1:ℝ)

decls.name: measurable_psi
decls.why: The ψ-integrand is integrable on `Ioi 1` for `re s > 1`.

decls.name: integrable_psi_cpow
decls.why: For `Re s > 1`, the function `ψ t · t^(−(s+1))` is integrable on `(1, ∞)`.
decls.proves: IntegrableOn (fun t : ℝ ↦ ((ψ t : ℝ) : ℂ) * (t : ℂ) ^ (-(s + 1))) (Set.Ioi (1:ℝ))

decls.name: F_eq_neg_logDeriv
decls.why: V2 — the identity on `re s > 1`. The Mellin–Stieltjes representation is Mathlib's `LSeries_eq_mul_integral_of_nonneg` (partial sums `O(n^1)`, from unconditional Chebyshev); `LSeries_vonMangoldt_eq_deriv_riemannZeta_div` names the left side; `integral_Ioi_cpow_of_lt` evaluates the main term.
decls.proves: F s = -deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s

decls.name: region
decls.why: The working region: past the critical line, minus the pole.

decls.name: isOpen_region
decls.why: The working region `{s | 1/2 < Re s ∧ s ≠ 1}` is open.

decls.name: preconnected_region
decls.why: The working region `{s | 1/2 < Re s ∧ s ≠ 1}` is preconnected.

decls.name: zeta_analyticOnNhd
decls.why: The Riemann zeta function is analytic on the working region.

decls.name: F_analyticOnNhd
decls.why: If `|ψ t − t| ≤ C·√t·(log t)³` for all `t ≥ x₀`, then the completed object `F` is analytic on the working region.
needs: hbound : ∀ t : ℝ, x₀ ≤ t → |ψ t - t| ≤ C * Real.sqrt t * (Real.log t) ^ 3

decls.name: F_mul_zeta_add_deriv_eqOn_zero
decls.why: The load-bearing identity: `F·ζ + ζ′` vanishes on the whole region.
needs: hbound : ∀ t : ℝ, x₀ ≤ t → |ψ t - t| ≤ C * Real.sqrt t * (Real.log t) ^ 3
decls.proves: Set.EqOn (fun s : ℂ ↦ F s * riemannZeta s + deriv riemannZeta s) 0 region

decls.name: F_eq_neg_logDeriv_ext
decls.why: V3 — agreement extends to the punctured half-plane. From `F·ζ + ζ′ ≡ 0` on the region: divide by `ζ` where it does not vanish.
needs: hbound : ∀ t : ℝ, x₀ ≤ t → |ψ t - t| ≤ C * Real.sqrt t * (Real.log t) ^ 3
decls.proves: F s = -deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s

decls.name: no_zero_right_of_half
decls.why: V4 — no zeros right of the line. At a hypothetical zero `ρ`, factor `ζ = (z−ρ)^(k+1)·g` with `g ρ ≠ 0`. The identity `F·ζ + ζ′ = 0` factors as `(z−ρ)^k · [(k+1)·g + (z−ρ)·(F·g + g′)] = 0`; off `ρ` the power is nonzero, so the bracket vanishes on the punctured neighbourhood — yet it is continuous at `ρ` with value `(k+1)·g ρ ≠ 0`. (Order `⊤` would make `ζ` vanish identically on the region, against `ζ(2) ≠ 0`.)
needs: hbound : ∀ t : ℝ, x₀ ≤ t → |ψ t - t| ≤ C * Real.sqrt t * (Real.log t) ^ 3

decls.name: RH_of_no_zero_right_of_half
decls.why: V5 — reflection. No zeros right of the line forces every nontrivial zero onto it: a zero at `re < 1/2` inside the strip reflects through `riemannZeta_one_sub` to one at `re > 1/2`.
needs: h : ∀ ρ : ℂ, 1/2 < ρ.re → ρ ≠ 1 → riemannZeta ρ ≠ 0

decls.name: RH_of_psiWeak
decls.why: B1 — the converse, assembled from V1–V5.
needs: hbound : ∀ t : ℝ, x₀ ≤ t → |ψ t - t| ≤ C * Real.sqrt t * (Real.log t) ^ 3

decls.name: RH_iff_psiWeak
decls.why: B2 — the equivalence. RH holds iff `ψ` satisfies the von Koch bound at one extra logarithm (von Koch's own exponent is `k = 2`; `k = 3` is the coarsened route's price). Forward is `RHPull.stmtPsiWeak_of_RH`; the converse is B1.
decls.proves: RiemannHypothesis ↔ ∃ C > 0, ∃ x₀ : ℝ, Stage3.StmtPsiWeak C 3 x₀

header: WeilBackground — the window as a test function of the explicit formula, and the on-line terms of the zero side. Rung 4b, first half, of the detection ladder (units 0316–0319). 2026-09-06.

decls.name: phi
decls.why: The window as a test function of the explicit formula: cut off to `[−h, h]`, times `e^{−u/2}`. Real-valued.

decls.name: phiC
decls.why: The complex-valued test function WeilDetect reads.

decls.name: phiC_real
decls.why: The complex-valued test function `phiC h γ` has zero imaginary part at every `u`.

decls.name: laplace_phi
decls.why: The transform in the explicit formula's convention. `laplace φ z = ghat h γ (−z − 1/2)`.
decls.proves: laplace (phiC h γ) z = ghat h γ (-z - 1 / 2)

decls.name: Psi_bound
decls.why: `|Ψ(s)| ≤ (2π + π²)/s²` for `s ≠ 0`: the lobe bound at a purely imaginary argument, where `cosh(Re w) = 1` and `‖w‖ = |s|`.

decls.name: Psi_le_two
decls.why: `|Ψ(s)| ≤ 2`: the integrand is at most `1` in absolute value on an interval of length `2`.

decls.name: online_term_eq
decls.why: On the line the term is a squared modulus: for `Re ρ = 1/2`, `laplace φ(−ρ)·laplace φ(−(1−ρ)) = (h/2)²·[Ψ(h(γ_ρ + γ)) + Ψ(h(γ_ρ − γ))]²`.
decls.proves: laplace (phiC h γ) (-ρ) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - ρ)) = (((h / 2) ^ 2 * (WeilTransform.Psi (h * (ρ.im + γ)) + WeilTransform.Psi (h * (ρ.im - γ))) ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: online_term_le_near
decls.why: Near the carrier: the on-line term is at most `4h²` (from `|Ψ| ≤ 2`).
decls.proves: (laplace (phiC h γ) (-ρ) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - ρ))).re ≤ 4 * h ^ 2

decls.name: online_term_le_far
decls.why: Away from the carrier: for `|γ_ρ − γ| ≥ 1` and `γ_ρ + γ ≥ 1`, the on-line term is at most `(h/2)²·[C/(h(γ_ρ−γ))² + C/(h(γ_ρ+γ))²]²`, `C = 2π + π²`.
decls.proves: (laplace (phiC h γ) (-ρ) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - ρ))).re ≤ (h / 2) ^ 2 * ((2 * Real.pi + Real.pi ^ 2) / (h * (ρ.im - γ)) ^ 2 + (2 * Real.pi + Real.pi ^ 2) / (h * (ρ.im + γ)) ^ 2) ^ 2

header: WeilBands — the on-line zeros counted by band. Rung 4b, second half, slice A of the detection ladder (units 0316–0320). 2026-09-06.

decls.name: order_eq_analyticOrderNatAt
decls.why: Upstream's multiplicity is the analytic order, at every nontrivial zero.
decls.proves: ((riemannZeta.order (ρ : ℂ) : ℤ) : ℝ) = (analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta (ρ : ℂ) : ℝ)

decls.name: mem_zetaWindow_of_online
decls.why: An on-line zero within `9/10` of height `T` lies in the count's window.

decls.name: band_count
decls.why: Band count. A finite set of on-line zeros within `9/10` of a height `T ≥ 2` has total analytic multiplicity at most `15·log T + 73`.
needs: hS : ∀ ρ ∈ S, riemannZeta ρ = 0 ∧ ρ.re = 1 / 2 ∧ |ρ.im - T| ≤ 9 / 10
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, (analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta ρ : ℝ) ≤ 15 * Real.log T + 73

decls.name: weightedTerm
decls.why: The on-line term with its multiplicity, as WeilDetect's sum weights it.

decls.name: band_sum_le
decls.why: Band sum. Over a finite set of on-line zeros within `9/10` of `T ≥ 2`, if every term is at most `M ≥ 0`, the weighted sum is at most `M·(15·log T + 73)`.
needs: hM : ∀ ρ ∈ S, (laplace (phiC h γ) (-(ρ : ℂ)) * laplace (phiC h γ) (-(1 - (ρ : ℂ)))).re ≤ M
decls.proves: ∑ ρ ∈ S, weightedTerm h γ ρ ≤ M * (15 * Real.log T + 73)

header: WeilBridgeLeaf — the zero-set lemma and the bridge leaf: `zeroForm` gets a prime side. Block 1 of `lean_stage3/design/bridge.md`. 2026-11-22.

header: WeilDetect — the zero side of Weil's form on bounded support, and the bounded-height detection statement. 2026-09-06, the first attempt at entry 297's rung-to-strip arrow, in the shape entry 303 §(d) drafted and did not add.

header: WeilLobe — the 2γ lobe bounded above. Rung 4a of the detection ladder (units 0316–0318). 2026-09-06.

decls.name: P_eq

header: WeilOddPower — the odd envelope `sin(πx)·P(x)^m` and its transform in closed form; the switched window and its transform. Rung 5, third slice. 2026-09-06.

decls.name: q_odd

decls.name: continuous_q

decls.why: The odd envelope is an exact derivative: `q m = −(2/((m+1)π))·f1 (2m+1)`, where `f1 (2m+1)` is the derivative of `c^{2m+2}`.

decls.name: S
decls.why: The odd envelope's transform, `∫₋₁¹ q m x · e^{wx} dx`.

decls.name: S_mul_QS

header: WeilOffLine — every term of the zero form is minus a square, and the sign of an off-line zero's own term. Rung 5, first slice of the detection ladder (units 0316–0325). 2026-09-06.
